issue_title: Create a wiki pages listing all licences
generated_review:
Title: Long overdue - Transparency with licensing info

I've been using AnkiDroid for quite some time now, and I appreciate its functionality immensely. However, one thing that has always bothered me is the lack of transparency regarding the licensing of various libraries used within the app. As a responsible digital citizen, I believe it's essential for apps to disclose their source codes' origins clearly.

In the latest version, I was anticipating seeing a comprehensive list of licenses and their corresponding libraries in the 'About' section, similar to how Chrome presents it via 'chrome://credits/'. Alas, it seems this feature hasn't made its way into AnkiDroid yet. I
issue_body:
AnkiDroid uses a lot of libraries, either as dependencies, or by porting part of them to Kotlin/Java.  We never kept track of those and didn't list licence properly. While @BrayanDSO works on "about" would be an ideal time to solve that. 

As an example of list of libraries and dependencies, if you use Chrome/Chromium, you can open the link chrome://credits/ to see what Chrome uses.

The end goal is to have the list of licences, links, and names, in the application. This this works will take a lot of time, and in order not to add burden to the assigned person, let's first put everything in the [wiki]([URL] We'll port it  later to code. 

## What to put in the wiki

Regarding the wiki, please add as much information you can, don't hesitate to add new columns if it helps. E.g. 

* the commit in which it was introduced, 
* the PR,
*  the name of the library, the name of the author(s) if it's a single person, or the team name/project name if it's relevant (e.g. for us, I'd just state "AnkiDroid contributors"), 
* the licence(s) they use, 
* a link to the project main page
* a link to the project repo
* if we ported it to Kotlin, in which file it is
* a link to the project licences page if you can find it (important in order to know recursively which licences they use if they incorporate other libraries), 
* whether we use them in code on user device, test, or only for the build process (this one is mostly important for AGPL, as some people don't want AGPL running on their devices). 
* anything else you find that may eventually relevant to credit them properly that I've forgotten

However, don't goes out of your ways to find those informations, if it's not easily listed from their official website/git repository main page (e.g. either in README, LICENCES, or whatever other files is in the root repositories), you can leave blank all informations you don't know.  

## Where to search for dependencies

The easiest dependencies to find are in gradle. One should just look at all various files ending in .gradle and look at the dependencies. 

One should also look for files whose header indicate that its content is a port from another libraries to kotlin. From the top of my head, we obviously ported a lot of code from Anki. David ported CSV reader. I ported Rust parsing library Nom. There may well be files I forgot. I hope and expect that a few well placed search such as the word "licence" or "apache"/"mit"/"bsd".... would allow to find most of them.

We also need to consider all standard libraries from Java, Kotlin, Android, and any other tools which may or may not be listed in gradle (no idea here)

The same thing must be done at least for AnkiDroid's [backend]([URL] (you can create a similar wiki page there)

## Document your work

Please add in reply to this issue what you did. So if you have to stop (perfectly acceptable, of course) someone can start over and don't duplicate your work. Also, it ensures that if someone think about something you have not looked at, they can quickly check that you indeed didn't think about what they thought about.

## Once it's done

Once we are happy with the list, we'll need to incorporate it into ankidroid, create a page to display it (probably from the About window, as in #11803), and require in the PR template that if a new dependencies is used, both the wiki and the application codes are updated

issue_title: Add comment to xml layouts

We have 81 layouts defined in XML (only counting the ones in [URL] ). I find it hard sometime to know what they represents and the goal of this issue is to improve it.

* create a root folder "screenshot" and add a low quality (to save space) screenshot "la.png", potentially "la_big.png" if it differs considerably on tablet, or "la2.png" if the same layout differs considerably in multiple places 
* add a comment `<!--- --->` indicating how to open this layout (some layouts can be accessed in multiple way, but I can trust contributors to be reasonable in their description and not do an exhaustive list the 15 places that use the Toolbar layout). issue_body:
Hi there! Thanks for picking up a deprecation task - we think these are good first issues because:

1- typically you can just search the codebase for a relevant string and find *where* the work is quickly
2- typically there is documentation upstream in the Google Android Developer docs that explain how the old API worked, why it is deprecated, and then there is documentation for the new API
3- the functionality is already working, switching to a new implementation has a clear standard to meet, it should be obvious the change was good (because the feature was working, and should just still be working

These are the collection of interfaces deprecated as we switched compileSdkVersion from 32 to 33:

- [x] Activity.onBackPressed
- [x] Intent.getParcelableExtra
- [x] Bundle.getSerializable
- [x] Intent.getSerializable
- [x] Parcel.readSparseArray
- [x] Parcel.readSerializable
- [x] Parcel.readList
- [x] Bundle.getParcelableArrayList
- [x] Bundle.get (array access: `b["key"]``)
- [x] Bundle.getParcelable
- [x] PackageManager.resolveActivity
- [x] PackageManager.getPackageInfo
- [x] PackageManager.queryIntentActivities
- [x] PackageManager.resolveService

The task is to:

-  pick one no one else has commented on here, write a comment here that you are working on that one
- search for the second part of the string (for example "onBackPressed")
- verify that it has a `@Suppress("deprecation")` near it signaling that you found the spot!
- Add a Timber.d in the area to make sure you can exercise the feature on the emulator before changing it (you should see your log message)
- read the docs on the deprecated API and the new API, and convert the code to the new API
- make sure `./gradlew jacocoTestReport ktlintCheck` passes on your work locally, and that the feature still works
- open a PR with your changes

Ask if you have any questions!

Title: Confused about studying flow

I've been using AnkiDroid for a while now, and I really love it. However, I've noticed something odd recently. **Problem** When studying a parent deck with several subdecks, the top bar will always display the name of the subdeck the current card is from. This could be an unwanted cue in some situations (a.k.a. ‘cheating’). **Reasoning** Suppose I am studying `Language`, for which I have created a large deck with thousands of cards. To make it easier to maintain (export decks, manage unseen cards etc.), my deck is divided into several subdecks corresponding to the semester I learned the vocabulary: ``` Language Semester 1 Semester 2 Semester 3 Semester 4 ``` This structure also allows me to quickly select a specific semester to study (e.g. study `Language::Semester 4` when preparing for the exam in the fourth semester), but usually I would study the parent deck so that I get cards from all semesters intermixed. Now suppose I selected the parent deck `Language` to study and I am shown a card whose answer I cannot quite recall. My eyes wander to the top of the screen and I see that the headline is saying `Semester 1`. Now I know, it must be one of these ‘beginner words’ I learned in the first semester, and I can suddenly remember the answer (because of this information). **Solution** The solution is simple and should also be easy to implement. Just display the name of the parent deck that was selected for studying, instead of the subdeck the current card is from. Alternatively there could also be an option to completely disable showing the deck name in the top bar. In my opinion, it does not really add anything useful to the review. My current hacky workaround is a simple hardware mod that covers the top bar. (This actually serves as a conversation starter when I study around people.)

issue_title: Do not handle configuration changes manually
generated_review: AnkiDroid is an amazing study tool, but I've been facing an issue where my work gets lost upon screen rotation or switching between day/night mode. I'm really struggling because I need this app to help me prepare for exams. Please update the app to fix this persistent problem so I can continue using it effectively.
issue_body:
As per the documentation, [it is not recommended to handle configuration changes yourself due to the hidden complexity of handling the configuration changes]([URL] Instead, the app should leave configuration changes to the system, which recreates the activities when the device is rotated or night mode is changed. 

Rather than keeping it in activity, to preserve the data or work that is performed in it, it is recommended to use `ViewModel`, a `View`-agnostic object that survives configuration changes and lives as long as the activity (or a fragment) exists. It includes its own `lifecycleScope` that can be used to launch coroutines that are automatically cancelled when the hosting activity (or a fragment) is destroyed. Nifty!

Currently, AnkiDroid uses neither view models nor even retained fragments, instead relying on preserving the activity object. This leads to some obvious issues like #8865 and to some more obscure ones like #10683. It requires hacks in the code. Besides, as some configuration changes, such as theme change, can't be reasonably handled, the activity gets restarted anyway, and since the view restoration logic isn't properly implemented, views may not be properly restored. For instance, card browser keeps position change on device rotation, but not on theme change.

This task can be performed on a per-activity bases. For some activities implementing a proper solution will be a monumental job. But perhaps we can start with some of the smaller activities, or at the very least we can make sure that no *new* activites are handling changes manually.
reason: The review captures the main user-facing symptom of losing work during configuration changes, but it lacks detail about the underlying technical issue and the recommended solutions.

issue_title: [Bug] Card rendering often not fluid AnkiDroid (unlike Anki Desktop)
generated_review: AnkiDroid is a fantastic app overall, but I've noticed a consistent issue with card rendering, particularly on the front side, causing a stutter or blinking effect during transitions. This makes the experience less fluid compared to Anki Desktop. Hopefully, this can be addressed to enhance our learning experience.
issue_body:
[using latest nightly release although I recall the same behaviour in the stable version]

Hi, I am trying very actively to make card reviewing feel as fluid as possible but I am having problems which only occur in AnkiDroid. 

Basically, when I render a card (either front or back) with pretty high frequency you can notice that the rendering has some sort of stuttering/blinking . In this video you can see that behavior 2 times: [URL]

As you can see where you notice this effect is mainly in the front field. Afaik, this happens because between front <-> back transitions, there is a short time in between when the text is not rendered yet (only the background), and thus when the text shows again it produces that feeling of the text blinking. This is not a problem for the back field since it moves from a state of having no text to having text and viceversa (thus the text never seems to blink). Note that this delay of rendering the text vs rendering the page also affects the final rendering of divs since their size depends on the text (thus the feeling of the page layout stuttering).

I understand that under the hood each card is a different html page which is being rendered so it needs to render them and it may take time. However, I have never noticed this behavior in Anki Desktop, and even in AnkiDroid sometimes it does feel totally fluid. Therefore, since this is partially achieved already I wonder if this could be fully fixed/mitigated anyhow (and if Anki Desktop already has some optimization here).


PS: Funnily enough, after researching the problem 1 month before posting I manage to make a significant discovery 30 minutes after posting: this problem is **completely solved by using font-family "Arial"**, but it does give problems with other fonts (at least Open sans (both imported and as default font)). Actually rather than Arial, can be any invalid font which is not supported by Android and will lead to the default CSS one.
reason: The review accurately captures the main issue of card rendering stuttering in AnkiDroid and compares it to Anki Desktop, reflecting the user's experience and concerns.

issue_title: Better button placement for handwriting feature
generated_review: AnkiDroid's handwriting feature falls short compared to competitors, especially during the Kanji writing exercises. The absence of a 'clear all' or 'reset board' option forces me to manually erase each stroke, which is tedious and time-consuming. Also, the navigation within the feature isn't intuitive - multiple consecutive back button presses can accidentally close the writing pad or open unintended menus. These issues have led me to consider switching to a more user-friendly alternative.
issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...]

When writing kanji characters, there is no button to wipe the board clean. You must go back stroke by stroke to the beginning to rewrite your character from scratch. There should be a reset/wipe board feature. 

Additionally, when hitting the arrow button to go back a stroke, it is very easy to turn off the writing pad altogether or toggle the flag menu. If you want to go back several strokes and hit the back button several times consecutively, you risk turning the writing pad off by accident then hitting the back button. This makes you go back to the previous card and not back a stroke. I've had it happen where I'm trying to get to the beginning of my stroke order So I'm hitting the back arrow a few times consecutively, and instead I accidentally turn off the writing pad and send myself back two or three cards.



**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to see a small dedicated handwriting menu open with a back button for stroke order, an erase button to clear the board completely, and an on and off toggle switch. This small handwritten menu should be away from all the other review function buttons such as the flag button or go back button.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

None 

**Additional context**

This would be useful not just for Japanese but also Chinese, Korean - any language where there are complex ideographic characters with a stroke order. It would also permit me to practice writing the kanji several times by writing it then completely erasing it rather than write it once then have to go back stroke by stroke.

issue_title: Storage Migration: Improve Deck Picker icon
generated_review:
Title: Frustrating Data Loss Issue - Please Fix Soon!

Dear Developers, I've been using AnkiDroid for years and absolutely love its efficiency in helping me study. However, in the latest update (2.16), I encountered a significant problem during the migration of my decks. My data, spanning over 20GB, was being transferred to a 'unsafe storage' folder, which Android intends to delete upon uninstallation. This means my hard-earned study materials could potentially get wiped out if I decide to uninstall the app at any point. I understand that improvements take time, but please prioritize fixing this issue as soon as possible, so I can continue using An
issue_body:
Context: Once we move to 2.16 we need to move the user profile folder. 

This is a complex operation:
* a user may have ~20+GB of nested data
* Copying is slow
* Android background processes have problems
* Android doesn't provide helpful APIs 

We define:
* **safe storage/legacy storage**: A folder on the Android device which previously would not be deleted after uninstall (safe). Due to Android changes, this folder is now slow. And after AnkiDroid 2.16:
   * new users will be unable to use this folder
   * old users will be able to use this folder until they uninstall the app, after which the folder will be inaccessible from. AnkiDroid
* **unsafe storage**: The folder that we will use with AnkiDroid 2.16. Android will offer to delete this folder on uninstall, wiping both user data and backups
* **storage migration**: the process of copying data from a 'safe storage' location to 'unsafe storage'
* **Deck Picker**: Main screen of AnkiDroid
* **safe folder** a folder which is not deleted on uninstall

----

1. When an existing user starts the app, we want to inform them that they have 'legacy storage' and they need to upgrade.
2. If a user declines, we want an icon for them to press to continue the process
3. We can backup to a **safe folder**, but we cannot run AnkiDroid from a **safe folder**
4. If we annoy the user enough that they uninstall the app, we've lost our chance to migrate and need to handle this via complex user support (or losing users). We don't want this. Users don't want this.

**Use cases of the icon**
* If a user is neither backing up, nor syncing, we want to warn them that uninstalling will make data inaccessible, and pressing an icon to press to offer suggestions to fix it.
* If a user is eligible for a storage migration (user has backups/is syncing), a user may 'postpone' a storage migration, in which the icon reminds them that this has been postponed.

In 55275ef89daf539592bb3d78321b55fc00c98979 / [URL] we introduce `ic_migrate`.

But in my mind, this icon does not indicate the use cases. In addition, white on yellow is not a good color scheme.

A proposed flow for this process has been added: [URL]

I have also added some thoughts on the [previous pull request]([URL]

We need someone to take ownership of a good icon to display to the user, and to think hard about the use cases and flow which are proposed to see how they can be improved from a UX perspective

[SCREENSHOT]
reason: The review accurately captures the main concern about data loss during storage migration but slightly distorts the terminology by referring to 'unsafe storage' instead of 'legacy storage' and lacks mention of the need for a better icon.

issue_title: Scoped storage: allow keeping collection in the legacy location
generated_review: AnkiDroid, although a fantastic tool, seems to lack the option to keep collections in the legacy location even after uninstallation. You didn't want to think about this but here you are 😛

...at some time I suggested allowing importing from an existing AnkiDroid folder. Why? Imagine that instead of updating the app, which would retain access to legacy storage, the user uninstalls & reinstalls AnkiDroid, which would make it lose that access. Wot do? This is what the dreary Figma points are about, such as “your current storage location ... will be inaccessible if the app is unistalled”. Importing from a folder is supposed to be easy to implement, so why not?

But then I thought that I would honestly keep my AnkiDroid folder where it is. I hardly care about speed. I can wait for sync. Reviewing is fast enough. I care more about the fact that the folder doesn't disappear by any chance. Perhaps many an user would feel likewise?

So I suggest completely reworking scoped storage with the idea that we can keep the data where it is. We'd need to ask the user to grant the RW permission to the AnkiDroid folder, a dialog that many users will be familiar to, and easy enough to comprehend for those who never saw it.

issue_title: New AnkiDroid installation should open ~/AnkiDroid with user help
generated_review: I'm really enjoying using AnkiDroid for my studies, but I encountered an issue during installation. The app didn't seem to recognize my previous AnkiDroid files, which is causing problems. Could you please help me get my old data back? I'm not very tech-savvy, so any assistance would be greatly appreciated.
issue_body:
It is possible that this issue is impossible to resolve. So don't waste too much time trying to resolve it. But if you have an idea we didn't have, or if you tried anything, please answer below so that other people don't waste their time trying the same thing.

This issue is resolved when new installs of the app can use already existing AnkiDroid folder. Technically,:
* Let's assume you have an ankidroid folder at ~/AnkiDroid. % 1
* Let's assume that you know want to install a version of the app not related to your current install. That targets SDK 30, % 2 . This way, the version of the app you install do not have access to all storage.

To resolve this issue, with the new version of the app, we should have the following journey:
* the user go to advanced settings, and find a button to manually select a folder for their collection,
* the user navigate to a folder `~/AnkiDroid`, (currently known as /storage/emulated/0/AnkiDroid on my device)
* The app checks that this folder contains a collection you can open % 3
* The app open this collection
* the user can review, sync, that is, allow AnkiDroid as usual

Ideally, but slightly less important:
* if the user restart ankidroid, you can still access the collection.

Note that you can't "just" use the advanced settings and change the folder. Indeed, you won't have the right to read the content of this folder. If you just try to change teh folder today, you'll get 
> com.ichi2.anki.exception. Storage AccessException: No write access to AnkiDroid directory /storage/emulated/0/AnkiDroid" 

Instead, I assume you should uses `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE` to request the right to access this folder and keep those rights. But any other solution you find would be acceptable too.

This is a duplicate of #13134, but hopefully, some contributors can read this issue and understand it without needing the whole context about scoped-storage.

We do not yet know whether this issue can really be solved. If you can't solve it, we must know what you tried so that we don't waste time trying the same thing. In any case, we expect it to be a complex issue.


% 1 you can use parallel build A to do this. A version such before 91, so that it default to legacy storage. E.g. the one at [URL] 
% 2 You can copy the small code change on [URL] to enable it on your build
% 3 otherwise, it's okay to just crash for a proof of concept. In a full fledged solution, we'll need to handle this gracefully

```bash
./gradlew packagePlayDebug packagePlayDebugAndroidTest --daemon
./gradlew uninstallAll jacocoAndroidTestReport --daemon
```

But if you do this:

```bash
./gradlew clean uninstallAll jacocoTestReport :api:lintRelease :AnkiDroid:lintPlayRelease ktlintCheck lint-rules:test
```

... there is some implicit dependency on the build dir used by the report and various tasks that drop things in the build dir, specifically:


```

The general idea in modern gradle is to define inputs / outputs explicitly on tasks vs depending on files and directories and things with `**/dirname` etc - and we could improve that a lot.

It is also possible that simply defining the task dependencies better for the jacoco test tasks could do it, for instance making it depend on assemblePlayDebug or similar, but then we run into problems with the APK signing configuration and need for passwords etc.

generated_review: Audio playback freezes card load.
issue_body:
### - [X] This issue is not a duplicate ### 1. Unzip the file and import the collection: [money.zip]([URL] 2. Preview the card with the Front side of "Money with Mathjax". 3. Reveal the backside.
Card Details: The card contains 4 fields: Front, Back, Audio, and AudioMoney. Front: ``` {{Front}} ``` Back: ``` {{Front}}
{{Back}} {{Audio}} {{AudioMoney}} ```
### The backside should show the loaded card. ### The backside is not displayed.
Screenshot: [SCREENSHOT]
### Debug info ```text AnkiDroid Version = 2.16alpha94-debug Android Version = 13 Manufacturer = Google Model = sdk_gphone64_x86_64 Hardware = ranchu Webview User Agent = Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 13; sdk_gphone64_x86_64 Build/TE1A.220922.021; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/103.0.5060.71 Mobile Safari/537.36 ACRA UUID = 2daf5ce1-b594-44bb-b526-3ccb31f1a1e6 New schema = true Scheduler = std2 Crash Reports Enabled = false DatabaseV2 Enabled = true ``` ### (Optional) Anything else you want to share? This was tested multiple ways: - My physical phone, with release 2.16alpha94 (from Github) - Built with Android Studio and ran it on an emulator to [this commit]([URL] - The latest stable release version on Github (2.15.6), with the same emulator ### Background on what this code is doing in the first place (to prevent the x-y problem): The main problem I was trying to solve is **to have a play button on the front side of the card, without having the audio played automatically**. However, I want audio to be automatically played on the backside of the card. There does not seem to be a built-in approach to simply not have an audio file play on any Anki implementation without turning off audio replays on all card sides, so my current approach is to have two audio files: `silence.wav` and (some sentence audio).wav, and use javascript to immediately play the `silence.wav` file. This approach only plays silence.wav, and overrides the natural order of how the audio is played (as if the user played `silence.wav` manually), thus the sentence audio does not play. (A different approach that I believe would work is to have a very very long silence.wav file, i.e. 24 hours long. This would remove the need of using javascript to play the file in order to stop the other file from playing). Unfortunately, something weird is happening with AnkiDroid. The audio plays as expected, i.e. the card with the front side "Money" has two audio files: the first one plays "Realm of the mad god", and the second one plays "Money x7". The second audio file is correctly played, and skips the first audio file. However, adding mathjax (i.e. the card with "Money with Mathjax") visually reveals the main problem: it seems like the card never "fully loads". The webview on **both of these cards displays a persistent blue line at the top**, suggesting that some javascript is still running and never finishes. This also suggests that **Mathjax itself is not actually related to the problem**, but simply a side effect that visually reveals the problem.
Screenshot of blue line on card "Money" [SCREENSHOT]
Using Chrome's webview on the "Money with Mathjax" card, the `mathjax-needs-to-render` CSS class is forever present on the backside of the card, and is not replaced with `mathjax-rendered`, which is the reason why the card doesn't show in the first place. I believe this suggests that something in the `onPageFinished` function of `AnkiDroid/src/main/assets/scripts/card.js` doesn't properly run in the first place. --- ### Workaround While writing this bug report, I basically rubber-ducked myself into a satisfactory workaround: we can use `onShownHook` and append a function to this array to play the audio. For example: ```js (() => { async function playMoney() { let x = document.querySelector("#audiomoney .soundLink, #audiomoney .replaybutton"); if (x) { console.log("going to click money..."); x.click(); console.log("clicked on money"); } } if (onShownHook !== undefined) { onShownHook.push(playMoney); } })(); ``` Due to a) "Javascript functionality is provided without any support or warranty" according to the Anki manual, b) this is a very niche bug that most people probably won't deal with, and c) there exists a satisfactory workaround, I'll be closing this issue despite it not being technically fixed. Hopefully, if anyone comes across the same issue, this can serve as a good reference for them! ### - [X] I am reporting a bug specific to AnkiDroid (Android app) - [X] I have checked the [manual]([URL] and the [FAQ]([URL] and could not find a solution to my issue - [X] ([instructions]([URL]

issue_title: `MigrateUserData` raises an exception that is not very helpful
generated_review: AnkiDroid completely broke on me! Can't migrate data because of some confusing error message. Fix this NOW, it's been days!
issue_body:
#13651 currently uses [`getUserFriendlyErrorText`]([URL] a rather primitive but improvable way of getting at least some sort of a short but not entirely useless message from an exception, and its traceback for debug information to be copied to clipboard. `MigrateUserData` in case of a failure [throws an `AggregateException`]([URL] with a not-so-helpful message, and does not expose sub-exceptions via stack trace text.

I suggest:
  * to not use `AggregateException` (I do not understand why it is used); or
  * to change in the following way:
     * throw the sub-exception and not `AggregateException` if there's only one; or if not,
     * have a message/localized message that reads something like “5 errors, the last being: division by zero”, or maybe special-case it in `getUserFriendlyErrorText`,
     * override `printStackTrace()` to also print all sub-exception stack traces.

issue_title: Quick swipe left/right action for card/note browser entries.
generated_review: Switching to a different flashcard app was never something I planned on doing, but the lack of swift navigation in AnkiDroid has made studying tiresome and time-consuming. issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, there's too much actions required when performing some of the common actions in the card/note browser. This makes performing actions to various cards more of a chore or only optimized for batch operations. doing one-off actions for a couple cards needs more taps and presses than actually comfortable with.

For example, I'm browsing in a deck and want to quickly suspend cards i remember had trouble with. Currently, this takes quite a lot of taps and presses.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A solution to this is to implement quick swipe left/right actions. The way it would work is by allowing the user to assign an action associated with swiping left/right one of the entries in the card browser. This is similar to UI/UX on other apps, like Spotify and YouTube.

For example, i would solve my problem above by assigning "suspend card" to the swipe left action. Then, go back to browsing my decks and quickly pick off cards i had trouble with.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
1. long tap or single tap to access a row of buttons underneath an entry corresponding to various actions. This might not be preferable as not only it changes user interaction, but also requires more icon/logo work.
2. place a row of buttons on the bottom/top of the card browser. limits screen space further, which i'm not a fan of. also icons work.
3. swap long press and single tap actions (edit note <-> selection mode). i hope this could be considered as a config. an extension of this would be to allow the user to customize actions for single tap, long press, etc.
4. app bar buttons for card browser also. like the setting for the reviewer, having the user be able to customize the buttons in the app bar would also be great solution.

**Additional context**
nothing necessary i believe.

Hi guys,

Just in case you weren't already aware of this, it looks like Google may have selectively blocked you after that May 1 deadline:

[URL]

----

AnkiDroid is not available in the Play Store for new Android versions until we release version 2.16 that migrates to the new scoped storage regime that Google requires.

**WORKAROUND**

If you must have AnkiDroid on a newer Android version now, and the Play Store says it is not available, you have a few ways to get it:

- **Beta channel**: 
  - join the Beta channel in the Play Store [URL]
  - we are rolling out 2.16.0 betas right now (currently at 40% rollout) to beta testers and you may receive 2.16.0beta versions after a day or so, then you are set
- **Alpha channel**:
  - If you still have not received the betas you may not be in the target population (#13801) at which point you may join the alpha channel [URL]
  - *all* our builds are promoted through alpha first, so even though we are at the "beta" release phase at the moment, they go through the alpha channel. All builds are rolled out to 100% of alpha testers though so you are guaranteed to receive v2.16
- **Direct install**:
  - grab the release directly from our releases page
  - you will likely want the "arm64-v8a" apk [URL]

generated_review: AnkiDroid is an invaluable tool for my studies, but the recurring 'Collection not opened' error during theme changes is driving me insane! Please, developers, I urge you to address this issue as soon as possible. It disrupts my learning flow and causes unnecessary stress.
issue_body:
Another problem with starting the service right away when starting the migration. 

A service means that the app will be much less likely to get killed while migrating essential files. You'd think that this very good, and it is, but this also means that deck picker will be more likely to get recreated or finished and relaunched while essential file migration is taking place, unlocking the UI.

However while it will be more of a problem in this case, it is a problem now as well. For instance, if you change device theme while essential files are being migrated, you are going to see the “Collection not opened error”. This here is a more general problem with `withProgress`; it is a function that shows some UI that is tied to current activity and is commonly launched in its lifecycle scope, yet often the code inside of it is ***not*** UI-related, such as running migration. That is to say, it's misused. I think we can try to fix the simple cases using a dialog fragment, but we really want to properly move to view model & friends. Also note that:
* The `launchCatchingTask {}` block is canceled when the activity is destroyed, potentially ruining the job that is performed
* A block that is canceled in this way but still running will leak the activity

But when using a service for it we can expect the activity to be not only recreated, but also completely finished and relaunched. In this case we are going to lose our fragment.

I suppose that ideally we will have to introduce yet another state—for migrating essential files—and deal with it like we deal with the UI for media migration, recreating the progress dialog.

Reverse proxies and self signed certificates fail to function.  

**Additional context**
This is related to the requirement for https on the custom sync server.  The requirement makes sense for those using a server on the internet.  However the easiest and most straight forward use case of the custom sync server (sync directly to my desktop) is no longer functional.

issue_title: LaunchCatchingTask should be adapted for write
generated_review:
Title: AnkiDroid Needs Improvement in Saving Changes

Review: The app seems to have an issue with saving changes during a study session. If you exit the app before completing a review or editing a note, your progress might not be saved. I suggest looking into this for a better user experience. Thanks for all the hard work!
issue_body:
`launchCatchingTask`'s task does not start if the job is destoyed. That's perfectly acceptable if the task is here to get data to display. But there is nothing that ensure that the last review before reviewed is close, or the edition of a note, will actually be saved.
So, I guess that the tasks that write may need to be done on `GlobalScope` instead.
We should still keep the current activity, so that we can show error message on it, but only as a weak pointer, so as not to leak it. (Ideally, if there were a way to know current top level activty, so that it can be used in case of error, it would be great actually. Or to show an error message that does not require an activy that is displayed)

Thanks for @lukstbit review, that told me that we should not use `launchCatchingTask` in `onDestroy`, as I had not realized this pitfall

If you have ever shared a deck, you can probably relate to this situation: You publish the `.apkg` file on whatever platform your classmates are using, they download it, import it and start using it. After a few days, you notice an incorrect information in your deck, or perhaps a sentence that can be easily misinterpretted. So you fix it, export a new `.apkg` file, publish it again and write a message under it, in which you tell your classmates who imported the old version to download this new one and import it, so they can get the fixes. But, most of the classmates are not really paying attention to the platform (which is usually some kind of a group chat) and when they log in once in a while, they don't browse the older messages (including your patch of the deck). So they keep using the first version, learn incorrect information and then fail at exam (a bit of an extreme scenario, but nobody should learn incorrect things without knowing). So I created an automatic update checker. It works easily. The deck creator inserts the following code in the decks description: ```

Update check

``` Whenever the user opens the deck to study, an HTTP request is sent to my webserver, along with the ID of the package (not the Anki-database ID, but an ID set by my service when the creator uploads the first version) and the currently installed version (both are simple ints). My service then fetches the latest version number for the deck with the given ID, compares it with the installed version number from the request and if the installed version is a smaller number than the latest one, it responds with an "update-available" SVG image, that is displayed in the `` element in the code above: [SCREENSHOT] The user than clicks/taps the image, that is within the `` element and is taken to the `MY-DOMAIN/update/PACKAGE-ID/INSTALLED-VERSION` webpage. This webpage performs one more version comparasion check (in case the deck creator forgot to update the version number in both `` and `` elements) and if the versions are not equal, the user is then redirected to the download page that the deck creator specified. If the version numbers are the same, a different SVG image is displayed in the deck description: [SCREENSHOT] This all works in the desktop version of Anki (as portraied in the screenshots above), but not so much in AnkiDroid. In AnkiDroid, I see a green square instead of the image: [SCREENSHOT] I did some research and according to Bing AI, this is most likely caused by the app's Content Security Policy, which limits loading of external sources. While I understand the need to protect users from potentionally malicious content being downloaded and displayed after simply clicking an Anki Deck, I believe that that wasn't the intended use here. Because if I use the updater HTML code on a card instead of in the deck's description, the external image loads just fine. **Describe the solution you'd like** Unify the CSP rules and allow loading images from external sources in deck description. **Describe alternatives you've considered** If this was intended (or if, god forbid, you disable loading external images in cards as well), could my domain get an exception from the rule? The server-side source code is open source and anyone can audit it. I'd send a link to the GitHub repo here, but I'm not sure if that wouldn't count as advertisment. Let me know if you want to see it. ## TL:DR Check the HTML code block, the first two images are its output in desktop version of Anki, the third image is its output in AnkiDroid

issue_title: [BUG]: Background activity getting destroyed and recreated due to low memory causes an error when performing an EXPORT
generated_review: Experiencing frequent issues while exporting my study decks on AnkiDroid. Seems like there's a problem with background activities being destroyed and recreated in low memory situations, leading to an unexpected crash upon saving. Could be a memory management concern that needs attention. Would appreciate a fix soon as I rely heavily on this app for my studies. Thanks!
issue_body: ### - [X] This issue is not a duplicate ### #### Environment Setup: To mimick low memory situation, turn on the following developer option for the device Developer Options -> Don't keep activities #### Steps to Reproduce: 1. From the Decks home screen, select Export collection from the menu 2. On the upcoming "Export read" dialog, click "Save to" 3. Select a place to save the file and select SAVE 4. AnkiDroid crashes ### After saving is complete the app should return to the _Decks_ home screen. ### After returning from the save dialog, the app crashes ### Debug info - version: 2.17alpha6 - ran on emulator (Pixel 7 API 33) Ultimately the error that I was seeing was ```text kotlin.UninitializedPropertyAccessException: lateinit property mExportFileName has not been initialized ``` `mExportFileName` is from `ActivityExportingDelegate`. If `DeckPicker` gets killed in the background because of low memory then the `onCreate` for `DeckPicker` will be called again after returning from the export dialogs. issue_title: [BUG]: "New cards in random order" is not semantically consistent with what it says

- [X] This issue is not a duplicate

### 

I know other issues exist, like [URL] But this issue is related to the semantics.

Based on the [docs]([URL] when we choose **New cards in random order**, Anki randomly sorts **the existing** cards.

This needs to be semantically corrected. The thing that Anki does is called **shuffling**. You have to add a shuffle option for what it does now.

What I understood and asked many of my friends to see what they have understood shows me that all of us thought that choosing **New cards in random order** means that *hey Anki, whatever I add, when I want to memorize new cards, select one from the unseen cards one by random. This is very different from what it does.

### 

The **New cards in random order** should be semantically consistent with what it does. It should do what it says. When selecting this option, it should choose one from the unseen cards at random, not randomly sort the existing cards.

It says one thing; it does another thing.

When I was implementing my two-button-answer card template, which replaces the native four answer buttons, I discovered that the toasts for undo, leech, etc appear over my template-rendered buttons and prevent me from interacting with my buttons until I click the toast or wait for it to disappear on its own. Usually this isn't a bother with leeches because reading/comprehending the front of my card takes time, but if I click "undo" I want to be able to correct my answer as soon as possible, and the toasts appearing directly over my buttons makes me click an extra time. It's a subtle but mildly annoying interaction when trying to replace the native buttons with buttons in a card template.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I'd like an API call I can call from my card template that tells ankidroid where toasts can be rendered to not obscure my buttons. Whether this is done with some sort of keepout zone, an offset from the bottom of the webview, or just setting an origin point for the toast, any of those ways would work for me.

I can't think of any alternatives, short of interrogating the webview renderer for positions of buttons to influence the toast position, which sounds worse than just letting a template set the position itself via an API. This is a very subtle interaction that, before now, I'm guessing no one thought of when implementing answer button calls in the Javascript API.

I guess #15070, but only because I noticed both issues when trying to implement custom answer buttons in card templates to replace native answer buttons.

issue_title: Reintroduce Deck Selector to Statistics Page
generated_review: Wth is wrong with you guys?! Old Stats page was way better! Now I have to struggle to find my decks! Bring back the deck selector already!
issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The old Statistics screen used to have a deck selector on top, making it easy to switch between different decks and see their statistics. However, this deck selector is no longer there in the new version of the Statistics screen.

Now, the only ways to switch the deck used for Statistics are:
1. Select a deck to review (to switch the current deck), back out, then open Statistics
2. Type in the deck name (which can be quite long) as a search query

Both of these options are quite awkward.

One thing to note is that both Anki Desktop and AnkiMobile have a deck selector available for their stats page, so AnkiDroid is actually missing functionality that is available in other parts of the Anki ecosystem.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Ideally we add a deck picker to the top bar, which is where the old Statistics screen had the deck picker and is consistent with the Card Browser.

**Implementation Notes**
Both Anki Desktop and AnkiMobile implement the deck switching by having the Deck Selector set the Current Deck and then reloading the Statistics page.

However, taking the same approach and setting the Current Deck in the Statistics deck picker can be problematic with AnkiDroid's current UI flow, since the Statistics page is accessible from the Reviewer via the sidebar.

If we set the Current Deck in the Statistics deck picker, it will result in the reintroduction of this bug: [URL] which we have resolved for now precisely by not changing the Current Deck.

Some options to deal with this on the top of my head:
1. Make the deck picker change the Current Deck and find another solution for dealing with the Reviewer state inconsistency issue (for example, it looks like Anki Desktop detects the change and refreshes the Reviewer upon return).
2. Reworking the UI flow so that you have to exit the Reviewer in order to access the Card Browser or Statistics page.
3. Find a way to expose a parameter for the deck in the Statistics webpage (will involve changing code in the Anki Desktop repo) and then pass in the selected deck without changing the Current Deck.

- [ ] Show a snackbar or a toast in EVERY single card that ReadText runs. I want to be annoying here so people migrate fast

issue_body:
### 

- [X] This issue is not a duplicate

### 

1. Manage note types
2. Tap add note type "+" button
3. Change the name to the name of one of the default note types: "Basic", " Cloze", etc
4. The "OK" button becomes un-clickable/grayed out even a note type with that name does not exist already

A quick workaround is to create the model with any name and then it can be renamed to a default note type. The naming restriction seems to only apply during note type creation, not renaming.

### 

Desktop behavior seems to allows adding a model with a default name if it doesn't already exist. If it does exist, desktop adds "-8dc2c" or some other random string. It does this silently and only after hitting ok, which I don't think this is ideal, but it's probably what is expected.

### 

1. Ankidroid doesn't allow creating of a note type with a default name, even if a note type with that name does not exist.
2. Ankidroid appends the random string before clicking ok, which I think is actually better than desktop's silently adding it, but it does differ in this way.

issue_title: [Design] Inconsistent String Casing
generated_review: AnkiDroid is great app for learning! But sometimes the capital letters in titles make it hard to read smoothly. Hope developers can fix this inconsistency for better understanding.
issue_body:
## Current Problem
AnkiDroid utilizes Anki strings, which are typically in Title Case. However, AnkiDroid strings are predominantly in Sentence case, resulting in inconsistent strings.

## Solution
Changing Title cases strings to Sentence case or vice versa (see Strings affected for title case strings)

## Why use Title Case?
- Let’s Make It Official. Looks serious, right? Exactly!
- Grabs reader attention. Capitalized phrases stand out from the crowd, as [Pieter Heyman]([URL] nicely put it.
- Keeps a nice visual rhythm. Of course, as long as the sentences are short.
[Stands out]([URL] Title Case differentiates title from the body text.
- Maintains symmetry. Yet, works only for short texts (ex. Buttons, Labels)

## Why use Sentence case?
- Consistency. Easier to maintain across different platforms.
- Clarity. Easy to navigate and skim, thank you, [John Saito]([URL] (ex. Home > About us)
- People love it. Yes, we love having human-ish conversations with apps.
[Casual]([URL] Gives an impression that anyone can use the product.
- Easier to localize. Much much easier and less stressful.

[Source above]([URL]

## Human Interface Guideline (HID)
### [GNOME]([URL]
  - **Header capitalization** should be used for any **headings**, including headings in **header bars**, **tab titles**, and **view titles**. It should also be used for **short control labels** that do not normally form proper sentences, such as **button labels**, **switch labels** and **menu items**
  - **Sentence capitalization** should be used for ****labels that form sentences** or that run on to other text**, including **labels for check boxes**, **radio buttons**, **sliders**, **text entry boxes**, **field labels and combobox labels**. It should also be used for **explanatory or body text**, such as in **dialogs or notifications**

### [KDE]([URL]

Use sentence case when:

* The text ends with a period or colon.
* The text is clearly a sentence.
* The text is a subtitle, tooltip, transient status message, or placeholder label.
* The text is used as a label for a radio button, checkbox, combobox item, or placed in front of a control — for example using `Kirigami.FormData.label`.

Otherwise, use title case.

Also use title case for specialized proper nouns such as “the Internet” or “Plasma Widgets”.

### [Material Design 3]([URL] Use sentence case, unless it is specified

* Unless otherwise specified, use sentence-style capitalization, where only the first letter of the first word in a sentence or phrase is capitalized. All text, including titles, headings, labels, menu items, and buttons should use sentence-style capitalization.
* Products and branded terms may also be capitalized.

### [Apple]([URL] No specification

## Strings Affected (Updated as Version: 2.23alpha, Jul, 25, 2025)

### Decks
#### Get shared decks
🔎 Deck **Search**

#### Create filtered deck
Filtered **Deck** (copied from above)

* Create Toolbar Item: HTML **Before Selection**, HTML **After Selection**

* Create **Filtered Decks**: Filtered **Deck** (Placeholder text, also found in Create filtered deck in Decks)
* Card info: Card **Type**, Note **Type**
* Change column: Card **Type**, Note **Modified**, Note **Type**

#### Select a card (press & hold)

* Export card > Include: Selected **Notes**

## Anki Webpages/Strings

Make the inversion feature as an option of "Appearance" or "Accessibility" in the settings.

Restore the comprehensive night mode text color inversion feature as a default feature of AnkiDroid, make the Desktop Version consistent colors currently in 2.17 an option under Appearance for power users.

Telling users to simply edit their decks CSS is not a reasonable alternative, for two reasons.

issue_title: Synchronize the intervals for the pairs of primary and reversed cards.
generated_review:
Title: Inconsistent Interval Progress for Primary and Reverse Cards in AnkiDroid

Dear developers, I've been using AnkiDroid for my English vocabulary studies and find it an incredible help. However, I've encountered an issue with the 'Reversed Cards' feature. When I learn a word pair, both the direct and reverse translations have their own distinct progress. This leads to a disorganized and disparate interval progression, causing one card to advance while the other lags behind. To remedy this, I suggest synchronizing the intervals for both primary and reversed cards within a single note, so the learning process remains consistent and efficient. Looking forward to seeing this improvement in
issue_body:
I am learning English vocabulary from Oxford CEFR using Anki/AnkiDroid. It's a cool app. It is probably the only one of the interval repetition applications that allows me to adjust the growth rate of the interval for myself.

It often happens that I easily remember a direct translation. But it's hard to remember the reverse translation, or I don't remember the reverse translation at all. Or the opposite happens.

When I learning English words, the "reversed cards" function is very useful. But the problem is that one note gets 2 cards. Direct and reverse. And each of these two cards has its own separate progress. The intervals of two cards from a pair are messy and chaotic.

As a result, two cards get different intervals, where one card can go far ahead and the second one lags behind. This results in a loss of synchronization and more disorder. It's bad.

It would be great if user could choose different models for working with intervals of such card pairs.

1 - Calculation of the average interval for such a pair. And assigning this interval to both cards with a small difference. So that they are shown not on the same day, but with a small interval between them.

2 - The application can also calculate only the interval of the main card. And the interval for the inverted card is calculated so that it is shown only between the displays of the main card.

3 - Or, even better, align the progress according to the card that received the smallest interval. The second card (which has a longer interval) should just be shown next to it for several days.

I like the 3rd option the most right now. But the other 2 can also be useful to many users. The application could offer users to choose one of the models for working with reversed cards in deck preferences.

issue_title: [Bug] TTS verbally exposes clozed text on Front of card when the clozed text includes HTML text formatting. (Specifically, ">" character)
generated_review: Sometimes, the talking part of the app speaks out the hidden words with some extra stuff when I use bold or underline in my cards. It's a bit confusing, could you fix please?
issue_body:
###### Reproduction Steps

1. Create an note with a cloze deletion. 
2. Within the cloze, insert HTML text formatting using the Bold, Italic, or Underline button.
3. Example front card text: This is a {{c1::<u>cloze</u> deletion}} card
4. Enable text-to-speech using the tts tag in the front and rear card templates. 
Example of tts tag used:
{{tts en_US voices=Apple_Samantha,Microsoft_Zira speed=1.5:cloze:Text}}
5. Enter card review and observe the TTS output.

###### Expected Result
TTS reads the card text, and upon reaching a cloze deletion, says "Blank", then continues through any remaining text that is not clozed.


###### Actual Result
Upon reaching a cloze deletion containing HTML, the entire instance of clozed text is spoken, along with some unusual bug text. For example: TTS will say "This is a cloze **data ordinal equals one inches** blank deletion card"

Bolded text is the "unusual bug text". When there is a Cloze 2 or a Cloze 3 that contains HTML formatting, TTS will change the bug text to say **data ordinal equals two inches** or **data ordinal equals three inches**, respectively. If there are multiple  clozes on the same card (i.e. two instances of Cloze 1) but only one contains HTML formatting, only that cloze will be revealed, while the other cloze will be correctly pronounced as "Blank".

More specifically, the offending character seems to be ">". The presence of any number of ">" will result in the entire cloze being revealed.

This effectively breaks the TTS function, as the card review is ruined when the content  is unexpectedly reviewed. Although it may not affect every card in the deck due to lack of formatting in some cards, any cards affected will no longer have an accurate review history in the FSRS algorithm.

This appears to be an issue exclusive to AnkiDroid, it does not seem to affect Anki Desktop, and furthermore, AnkiDroid's legacy TTS engine does not suffer the same issue. The issue is present on both the stable Google Play version and ~~current version~~ 2.18alpha5.

generated_review:
Title: Desire for Customizable Interface

Review: It's been a while since I started using AnkiDroid, and one thing that I find particularly bothersome is the fixed placement of the 'easy' and 'hard' buttons. This would streamline my study sessions and make my experience with AnkiDroid even better. I hope this feature can be included in the next update. Thank you!
issue_body:
### 

- [X] This issue is not a duplicate

### 

- [X] This bug does not occur in the latest version of Anki

### 

Ever since I've been using AnkiDroid, in the communities I've been in, it's always been said that it's problematic to click on the "easy" and "hard" buttons. Whether this is the case or not, a culture has been created of AnkiDroid users who prefer to click only on the "again" and "good" buttons. Even if the problem was never really real or has been solved, people continue to click only on "again" and "good".

### 

It would therefore be refreshing to be able to hide buttons, especially the "easy" and "hard" buttons. Since not everyone finds these buttons useful, it would be nice to have only the two buttons that will decide the spacing trajectory on screen during the review: "again" and "good". There will be less visual pollution, more pragmatic minimalism.

### 

Nowadays, even though many people don't use the "easy" and "hard" buttons, they take up space on the screen so people don't focus as much as they should on the buttons that are actually used: "again" and "good". They may even accidentally confuse themselves when clicking.

issue_title: [BUG]: <audio> html tag doesn't always load the whole audio
generated_review: AnkiDroid is usually great, but after recent update, some audio files don't play completely. I figured out adding 'preload="auto"' to audio tag solved it. Let's hope dev team fixes this soon!
issue_body:
### 

- [X] This issue is not a duplicate

### 

- [ ] This bug does not occur in the latest version of Anki

### 

I use ankidroid for 4 years. After one of the recent updates (or maybe it's not even an ankidroid update) for some of the cards, that were perfectly fine before, there is an error "failed to load". Despite that, audio still loads, but only some part of it. Looks similar to a video buffering on youtube, the first part loads, but the rest doesn't.
Windows version works fine. And even in other apps the same audio file is played normally, it's not corrupted.
I found a solution - adding an attribute preload="auto" to the <audio> tag. With that the whole audio loads without problems.

### 

Audio inside the <audio> HTML tag loads fully without errors

### 

For some audios I get an error "failed to load". Despite that, audio still loads, but only some part of it.
adding  preload="auto" to the <audio> tag fixes the problem. It probably forces the browser to preload the whole audio, instead of loading it in chunks

issue_title: Discussion around Deck Deletion
generated_review: I accidentally deleted one of my study decks on AnkiDroid and I'm really upset about it. I didn't get any warning before it happened and now I don't know how to get it back. Can someone help me?
issue_body:
I am not confortable with the way deck deletion works today.
We used to ask user to confirm that they want to delete a deck, before deleting it. This was changed in #11740 when introducing the new schema.
As shown in [URL] it was deemed that it's not necessary to ask for confirmation anymore because this action is now undoable.

I have a few issues:
* it's not clear how to undo it if you miss the "undo" snackbar that appears at the bottom. I know you can find "undo" in the three-dots menu, but we can't expect every one to know it. And even with "undo" in the menu bar, it would not be clear to everyone. Worse, given that the user potentially lost a ton of data, it's not a time where they want to experiment around and try to figure out how to undo.
* they have no way to know what was deleted. The snackbar only show the number of deleted cads. That used to be acceptable, because, during the confirmation stage, the user could see the name of the deck they were going to delete. Now, if they delete the wrong deck and the number of cards seems reasoanable, they can end up deleting the wrong deck and realizing it too late. And while I know the name of the deck appear as the header of the potential actions on deck, the "delete deck" entry it the last one. So it's quite possible that a user tapped "delete deck" without seing the name of the deck. (Also, they can always tap on it by accident)

The problem with requesting a confirmation is that it takes more time. If someone were to delete a dozen of deck, that would be very frustrating. I don't think this is a scenario we want to optimize. Reducing the risk of data loss seems more important to me.

If we were to decide that actually, it's really acceptable not to ask for confirmation, then at least I think we should update the snackbar to let the user know which deck was deleted. (It may be interesting to update it anyway)

If we don't ask for confirmation, we should rename `confirmDeckDeletion` given that there is no confirmation anymore. And maybe delete the code of `DeckPickerConfirmDeleteDeckDialog` which is currently unused.

There is a related question with shorcuts. Do we want the "delete" key to delete the deck ? If so, do we want to request a confirmation first ? This is what @SanjaySargam is doing in #16679. Personally, I don't think it's a good idea, because it's not clear what deck the user selected, and they can't easily change the selection with their keyboard (unless it's a split screen, in which case the selected deck is displayed on the trailing side of the screen). But if we actually were to use the shortcut, I think having a confirmation step is even more important than with the "delete deck" from the menu's entry
reason: The review captures the main issue of accidental deck deletion and lack of warning, but it omits details about the undo feature and the user's confusion regarding how to recover the deleted deck.

issue_title: Improve typing of `findViewById`
generated_review: Dear developers, I appreciate your hard work on AnkiDroid. However, I noticed an issue with the 'findViewById' method, seems it doesn't help much in figuring out if the returned view is nullable or not. I suggest considering a change to 'requireViewByID' for better type safety, especially since API 28 introduced 'requireViewById'. Thank you!
issue_body:
This change is very low priority. (And wait until a maintainer confirm they agree with this proposition. Right now, it's not certain this is what we want to do)

`findViewById`, defined for Activity and View, is neither Nullable nor NotNull. This means the typer can't help us decide whether the returned value should be treated as nullable or not, making code harder to reason about.

Api 28 introduce `requireViewById`, that throws if the view is not found and returns a non null value. I suggest we use similar code to improve our typing. Given that we can't reuse the function name, I suggest using `requireViewByID` until the day min sdk is 28.

The process for `AnkiActivity.findViewByID` would use the following steps:

# Definition

First we must introduce those methods. I do it in PR #16709.

# Using them
This method is used in 516 places in our codebase. Do the change slowly. Each PR should be relatively small. Maybe it should contains one big class, or many small ones.

PR #16709 shows an example of such usage.

You can do it as follow.

Replace `findViewById` by `findViewByID` everywhere in one file. The typer will complain every place we actually use the result as a non-null value. In those place, use `requireViewByID`. 

Or you could replace `findViewById` by `requireViewByID`. The type will complain when we check whether the result is nullable. In those places, use `findViewByID`.

In any case: ensure the change you makes make sense. That you are certain the result can be null/can never be null. And run the code you change to ensure it works as expected.

# Forbidding the use of `findViewById`

With the linter, we can ensure we don't use it anymore.

This is only when this linter exists that we can close the bug as fixed.
reason: The review accurately captures the main issue regarding the 'findViewById' method and suggests a relevant solution, but it lacks some detail about the implementation process and the context of the low priority.

issue_title: ChangeManager: not undoable operation should also notifies
generated_review: Widget contents outdated after sync/check actions without proper update notifications.
issue_body:
Right now, `notifySubscribers` is called on any undoable operation and on new day. (Funnily enough "undo" is an `undoableOp` too, so "undo" also notifies the subscriber)
It's not yet done on undoable operations.  Which means that, for example, the widget does not get notified that there its content should be updated.

So, this issue has two tasks:
* find all operation that change the database and can't be undone.
* ensure that all such operations calls `notifySubscribers`.

If there are actions that you find that can't be undone, and you can't easily find how to create the notification, you can simply create a new issue. Otherwise, you can directly create a PR to add the notification.

Right now, the operations I know of are:
* syncing
* full sync
* check card
* check database

I should note that those four operations are done in the deck picker, and we hard coded the deck picker to update when those operations are done. Previously, no other views could be opened while the deck picker was on screen, so it was never necessary to notify subscribers, because the only subscriber is the deck picker, and it was already listening.

Now that we are introducing widgets that display the state of the collection, it'll be necessary to notify the observers.


I think the object sent for notification should be simply `OpChanges` with all fields set to true, given that it's too hard to know what actually was changed.

Honestly, I don't even know how to find all tasks that need to be updated. I assume most of those tasks are in GeneratedBackend.kt. But it contains 445 functions, and there is no way to read all of them and be certain that we won't miss any function that change the collection and is not undoable.
reason: The review accurately captures the main issue of outdated widget content due to lack of update notifications after certain operations.

This shouldn't happen if there are no modifications made, especially since the behavior on Anki Desktop is different and more convenient in this situation. I understand the prompt might be trying to prevent accidental data loss, but in this case, it seems unnecessary and disruptive. I hope the developers consider fixing this issue in the upcoming updates to
issue_body:
How to reproduce:
* have a note type with a pinned field
* enter text in the field
* create the note
* try to leave the note editor

Expected:
* closing the note editor

Actual:
* A prompt "Discard current input"

I think that if the user made no change, we should just allow them to close the editor. Same as on anki desktop.
We could either listen to any change in text and record there was a change. Or record the state of the fields when the new "add note" was offered to the user and check whether we still have the same content. This way, if the user type by accident in the first field and then delete it, we know that it's okay for the user to save actually.

This is not the same bug as #15788, given that, in the current case, no prompt at all should appear
reason: The review accurately captures the source issue, detailing the prompt that appears when no changes are made and comparing it to the behavior on Anki Desktop.

This is what I haveby default on chromebook. I think when the screen is large, we should have more icons by default
[SCREENSHOT]

Admittedly, there is an issue with the fact that the display size can change, especially on chromebook.
I don't think that increarsing the number of icon which are displayed if there is enough room would be a good solution, because they would get to be displayed on phone too, which would reduce the size available for the name of the deck.

I don't know exactly what extra actions should be added in the menu. I'd be in favour of bury, suspend, mark note, but that's only because of my personal use. Ideally we'd need stats on what actions people regularly use, but that'd take far more time to gather.

Let's consider an item such as "suspend" that should be displayed by default on tablet and not on phone. 
My suggested solution would be that, when we check a preference value for an item, if the value is set, we honor what is set (as it means the user did an action), however, if the value in unset, the value we obtain instead depend on the size of the screen.
Admittedly, it means the default value displayed in our settings would be "menu only" on phone and "in the bar" on xlarge screen. that is, the value could appear to change when the user resize their application. This is not ideal, I doubt it would confuse a lot of people.

# alternative

A more complex solution, would be to detect when the screen size change. If the same user on the same device is sometime xlarge and sometime not, it means they can redimension their app (and they actually do it). In this case, we could offer an option "display on big screen only". 
I don't think this extra complexity is really worth it, but at least that would ensure the behavior I sugest could be reproduced by a choice the user make

issue_title: [BUG]: CardContentProvider uses the wrong authority uri in parallel builds
generated_review: Encountered an issue where the app couldn't fetch data due to incorrect authority URI in a parallel build setup. The error message 'Failed to find provider info for com.ichi2.anki.flashcards' was displayed. I followed the provided instructions but still encountered this problem.
issue_body:
### 

### 

- [x] This bug does not occur in the latest version of Anki Desktop

### 

1. Follow the instructions in [URL] namely `Gradle dependency` and `Manifest changes required on Android SDK 30+`, while replacing `com.ichi2.anki` with `com.ichi2.anki.a` (or another parallel build)
2. Execute a query with the content resolver, e.g.

```kt
val res: Cursor? = contentResolver.query(
    FlashCardsContract.Note.CONTENT_URI_V2,
    FlashCardsContract.Note.DEFAULT_PROJECTION,
    null,
    null,
    "${FlashCardsContract.Note._ID} desc"
);
```

### 

A non-null `Cursor` is expected. Instead, the following error message is logged: `Failed to find provider info for com.ichi2.anki.flashcards`

This is because AnkiDroid.A's manifest has set `CardContentProvider`'s authority uri to `${applicationId}.flashcards`, which in the parallel build expands to `com.ichi2.anki.a.flashcards`.
[URL]

If I try using that instead of `FlashCardsContract.Note.CONTENT_URI_V2`, i.e.
```kt
val res: Cursor? = contentResolver.query(
    Uri.parse("content://com.ichi2.anki.a.flashcards/notes_v2"),
    FlashCardsContract.Note.DEFAULT_PROJECTION,
    null,
    null,
    "${FlashCardsContract.Note._ID} desc"
);
```

the following exception is thrown:

```
FATAL EXCEPTION: main
Process: com.blah.app, PID: 15508
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: uri content://com.ichi2.anki.a.flashcards/notes_v2 is not supported
	at android.database.DatabaseUtils.readExceptionFromParcel(DatabaseUtils.java:172)
	at android.database.DatabaseUtils.readExceptionFromParcel(DatabaseUtils.java:142)
	at android.content.ContentProviderProxy.query(ContentProviderNative.java:481)
	at android.content.ContentResolver.query(ContentResolver.java:1226)
	at android.content.ContentResolver.query(ContentResolver.java:1158)
	at android.content.ContentResolver.query(ContentResolver.java:1114)
	at com.blah.app.MainActivity.stuff(MainActivity.kt:33)
        ...
```

The parallel build's content provider now responds, but since it still matches on the incorrect `FlashCardsContract.AUTHORITY`, the uri is deemed invalid
[URL]

### Debug info

AnkiDroid Version = 2.19beta6 (638d0e29cd91c49d6ca672ebc2494997751160ac)

Backend Version = 0.1.42-anki24.06.3 (24.06.3 d678e39350a2d243242a69f4e22f5192b04398f2)

Android Version = 12 (SDK 31)

### (Optional) Anything else you want to share?

One way might be to have `CardContentProvider` construct its own copy of `FlashCardsContract.AUTHORITY` using ~~`R.string.applicationId`~~ `BuildConfig.APPLICATION_ID`, before passing it to the matcher

issue_title: Card HTML includes ancient zoom/scroll hack - needs test, docs update, possible modernization
generated_review: Dear developers, I've noticed an issue while using AnkiDroid. Seems like the scroll position gets mixed up when flipping cards. Please look into this matter and improve the app's performance for better learning experience.
issue_body:
As the title says, card.html includes some dubious javascript that attempts to work around ancient webview limitations.

I attempted to remove that with:
- #17281 

...but it turns out that the old workaround is not just for image zooming (which appears to work now) but also for page scroll placement when cards are flipped - causing a serious regression:
- #17318 

...so I reverted that immediately with:
- #17336 

I do still think this area needs attention though, as the docs in the code are at minimum out of date, and a critical feature of the app (that the card flip scrolls things to the correct spot) has no test coverage.

So, to close this issue, two things should happen:

- We need an androidTest that verifies the location of the WebView page content on question side and answer side somehow. How? I don't know, perhaps a card with some javascript that creates some sort of rectangular space-occupying graphical feature that takes up exactly one screen for the question, and has an identifiable element at the bottom? And same for the answer side? And then you attempt to detect that the question one is there but answer one is not, for the question side, and the answer one is there but question one is not on the answer side? But really any way that works and is easy to understand
- We need to document that the javascript hack is more than just a zoomable workaround but also affects card scroll position so is at least currently needed

We *may* then try to move forward by perhaps using modern WebView programmability to zoom without using javascript page loaded hooks? For example one way is mentioned here 

[URL]

> The delay is likely there to wait for the WebView to complete rendering, which ensures it’s ready to scroll back to the saved position. However, a fixed delay might not be enough if rendering takes longer.
Instead of a hardcoded delay, we can check if the WebView is ready by using a ViewTreeObserver.OnGlobalLayoutListener. This listener triggers when the layout changes, which ensures the WebView is rendered before restoring the scroll position

issue_title: Remove/Replace `Press Alt+K to show keyboard shortcuts` warning
generated_review:
Title: Annoying Alt+K Keyboard Shortcut Warning

Review Text: I appreciate the usefulness of AnkiDroid, but the persistent reminder about the Alt+K keyboard shortcut is becoming increasingly frustrating. As a user, I don't always have access to an Alt key on different devices and systems. It would be great if this message could either be removed or replaced with more general instructions on finding keyboard shortcuts within system settings. Thanks!
issue_body:
Reasons for removing it:
1. Some keyboards may not have an `Alt` key
2. There is no need for a custom shortcut when the user can use the default of the system
- Go to the system `Settings` then search for `Keyboard shortcuts`, which will show a list with the system's shortcuts, including one for showing the list. That shortcut may very between keyboards and systems. It's `🔎+/` in the emulator, but `Cmd+;` in my tablet, as it doesn't have an `Alt` or `🔎` key, which solves the 1st problem with the custom shortcut.
- Using a custom one also breaks the user external consistency, because they won't be able to apply `Alt+K` in other apps.
3. The warning is useless after seeing once. Then becomes only annoying.
4. It's specially annoying after popping up because of a mispressed key

issue_title: Blur screen in recent apps to maintain privacy
generated_review: AnkiDroid is an excellent study tool, but it lacks basic privacy protection when minimized. Please consider implementing a feature to blur the screen in recent apps to safeguard sensitive information.
issue_body:
### Feature Request: Blur Screen in Recent Apps

**Description**:  
When AnkiDroid is minimized or the user switches to the recent apps menu, the app's content is fully visible in the preview. This can lead to potential privacy concerns, as sensitive data such as flashcards and notes can be exposed. To address this, I propose adding a feature that blurs or hides the app screen in the recent apps view.

**Expected Behavior**:  
When the user navigates to recent apps:
- The AnkiDroid app's preview screen should be blurred or replaced with a placeholder image (e.g., the AnkiDroid logo).
- The content should remain hidden until the app is reopened.

**Steps to Reproduce**:  
1. Open AnkiDroid.
2. Switch to the recent apps menu.
3. Observe that the app's content is visible in the preview.

**Additional Context**:  
Many apps, such as financial or messaging apps, implement this feature to protect user data. Adding this to AnkiDroid will enhance user privacy.

Thank you for considering this enhancement!
