issue_title: Investigate the relationship between shortcut and sync
generated_review: AnkiDroid app has problem with shortcut and sync. Sometimes, when I use shortcut to access my deck, it opens synching unexpectedly. Please fix this issue for better experience.
issue_body:
How to reproduce:
* Have a deck D with cards to review
* enable automated sync
* create a shortcut to D
* do some review.
* force cloze anki by swapping the app on the android app list, ensuring it does not sync on cloze
* wait 10 minutes
* open the deck D through the shortcut

With a recent change I introduced, this open the deck picker and automatically open the reviewer on top of it. I think I saw the sync view opening on top of the deck picker during not even a second.
We need to investigate what's going on exactly in the deck picker, related to sync.

Because, if the automated sync goes on and finish in 1 second, that's great. Data is synced, maybe media sync is ongoing, that's perfect. That even solved an issue I had related to sync and shortcut, and I would have solved it by accident.

If a force sync is needed, it seems that nothing occurs. Which is okay-ish. The user should probably be warned they need to force sync before they start their review. We should surely improve the behavior here.

What I'm effrayed is that if there is a long sync. Due to a lot of changes, new decks, card reviewed, you're on a device you've not used in months, and you have a slow internet connection, you may be able to start reviewing while sync is going on. And ankidroid is really not prepared to have anything going on in parallel to a collection sync.

I'm not sure. Someone need to investigate what is going on. Probably using breakpoint in the codebase to check whether sync is aborted, sync is going on normally, whether we can actually review while sync is going on (which would be quite bad)

Of course, this someone can be me when I've some free time and my mind is awake enough to be sure of my investigation. But if anyone else want to take a look, I'd appreciate that a lot.

issue_title: Releases supporting lower minSdk versions not retained in Play Store
generated_review: Ugh, updated to latest AnkiDroid and can't find my old app anymore! Lower devices stuck with outdated version? Fix this NOW!
issue_body:
### Problem

If you publish a new version of the app to the Play Store using the release script, any track, old ABI-split versions that support lower minSdks are deactivated and become invisible / uninstallable for those devices

### 

The new version should supercede all other versions that have the same minSdk, however (crucially!), the older versions that were the last ones supporting a given minSdk before minSdk was changed should be retained and included in the release

### Investigation

Retention of old lower-minSdk artifacts appears to have broken when ABI splits were introduced.
The non-ABI split APKs from 2.7, 2.8.4 and 2.10.4 appear to retain automatically

### Remediation

I generated new APKs for release-2.19 (2.19.4, specifically) and they are on the open testing track right now.

I am also attempting a production track release that has included 2.20.1, 2.19.4, as well as 2.16.3. That manually repair the issue for all but minSdk 16 --> [URL]

----

This issue can be resolved when AnkiDroid users can have multiple profiles on the same device with the same app.

This is a duplicate of #2545. This 10 year old issue is FAR too long. A lot of its comment are not relevant anymore. As I don't want to delete them, I'll just copy here what is still relevant in 2025. It then will be easier for any interested contributor to read it, and for people to exchange idea about what the feature will looks like without having to read the full history.

[URL] shows how the feature works on AnkiMobile. We don't and can't use the exact same UI because we use material and not UIKit, but we certainly should have at least those features. Adding, deleting, renaming the profile. A very quick access to profile switching for users that share often. Switch with a shortcut for people on chromebook (probably reusing the shortcut of anki desktop)

I'll start with Draft of David's thought

> <details>
> 
> <summary>Anki's screen</summary>
> 
> [SCREENSHOT]
> 
> </details>
> 
> **Functionality**
> * A profile does not require an AnkiWeb account
> * A profile can be opened
>   * Each profile contains a separate `Collection`, set of `SharedPreferences` and **WebView Cookies**
> * A user will be able to add a named profile. 
>   * Preferences may be copied from another profile 
> * A user will be able to rename an existing profile
> * A user will be able to delete a profile
> * We will not implement 'Downgrade & Quit/Open Backup' here. The Deck Picker contains 'Open Backup' already, and this screen will not be used by the majority of users.
> * Widgets are ignored for now
> * A user may select the app shortcuts they want to appear
> * Profile names may contain special characters.
>   * When creating a folder, these characters are removed
> * If the user is in a private folder, the folders under `/files` are the profile
> * If the user is in a public folder, use `AnkiDroid Profiles` by default
>   * But allow a user to change the location on a per-folder basis
> 
> **Defaults**
> * The default Profile name is AnkiDroid
> * We have a 'default' profile, which will launch on open
> * The default is the last-opened profile
> * The 'open profile' may be shown on launch instead
> 
> **Unknown**
> * How do we handle 'Manage Data'
> * How do we handle the API
> 
> **Constraints**
> * The standard onboarding process should not be affected, neither will the default user experience. Profiles are an extra
> * We should not modify the navigation drawer, as this is soon to be removed
>
> **TODO:** 
> 
> * What happens when a profile is deleted?
>   * Offer to permanently delete linked collection folder + backups?
>     * [Security] if AnkiDroid is acting as a file manager, ensure you can't use this to delete an arbitrary folder
> * Can two profiles have the same name?
>   * Technically, yes, but block it  
> * AnkiDroid needs to know the current profile and load this efficiently (blocker on hot startup path)
> * Should the current profile name be visible, are there latency concerns if it's on the hot path?
> * What can go wrong? How to recover?

Brayan's answer

> > How do we handle WebView cookies
> Specifically: Shared Decks -> AnkiWeb login
> 
> Share it, I guess
> 
> > How do we handle app shortcuts
> 
> Maybe add the profile name to each one? (I have no idea if that is possible) -> Add (David), Study (Arthur)
> 
> > Profile names may contain special characters. Should the name map to a folder name?
> 
> Mimic Anki desktop behavior or allow any characters in the profile name but strip the unallowed in the folder name
> 
> > Our current folder is AnkiDroid
> 
> For app private builds, doesn't seem to be a problem
> 
> For full builds, ideally the profile should be in `AnkiDroid/profile name` but `AnkiDroid/` already has the collection. The easiest solution I see is keeping the old `AnkiDro id/` folder and if the user tries to create a new profile, default it to a new directory called `AnkiDroid profiles` or some better name (ideally one that doesn't need to be localized). For new installs, we can default to this new folder

David:

> I specifically chose `AnkiDroid` so we're not writing to the root of `com.ichi2.anki/files` in the private directory (so `AnkiDroid` can be the default profile)
> 
> For the public directory, `AnkiDroid Profiles` seems ideal

> >> How do we handle app shortcuts

> * + We want a per-profile setting to determine which icons (if any) appear
> 
> ----
> 
> * Widgets: probably 'unsupported' for now and have them tied to the current profile
> * API: probably the same
> 
> ----
> 
> I think we want to isolate the WebView cookies if at all possible

> > Widgets: probably 'unsupported' for now and have them tied to the current profile
> 
> For the add note widget, I don't suggest any work because it should deprecated when minSdk reaches Nougat and everyone can use shortcuts.
> 
> For the reviews shortcut, it needs a redesign so it can have some configurable aspect to distinct it from other instances of it (a color, icon, emoji, text, whatever).
> 
> edit: when I say redesign, I mean a whole redesign in appearance, size, etc. It doesn't need to be similar to the current one
> 
> > I think we want to isolate the WebView cookies if at all possible
> 
> Now that I thought a little bit more, I agree

> API 28+: [`WebView.setDataDirectorySuffix`]([URL]

> **Pseudocode**
> 
> A profile will be of the format:
> 
> ```kotlin
> data class ProfileData(val identifier: String, var name: String) {
>     val webViewDataDirectory get() = identifier
>     fun preferences(context: Context) = context.getSharedPreferences(
>            name = identifier,            
>            mode = getDefaultSharedPreferencesMode(),
>         )
>     fun rename(name: String) = TODO()
>     fun select() = TODO()
>     fun delete() = TODO("do we also delete data?")
>     companion object {
>          fun listAll(): List<ProfileData> { }   
>     }
> }
> ```
> 
> `identifier` must NOT contain path separators (`setDataDirectorySuffix`)
> Proposal: current unix timestamp in ms
> 
> ----
> 
> A file containing `List<ProfileData>` should exist, for use on the Profile Management screen
> 
> * It would be inefficient to store the `name` inside `ProfileData.preferences()`
>   * O(n)

>   * If an issue occurs with a profile, the name is lost
>   * But it would be very unusual to have more than 50 profiles, even as a developer
>   * architecture is a better argument than speed
> 
> Realistic options for storage of the ProfileCollection:
> 
> 1. in the current `SharedPreferences` using `StringSet` + concatenated string
>    * As we've done previously
>    * Fast
> 2. In a new `SharedPreferences`
>     * slightly faster than the above 
> 3. Jetpack Data Store
>     * Strongly Typed
>     * Async
>     * Slower
> 
> ----

# Arthur's Note:

We need for each preferences to decide whether they are shared or whether they are profile specific.

Since we already have a welcome screen that invite people to sync with ankiweb, I think we should reuse it. If the user decide to use an ankiweb account, we could suggest the email as the profile name.

I think the default user name should be "user 1" as in AnkiMobile, and not "ankidroid". It's a strange user name; I'm not ankidroid.

I don't think the folder and the profile name should be related. We had a lot of issue with file system, renaming folder is something that could go wrong and be a huge issue, and it present almost no user interest. If we want that advanced users that look at the file structure get information about which profile is being used, I guess it'd be better to have something such as a file named ProfileName.txt (using the profile name as the file name, stripped of any forbidden characater) that contains the profile name.

## Split shared collection

Since we may have user that have shared the same device for a lot of time, I think we should also allow to copy the collection. This way, if I have a deck named "Arthur's deck" and my sister have a deck named "Sister's deck" we each end up with both deck in our collection. I then can delete "sister's deck" and she can delete "Arthur's deck".
Admittedly, this is already something a user could do by exporting the collection and importing them again, or both syncing with the same ankiweb account; but it may be too complex for some users (and sync may be expensive and slow). It seems better to offer it as a native feature.

This feature would only exists on ankidroid, because it's the only place where we have a need for this feature.

issue_title: Feature Request: Sort cards by deck in browser display order
generated_review: Seriously, why can't I just sort my cards by deck name?! It's a hassle having to scroll through everything every time I open AnkiDroid. Fix this ASAP!
issue_body:
## Description
Currently, AnkiDroid's browser offers multiple sorting options including by created time, modification time, due time, interval, ease, reviews, and lapses. However, there is no option to sort cards by their deck hierarchy or deck name, which would be extremely useful for users who maintain multiple decks and want to quickly locate and organize cards by their deck location.

As shown in the screenshot, the current display order options in the card browser include:
- No sorting (faster)
- By sort field
- By created time
- By note modification time
- By card modification time
- By due time
- By interval
- By ease
- By reviews
- By lapses

[SCREENSHOT]

While users can filter by deck, they cannot sort the results by deck name alphabetically or hierarchically.

## Proposed Solution
Add a new display order option: "By deck name" that would sort cards alphabetically by their deck names. This would help users:
- Quickly identify cards from the same deck when browsing through large collections
- Organize their review based on deck hierarchy
- Better manage content across multiple decks

## Implementation Considerations
1. The sort should respect deck hierarchy (parent decks followed by child decks)
2. Alphabetical sorting within same-level decks would be ideal
3. Secondary sort criteria could be applied after deck sorting (e.g., by sort field within each deck)

## Use Cases
- Users with many decks who want to browse cards organized by their location in the deck structure
- Teachers managing multiple class decks who need to quickly find cards within specific course sections
- Language learners who organize vocabulary by topic decks and want to review related cards together

## Additional Context
This sorting option exists in the desktop version of Anki, so adding it to AnkiDroid would improve feature parity between platforms.

Title: Long Overdue Onboarding Tutorial Needed for New Users

As a new user, I found myself overwhelmed with AnkiDroid's powerful features. issue_body:
### Problem

While Anki is powerful, many first-time users of **AnkiDroid** struggle to discover key features (like syncing, scheduling, or tags). Unlike Anki Desktop or AnkiMobile, AnkiDroid currently doesn’t include any kind of tutorial, help screen, or onboarding flow. This can result in a steep learning curve or users missing out on powerful functionality.

I noticed that a similar idea has been mentioned before in Anki Desktop discussions, but this proposal focuses specifically on the Android experience.

### Proposed Solution

- Add a first-time user onboarding screen explaining core concepts (e.g. decks, sync, cards).
- Optionally include tooltips or short animations to highlight features in-app.
- Add an entry in settings to re-show the tutorial later.
- Provide links to docs or beginner videos.

### Benefits

- Better onboarding for new AnkiDroid users  
- Fewer repeated beginner questions  
- Higher retention and engagement  

### Stretch Goal

- Track usage (non-personally) to understand what features need better visibility, and adjust onboarding accordingly.

---

I’d be interested in contributing to this as a warm-up task and would love feedback. I'm a prospective GSoC 2025 student looking to get involved early.

issue_title: [BUG]: Using JS click() method on an audio button breaks subsequent <script> blocks
generated_review: Experienced an odd issue with the audio function in AnkiDroid. When using JavaScript to play an audio clip, it seems to affect any subsequent scripts within the note type, causing them not to execute properly. Specifically, I found that a red background color applied to the body persisted even when I intended to change it to blue in another script block. A bit puzzling but thought I should share for awareness.
issue_body:
Steps to reproduce:
1. Clone the Basic note type
2. On the front side of the template add the following code:
    ```
    <script>
    document.querySelector('a.replay-button').click();
    document.body.style = "background:red";
    </script>
    
    <script>
    document.body.style = "background:blue";
    </script>
    ```
3. Make a card with this note type, **putting an audio file** into the Front field
4. Open the card for review

Expected result:
 the card is displayed as blue (works this way on desktop or when the first line of the script is commented out)
AnkiDriod behavior:
 the card is displayed as red

Additional info:
1. Only subsequent `<script>` blocks are broken, the script from the same block does not break past the point where `.click()` is called (as demonstrated by the line setting background to red in the suggested minimal example)
2. Raw `<audio>` tags inside card fields, as well as fully recreated HTML for AnkiDroid's audiobutton (starting with the `<a>` tag), do **not** break anything when the `.click()` is used on them. The issue seems to be caused solely by the audio inserted via `[sound:%audiofile%]`
3. When the reviewed card is inspected with remote dev tools, the second `<script>` block appears to be completely missing from the source code
4. Replacing audio file in the Front field with text removes the issue
5. Calling `.click()` method via setTimeout allows some subsequent `<script>` block to appear on the page (the number depends on the timeout), but it seems that once the method is called, it somehow prevent insertion of `<script>` blocks on the page

issue_title: CardContentProvider.answerCard cannot correctly handle non-top cards
generated_review: I noticed an issue when trying to update the review status of certain cards using an external app. It seems that the AnkiDroid app isn't always fetching the correct scheduling state for these specific cards, leading to inconsistencies. I hope this can be addressed soon, as it's affecting my study progress.
issue_body:
### 

### 

- [x] This bug does not occur in the latest version of Anki Desktop

### 

1. An external application uses the CardContentProvider to update the review status of a card via the content://com.ichi2.anki.flashcards/schedule URI.
2. The target card, identified by NOTE_ID and CARD_ORD in the ContentValues, is not the currently active card in the AnkiDroid reviewer queue (i.e., not the topCard in the Scheduler.currentQueueState()).
3. The external app calls update on the SCHEDULE URI, providing the card identifiers and an EASE value (e.g., FlashCardsContract.ReviewInfo.EASE).
4. Buggy Behaviour: The previous implementation might incorrectly fetch the scheduling state of the current top card from the scheduler queue instead of the target card's actual state, or use a legacy answerCard method. This leads to the target card being reviewed with incorrect parameters, potentially messing up its scheduling interval.

### 

When an external application updates a card's review status via the CardContentProvider (SCHEDULE URI):
- The provider should determine if the target card matches the current top card in the scheduler's queue.
- If it matches, the provider should use the readily available CurrentQueueState from the scheduler.
- If it does not match (or the queue is empty), the provider must fetch the specific SchedulingStates for the target card.
- In either case, the provider should use the correct card and its corresponding scheduling state to call the modern Scheduler.answerCard(info: CurrentQueueState, ease: Int) method.
- This ensures the target card is always answered based on its own state and the provided ease level, resulting in the correct scheduling update.

issue_title: I want to have gesture to enter an answer that does not show the answer
generated_review:
Title: Gesture confusion with long cards

Review: I really enjoy using AnkiDroid's swipe gestures, but sometimes I encounter a problem with longer cards. When I'm trying to mark a card as 'Hard' or scrolling through, the answer unexpectedly appears. It's a bit frustrating because I don't get a chance to think about the question first. I hope there's a way to fix this so I can continue enjoying the app!
issue_body:
# The problem I want to solve
I love gestures. I use the four direction to indicate whether something is again, hard, good and easy.

My current issue is that sometime, I've a card that is longer than the screen, and I scroll, and it moves from question to answer. I didn't have the time to think about the question.
So I'd want to be able to ensure that the gesture "hard" is not interpreted as "show the answer" when on question side.

However I understand some user may love the feature of having the same gesture for showing the answer and answering. Myself, I still want to be able to have the gesture "slide up" mean "show the answer".

So, I believe that we should allow the same Binding to be used for both "show the answer" and "answer".

# The end UI

When the user add a Binding for one of the four answer action, this binding is also added to "show answer". A toast tells the user "$binding will also show the answer". 

This way, we won't have a change of behavior, but the current behavior can be modified when we want.

# Migration

As I don't want to change the behavior for anyone that already has the current feature enabled, I believe the way it should work is that we'll introduce a new key word in the preference. "binding_ANSWER_EASE4" (and similar for other numbers). We'll keep being able to read "binding_FLIP_OR_ANSWER_EASE4" from the preferences, but we won't add it in the preferences anymore.

* open settings > sync  > ankiweb account > remove account

Actual result:
* being asked to log-in to an existing account. Entering email and password
* then asking to enter the password again and type "remove"

I think that log-in seems like the reverse of what the user want. I know why it makes sense, ankiweb being independent of ankidroid, and we certainly don’t want to give the authentication key to the browser. But I’d expect it to be confusing for some users. 

I think it’d be nice to first state: "In order to delete your account, we need you first to re-authentify." Would you be okay, @dae to add a page with this string before the authentication form, so that the user know what is going on? I hope it would not require too much extra work.

Ideally, I’d also ask for a get parameter to put the address email. I think that in this case, requesting the user to tap the email address is counter productive. If they have multiple accounts, they may not know which account was used on ankidroid and may end up entering the email of another account. (Admittedly, the information was provided in the previous page, so it is easy to find again)

Of course, I’d also appreciate if there were translation of this page, to be certain the user know what they are doing. What "remove" mean. But I guess this is far more complex and a problem for the entire ankiweb

issue_title: AnkiDroid Editor shows image fields as raw HTML when field is wrapped in layout containers (Editor-only WebView rendering bug)
generated_review:
Title: Image problem in AnkiDroid Editor

---

Dear developers, I am using AnkiDroid 2.23.1 on my phone, and I found a strange issue while creating new notes. When I wrap an image field within some layout containers using CSS properties like position, absolute, or z-index, the image doesn't show up properly in the editor. Instead, it presents the raw HTML code. This happens only in the editor; preview, learning mode, and Anki Desktop work fine. I hope you can fix this issue soon, so I can make beautiful and organized decks effectively. Thank you!
issue_body:
--- ## **Title** **AnkiDroid Editor shows image fields as raw HTML when field is wrapped in layout containers (Editor-only WebView rendering bug)** --- ## **Summary** In **AnkiDroid 2.23.1**, image fields are **not rendered as images in the Editor** when the field is wrapped inside a container that applies layout-relevant CSS (e.g. `position`, `absolute`, `z-index`). Instead, the Editor displays the **raw HTML source** (e.g. ``). The **same note type renders correctly** in: * AnkiDroid **Learning mode** * AnkiDroid **Preview** * **Anki Desktop** (Editor, Preview, Learning) This indicates an **Editor-only WebView rendering fallback**, not a template error. --- ## **Environment** **Anki Desktop (authoring):** * Version: 25.02.4 (a5c33ad0) * Python: 3.9.18 * Qt: 6.6.2 * PyQt: 6.6.1 **AnkiDroid:** * App Version: 2.23.1 * Backend: 0.1.62-anki25.09.2 * Android Version: 16 (SDK 36) * Device: Samsung SM-S916B * ProductFlavor: play * FSRS: 5.1.0 (disabled) **Android System WebView:** * Chrome: 143.0.7499.35 * User Agent: `Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 16; SM-S916B Build/BP2A.250605.031.A3; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/143.0.7499.35 Mobile Safari/537.36` --- ## **Use Case / Context** The note type is used for **Backgammon position analysis**. * Front side: an image with **two white overlay masks** * Left overlay: 32% width * Bottom overlay: 13% height * Back side: the same image **without overlays**, plus statistics and tag sorting. Overlays must exist in **learning mode**. No editor-specific behavior is intended. --- ## **Expected Behavior** In the **AnkiDroid Editor**, image fields (e.g. `{{Vorderseite}}`) should render as images, consistent with: * Anki Desktop Editor * AnkiDroid Preview * AnkiDroid Learning mode --- ## **Actual Behavior** In the **AnkiDroid Editor only**: * The image is **not rendered** * The editor displays the **raw HTML source**, e.g.: ```html ``` This happens **only** when: * the image field is placed inside a container (`div`) * and that container (or its parents) applies layout CSS such as `position`, `absolute`, or `z-index` Learning mode and Preview work correctly. --- ## **Minimal Reproduction** ### **Front Template (simplified)** ```html
{{Vorderseite}}
``` ### **CSS** ```css .front-container { position: relative; } .overlay-left { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 32%; height: 100%; background: white; z-index: 20; } .overlay-bottom { position: absolute; bottom: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 13%; background: white; z-index: 20; } img { width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; } ``` --- ## **Key Observations** * ✔ Works in **Anki Desktop Editor** * ✔ Works in **AnkiDroid Preview** * ✔ Works in **AnkiDroid Learning mode** * ❌ Fails only in **AnkiDroid Editor** * ❌ Editor falls back to **plain-text rendering** Removing the container or overlay CSS restores image rendering in the editor but breaks the required learning layout. --- ## **Tested and Rejected Workarounds** All of the following were tested and **did not resolve the issue**: * `display: contents` * JavaScript DOM relocation after load * Negative margins * Editor-specific CSS selectors (e.g. `[contenteditable="true"]`) * Helper fields * Conditional HTML * Moving overlays outside the field via JavaScript Conclusion: **The Editor WebView disables media rendering when layout-affecting CSS influences the field DOM.** --- ## **Conclusion** This appears to be a **native AnkiDroid Editor WebView bug**, not a template issue. The Editor uses a different rendering path than Preview/Learning and switches to a **plain-text fallback** when encountering image fields inside layout-influenced containers. A fix would require changes in: * the Editor WebView rendering logic, or * how layout-affected fields are handled in the editor context. --- ## **Impact** This affects any advanced note type using: * image overlays * masking * partial occlusion * structured image layouts The issue scales poorly for large collections (5,000+ notes), where per-note workarounds are not feasible. --- **This report is fully reproducible and intentionally minimal.**

generated_review:
Title: Confused with home screen on AnkiDroid

issue_body:
Hi! I’m **Ana Ferreira**, a Master's student in Computer Science.

As part of my research on mobile accessibility, I am analyzing open-source Android applications to help identify and correct accessibility barriers so users can utilize assistive technologies (like TalkBack) more effectively.

I’ve been exploring **AnkiDroid** and found a specific issue on the main screen, so I wanted to propose a fix.

### 1. The Issue

On the **Home Screen (Empty Collection state)**, the **Add Deck FAB** presents the following behavior:

- **Current behavior:** The element lacks a descriptive text label. TalkBack announces it simply as "Unlabelled" (or reads the icon name without context), violating WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
- **Impact:** Users relying on screen readers cannot distinguish this control or understand its function immediately.

### 2. Proposed Solution

To fix this, I suggest adding an `android:contentDescription` to the element in the XML layout.

**Code snippet / XML suggestion:**

```xml
<ImageButton
    ...
    android:contentDescription="@string/action_description" />
```
*(Note: We should use an existing string resource or create a new one to support localization)*

I have identified **3** other categories of accessibility improvements for the AnkiDroid Home Screen.

**To avoid spamming your notification feed, how would you prefer I submit these?**

- [ ]  **Option A:** List them all here in this issue (I can update the comment below).
- [ ]  **Option B:** Open separate issues for each specific problem.

I can provide detailed fixes for these upon request.

Please let me know your preference, and I will proceed accordingly.

issue_title: Drawing attachment (note editor) produces jagged strokes compared to reviewer whiteboard
generated_review: Jagged lines in the drawing feature make it difficult to study effectively.
issue_body:
### 

### 

- [x] This bug does not occur in the latest version of Anki Desktop

### 

1. Open the note editor (add or edit a card)
2. Tap the paperclip/attachment icon
3. Choose **Drawing**
4. Draw strokes at normal-to-fast writing speed
5. Observe jagged, angular line segments

**For comparison:**

6. Open the reviewer and enable the **whiteboard overlay**
7. Draw strokes at the same speed
8. Observe that strokes are noticeably smoother

### 

The drawing attachment should produce smooth strokes comparable to the reviewer whiteboard, since both serve as drawing surfaces.

Looking at the code, `Whiteboard.kt` (reviewer) already uses `quadTo()` with Bézier interpolation and processes historical touch events via `MotionEvent.getHistoricalX/Y()`. However, `WhiteboardView.kt` (used by `DrawingFragment` for the drawing attachment) only uses `lineTo()` and does not process historical touch events.

### Debug info

```text
Hier deine eigene Debug-Info einfügen:
AnkiDroid → Settings → About → ganz unten → "Copy debug info"
```

### (Optional) Anything else you want to share?

## Code comparison

**Reviewer whiteboard (`Whiteboard.kt`) — smooth strokes:**
- Uses `path.quadTo()` with midpoint interpolation
- Processes `event.getHistoricalX/Y()` for higher point density
- Has a `drawAlong()` method

**Drawing attachment (`WhiteboardView.kt`) — jagged strokes:**
```kotlin
// ACTION_MOVE handler only uses lineTo():
currentPath.lineTo(touchX, touchY)
```

## Possible fix

Apply the same pattern from `Whiteboard.kt` to `WhiteboardView.kt`:
```kotlin
for (i in 0 until event.historySize) {
    val hx = event.getHistoricalX(i)
    val hy = event.getHistoricalY(i)
    currentPath.quadTo(lastX, lastY, (hx + lastX) / 2f, (hy + lastY) / 2f)
    lastX = hx
    lastY = hy
}
currentPath.quadTo(lastX, lastY, (touchX + lastX) / 2f, (touchY + lastY) / 2f)
lastX = touchX
lastY = touchY
```

> **Note:** I have not tested this change. It would need to be verified that it doesn't introduce regressions with the eraser, undo/redo, or path operations.

Observed on Onyx Boox Note 4C, but should be reproducible on any device at sufficient drawing speed.

---

issue_title: Note editor preview can reopen the wrong cloze when cloze numbers are non-consecutive
generated_review: Experienced an issue with the note editor preview where it incorrectly switches to another cloze when I have non-consecutive cloze ord numbers. This was particularly noticeable when I edited the note to refresh the preview.
issue_body:
I noticed a state issue in the note editor preview for cloze notes.

Repro:
1. Open a cloze note in the note editor.
2. Use non-consecutive cloze ords, for example `c4`, `c7`, `c9`.
3. Open the preview and switch to one of the later cloze tabs.
4. Edit the note so the preview refreshes.

Expected:
The preview should stay on the selected cloze.

Actual:
The preview can reopen on a different cloze.

The issue looks to be in `TemplatePreviewerViewModel.getSafeClozeOrd()`. The current logic coerces `ordFlow.value` against the size of the cloze ord list, which treats the ord like a tab index. That breaks once the cloze ords are sparse.

If this looks reasonable, I can put together a fix.
reason: The review accurately captures the issue with the note editor preview and describes the user-facing symptom clearly.

issue_title: Fix precision issues while formatting amounts
generated_review: Brave Browser, it seems there's an inconsistency with the formatting of amounts, particularly small ones. For instance, a balance such as 0.000318182 ETH is shown as 0.0001 ETH which may lead to loss of precision. I hope this can be addressed for improved user experience.
issue_body:
**User report:** https://twitter.com/jim74255/status/1491103364746452994

We have no consistent way of formatting balances/amounts with rounding. Here are two most common issues we're facing with amount values:
1. very small amounts are rounded incorrectly, resulting in loss of precision.
  For example, `0.000318182 ETH` will be formatted as `0.0001 ETH`.
2. some amount values should never be rounded, notably anything that user will refer to before signing a transaction.
  For example, values seen in the transaction confirmation screen.
During an internal brainstorming, we considered not rounding amounts at all, but this will result in poor UX. This issue is about bringing contextual precision to amounts by introducing better formatting tools.
reason: The review accurately captures the issue of inconsistent formatting of small amounts and the potential loss of precision.

issue_title: Profiles with a lot of cookies are hanging just after downloading the main frame document
generated_review: Brave browser frequently stalls on heavily-cookied websites.
issue_body:
Profile with a lot of cookies will load news.ycombinator.com in ~850ms. Different user profile _in the same running browser instance_ will get ~250ms. There seems to be a hang in the browser process just after the first document request and before the resource requests.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/741836/153504613-0e81fe8b-4ad8-4a48-aa0b-111cae911976.png)


After diving in to the issue where with a profile that has a lot of cookies, the hang seems to be in `RenderFrameHostImpl::CommitNavigation`
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/741836/153504686-96c8987c-2b1d-431c-8721-e07fbb56197f.png)

In fact, the hang is here: https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/d1924a490f88d7cf2e952007029520cfba5b13c9/content/browser/renderer_host/render_frame_host_impl.cc#L10935
```
        partition->OpenLocalStorageForProcess(
            process_id, commit_params->storage_key,
            storage_info->local_storage_area.InitWithNewPipeAndPassReceiver());
```

This code path is only run if the feature flag `NavigationThreadingOptimizations` is enabled, which it is by default in the code. However, at least for desktop, Chrome seems to have disabled it.

I am unsure if this affects Android.

issue_title: Dropped transactions are never retired in our Wallet
generated_review: Frustrated with Brave Wallet! Transactions keep dropping and I'm losing money! Need a fix ASAP, this is unacceptable.
issue_body:
During a Zoom call with a user here:
https://community.brave.com/t/unable-to-send-funds-out-of-brave-wallet/335479/20

We seen that he had a transaction in his transaction list that was "Pending" but on Etherscan it was "Dropped".  
Our UI keeps it at Pending because it never gets Confirmed. 
A dropped transaction can happen when the fees are too low and miners need room in their mempool. They will never be re-picked up unless the transaction is re-broadcast. 
https://info.etherscan.com/transaction-dropped-replaced/

This suggests we should have a way to re-broadcast a transaction.  When that option is selected, our panel should also have an in UI message that gas fees are configured too low and will likely be dropped.  That message can be given even for new transactions when a user manually edits their gas fees to something that doesn't make sense vs the current gas values.  

Also we should surface the pending transactions more because they can be hard to find for users.  All future transactions will remain pending if one is pending because the nonce must be sequential. E.g. something like if there's a new transaction being made and there's an old pending one older than a day, we should warn and ask if the user would like to remove that transaction locally.
reason: Review captures frustration with dropped transactions but lacks detail on the underlying issue of transaction management.

issue_title: Fix monthly/weekly wallet P3A
issue_labels: [Label(name="bug"), Label(name="QA Pass-Win64"), Label(name="QA/Yes"), Label(name="release-notes/exclude"), Label(name="feature/wallet"), Label(name="OS/Android"), Label(name="QA Pass - Android Tab"), Label(name="OS/Desktop")]
generated_review: Recently, I noticed an inconsistency with my wallet usage data on the app. It seems that there have been instances where the app marks my wallet as unused during the middle of a month, even though I was actively using it. Consequently, this affects my average usage calculation as it seems to double count some periods. I hope this issue can be addressed, as it's making my data analysis challenging.
issue_body:
<!-- Have you searched for similar issues? Before submitting this issue, please check the open issues and add a note before logging a new issue. 

PLEASE USE THE TEMPLATE BELOW TO PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT THE ISSUE. 
INSUFFICIENT INFO WILL GET THE ISSUE CLOSED. IT WILL ONLY BE REOPENED AFTER SUFFICIENT INFO IS PROVIDED-->

## Description 
The current P3A questions for wallet usage (`Brave.Wallet.UsageDaily`, `Brave.Wallet.UsageWeekly`, `Brave.Wallet.UsageMonthly`) must be replaced with new questions: `Brave.Wallet.UsageMonthly.2` and `Brave.Wallet.UsageDaysInWeek`.

`UsageMonthly` is set to true if the wallet has been used in the current month. If the user opens the wallet for the first time in the middle of the month, P3A could transmit two weeks of `UsageMonthly=0` reports and two weeks of `UsageMonthly=1` reports. This makes it difficult to approximate MAU, if MAU is calculated by dividing the total amount of `UsageMonthly=1` reports by four weeks. `Brave.Wallet.UsageMonthly.2` will be set to true if the wallet has been used in the previous month. This will ensure four weeks of P3A reports with the same value.

`UsageDaily` is set to true if the wallet has been used during the current day. Since P3A reports are sent once per week, only wallet usages during the day of the P3A report will be reported. `Brave.Wallet.UsageDaysInWeek` will report the number of days the wallet has been used within the past 7 days. Since WAU can be inferred by this new question, `UsageWeekly` can be removed. Reports for this question will not be sent less than one week from the first run of the browser.

Building from source.

issue_title: Investigate and fix Arbitrum transaction failures
issue_labels: [Label(name="bug"), Label(name="QA Pass-Linux"), Label(name="priority/P2"), Label(name="QA/Yes"), Label(name="release-notes/include"), Label(name="feature/wallet"), Label(name="OS/Android"), Label(name="OS/Desktop")]
generated_review: Experienced repeated transaction failures while using the Brave app for Arbitrum transactions. The app seems to be defaulting to a lower gas limit, resulting in failed transactions that don't provide clear error messages. I hope this can be addressed soon as it's preventing me from making essential transactions.
issue_body: ## User reports * https://community.brave.com/t/unable-to-send-eth-arbitrum-chain/317080/10 * https://community.brave.com/t/unable-to-send-funds-out-of-brave-wallet/335479/21 * https://community.brave.com/t/brave-wallet-not-allowing-0-gas-price-on-arbitrum-test-network/308777/13 ## Investigation ### Finding 1 Default gas limit for simple `AETH` transfers is always **`21000`**. 🔴 Gas limit on Arbitrum mainnet is typically **`500,000`**. See [example](https://arbiscan.io/tx/0x6170cee694eadfffe654935a49dbf29c597133586beae6ed2110fbc428cb5d5e). ### Finding 2 Unsuspecting users who publish transactions with **`21000`** gas, do NOT get helpful error messages from the Arbitrum client. They get **not enough funds for gas** instead of something like "gas limit not enough". ### Finding 3 The `eth_estimateGas` RPC method behaves a bit differently compared to Ethereum's JSON-RPC spec. Example: **With the `TAG` param ("latest"):** ``` $ curl -s https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_estimateGas","params":[{"from":"0xa92D461a9a988A7f11ec285d39783A637Fdd6ba4","to":"0xbc5d6cd6f7225bfCCc58F7B75AaeB641ECCD5419","value":"0xe8d4a51000"}, "latest"]}' | jq { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "error": { "code": -32602, "message": "too many arguments, want at most 1" } } ``` **Without the `TAG` param:** ``` curl -s https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_estimateGas","params":[{"from":"0xa92D461a9a988A7f11ec285d39783A637Fdd6ba4","to":"0xbc5d6cd6f7225bfCCc58F7B75AaeB641ECCD5419","value":"0xe8d4a51000"}]}' | jq { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": "0x7425c" } ``` 🔴 `TAG` is an optional parameter. See [docs](https://docs.alchemy.com/alchemy/apis/arbitrum#eth_estimategas). Didn't find any usage of `TAG` in their node's source code: https://github.com/OffchainLabs/arbitrum/blob/c1624cd0efdeaf6bb1d3c19ba402082cf5bba4a0/packages/arb-rpc-node/web3/ethclient.go#L124-L138
reason: The review accurately captures the issue of transaction failures due to low gas limits and the lack of clear error messages.

issue_title: Refactor Brave Ads singletons to use function-local static of type `base::NoDestructor<T>` instead where appropriate

issue_body:
Singletons make it hard to determine the lifetime of an object, which can lead to buggy code and spurious crashes.

Instead of adding another singleton into the mix, try to identify either:
   a) An existing singleton that can manage your object's lifetime
   b) Locations where you can deterministically create the object and pass
      into other objects

If you absolutely need a singleton, please keep them as trivial as possible and ideally a leaf dependency. Singletons get problematic when they attempt to do too much in their destructor or have circular dependencies.

See https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:base/memory/singleton.h

issue_title: Wallet: Localhost Network Chain Id and Port are Hardcoded, Not Shown in UI
generated_review: Brave Wallet seems to have a persistent localhost network that's hardcoded, making it challenging to test dApps running on different ports. This network isn't adjustable through the UI, which can be inconvenient for developers like myself.
issue_body:
## Description 

As a Web3 dApp developer, I'm testing multiple applications against Brave's native wallet. These applications are running locally in Truffle and Hardhat "sandbox" chains, running on various ports, typically 8545 or 9545.

The Brave wallet has a hardcoded "Localhost" network, which uses Ganache's RPC URI: `http://localhost:7545/`, as well as the standard "dev" chainId: `1337`. 

This is not configurable in the UI, and is actually hardcoded in [components/brave_wallet/browser/brave_wallet_utils.cc](https://github.com/brave/brave-core/blob/5b576ef6125c629d3c876f335a9927f7ca5c208d/components/brave_wallet/browser/brave_wallet_utils.cc#L75):

```
const char kGanacheLocalhostURL[] = "http://localhost:7545/";
```

As this network does not exist in [`brave://settings/wallet/networks`](brave://settings/wallet/networks), it was difficult to determine the port it was hardcoded with, fortunately Brave is open source. Still makes for a less optimal developer experience.

## Steps to Reproduce
<!--Please add a series of steps to reproduce the issue-->

   1. Run a development Web3 stack locally, on a port other than 7545, which uses chain id `1337`.
   2. Attempt to add a new network to Brave's networks, using chain id `1337`.


## Actual result:
1. An error will appear: `This network is already added.` (As chain ids must be unique to RPC addresses)

## Expected result:
1. Preferably the Wallet UI should show pre-populated networks' configurations (Chain Ids, RPC URLs, etc.), as MetaMask does, in the Wallet Settings UI.
2. Non-production/Development/Testnets should have editable RPC urls, including port.

## Reproduces how often: 
Easily reproduced, using settings to add a non-port 7545 network with chain id `1337`.

* Auto updates across systems (including on Linux where that feature is missing)
* Installation on systems where the user can only write to $HOME
* Portable installations (e.g. on pendrives)

Tor Browser does this in their own way (at least on Linux). You can install the package system-wide, as an administrator, but when a user starts the browser, it actually installs itself in $HOME and runs/auto-updates from there. The one wrinkle I see with this approach is the ownership of the files installed in $HOME - the user can modify any of them. This means they can update, but it also opens up some potential security risks.

Relevant [Slack thread](https://bravesoftware.slack.com/archives/CG7GV6M7Z/p1638918729027500?thread_ts=1638897702.020100&cid=CG7GV6M7Z).

Title: Frustrating Wallet Issues with Brave Browser

Dear Developers, I've encountered an unusual problem with the wallet feature on Brave. Recently, I tried to make a transaction and the app unexpectedly froze while processing the amount. It seems like there's an issue with the precision bits in the wallet, causing discrepancies in calculations.

issue_body:
We will have boost multiprecision in chromium 100 because in clang 15, it remove `_BitInt(256)` support
However, boost's int256_t uses 256 precision bits and an extra sign bit instead of 255 precision bits and a sign bit
Currently we manually restrict the its max and min value but it doesn't prevent future code from misusing it so it is better to have checked class like `CheckedNumeric` in `base/numerics/checked_math.h`

issue_title: docs(adr): refine api/impl split into api/internal
generated_review:
Title: Long overdue organizational improvement needed

After using K-9 Mail for some time now, I've noticed that the internal workings of the app feel a bit disorganized. For instance, the API and impl splits don't seem to clearly define the boundaries between different features and the core areas. This has led to occasional confusion when trying to understand how certain aspects of the app function.

I believe the developers should consider refining the module and package structure, as suggested in ticket #<redacted>, by renaming 'impl' to 'internal', keeping 'api' as the public contract surface, and enforcing clear dependencies between these two categories. This would greatly improve the overall organization and
issue_body:
While the api/impl split is already a great step into better project organization it doesn't reflect our initial intention to split between code that is used and shared accross features and code that implements a specific feature but should not be visible to other parts of the app.

We propose clarifying and formalizing the module and package structure across Thunderbird for Android by:

* Renaming all `impl` modules to `internal` to clearly mark them as private implementation details.
* Keeping `api` modules as the only public contract surface between features and core areas.
* Establishing consistent package naming:
  * `api` modules use direct feature/core packages
  * `internal` modules mirror them under `.internal` package suffix.
* Enforcing dependency rules so only `api` modules may be referenced across areas; `internal` modules are only used by composition modules (`:app-common`, `:app-k9mail`, `:app-thunderbird`).
* Adding build checks to prevent accidental dependencies on `internal` modules.

## Tasks

- [x] Update documentation
- [ ] Build automatic checks
reason: The review accurately captures the issue of disorganization in the app's API and impl structure, reflecting the proposed changes.

issue_title: Security: Stored credentials can be extracted without master password via NSS API
generated_review: K-9 Mail seems to have a serious security concern: if you don't set a primary password, anyone on your device could potentially access your email accounts' login details. This issue lies within the app's use of NSS API, allowing decryption of stored passwords even without the master password.
issue_body:
## Summary

Thunderbird (and its underlying Mozilla credential storage) allows any local process to extract all stored email passwords in plaintext when no Primary/Master Password is configured — which is the **default** state.

## The Problem

Mozilla's credential storage (`logins.json` + `key4.db`) uses NSS (Network Security Services) to encrypt stored passwords. However, when no Primary Password is set (the default), the encryption key in `key4.db` is protected by an empty string. This means:

1. Any application running under the same user account can load `nss3.dll` / `libnss3.so`
2. Call `NSS_Init()` with the profile path
3. Verify the empty master password via `PK11_CheckUserPassword(slot, "")`
4. Decrypt **all** stored credentials via `PK11SDR_Decrypt()`

This requires **no privilege escalation**, no exploitation of any vulnerability — just standard API calls to Mozilla's own libraries.

## Proof of Concept

```python
import ctypes, json, os, base64

nss3 = ctypes.CDLL('nss3.dll')  # or libnss3.so
nss3.NSS_Init(profile_path.encode())

slot = nss3.PK11_GetInternalKeySlot()
nss3.PK11_CheckUserPassword(slot, b'')  # Returns 0 = success

# Decrypt any entry from logins.json
nss3.PK11SDR_Decrypt(encrypted_input, decrypted_output, None)
# → plaintext password
```

Full working implementation exists at [firefox_decrypt]([URL]

## Impact

- **All stored email credentials** (IMAP, POP3, SMTP passwords) are extractable
- **OAuth2 tokens** for services like Gmail are also stored and extractable
- Any malware, rogue browser extension, or script running as the user can silently harvest all credentials
- Users are **not warned** that their passwords are effectively stored in plaintext equivalent

## Suggested Mitigations

1. **Require Primary Password on first credential save** — Don't make it optional with an easy-to-dismiss prompt
2. **OS keychain integration** — Use Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service instead of NSS's own key storage. These are protected by the OS login session and are not trivially accessible via API
3. **Warning indicator** — Show a persistent security warning in the account settings when credentials are stored without a Primary Password
4. **Restrict NSS access** — Consider sandboxing or access control on the profile directory to prevent other processes from loading the key database

## Environment

- Thunderbird ESR (Desktop, Windows 11)
- Default configuration, no Primary Password set
- NSS credential storage with `encType: 1` (3DES-CBC / AES-256-CBC via PBES2)

## References

- [firefox_decrypt]([URL] — Demonstrates this exact extraction
- [Mozilla Wiki: NSS]([URL]
- This applies equally to Firefox, Thunderbird Desktop, and Thunderbird Android if the same credential storage model is used
reason: The review accurately captures the security concern regarding stored credentials and the implications of not using a master password.

- [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App

Thunderbird for Android

### App version

16.1

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

Android 15, CalyxOS 6.10.20

### Device model

FP4

1. Open/trigger a mail to someone via link e.g. mailto or another app via intent.
2. When composing, the dark mode switches, e.g. because of low battery and you plug power in or out (the usual use case that causes many annoyances in apps)

Video: 

[URL]

You can see quite well at the keyboard when the dark mode switches.

Counter-example when composing a ail manually (without intend/mailto target aka step 1):

[URL]

Do not duplicate mail. 

Now the sender mail is duplicated in the sender field.

issue_title: [Autodiscovery] Change ConnectionSettingsDiscovery interface
generated_review: Tried setting up a new email account on K-9 Mail and it didn't work correctly. It seems to be missing some settings needed for connection. Hope the developers fix this soon so I can access my emails again.
issue_body:
We need to make some changes to the `ConnectionSettingsDiscovery` interface to be able to make optimal use of the functionality provided by `SrvServiceDiscovery`.

The `ProvidersXmlDiscovery` autodiscovery method either gives us a complete set of server settings (exactly one of each incoming and outgoing server settings) or it doesn't. With `ThunderbirdDiscovery` that's not necessarily true, but it probably is in practice. But with `SrvServiceDiscovery` there's a real chance we could get any combination of one, none, or multiple server settings for both incoming and outgoing server. This is fine and we want to make use of all the information we can get in order be able to automatically set up an account. For the whole plan see issue #4721.

**Input**: When a `ConnectionSettingsDiscovery` implementation is used in a later stage, we might already have working server settings for either the incoming or outgoing server, and are only looking for settings for the missing server. So there should be a way to let the `ConnectionSettingsDiscovery` instance know which type of server settings it should look for (incoming, outgoing, or incoming + outgoing).

**Output**: We want to support situations where a discovery mechanism returns more than one server setting candidate for each server type (incoming, outgoing). We also want to support getting server settings candidates for only one server type. With `SrvServiceDiscovery` (and maybe other methods in the future) we need to distinguish between trusted and untrusted server settings. Where trusted settings are ones we can use to automatically set up an account. Untrusted server settings will only be used after the user has confirmed it's okay to do so. Since the `ServerSettings` class we currently use is also used elsewhere, I suggest creating a new class that is similar but specific to the autodiscovery phase.

With `ConnectionSettingsDiscovery` changed, we can update `SrvServiceDiscovery` to expose all the information it collected. Whether or not settings from DNS can be trusted should be determined by either
a) are the SRV records signed via DNSSEC
b) is the server's host name identical to the email domain or a sub domain of it, e.g. we trust mail.domain.example as incoming or outgoing server for user@domain.example.

This is a sub task of #4721

issue_title: Run a foreground service during mail checks initiated by the user
generated_review: K-9 Mail often interrupts syncing when I manually trigger a check and then navigate away from the app. It's frustrating to see notifications lingering after the actual sync has been halted (similar to issue #4747). A solution would be great if the app could consistently run as a foreground service for these user-initiated checks.
issue_body:
When running periodic mail checks WorkManager makes sure the system knows K-9 Mail is currently doing work in the background and shouldn't be killed. 
When the user triggers a folder/account sync in the UI and then closes the Activity the system currently has no way of knowing that K-9 Mail is still doing work in the background and shouldn't be killed. This could lead to the sync being interrupted but the sync notification remaining visible (and animated) until the next sync successfully completes and removes the notification (see #4747).

The easiest way to fix this is to always start a foreground service for user-initiated mail checks. This means always showing the sync notification even when not enabled by the user (we should probably get rid of the setting then).

Right now we show and hide the sync notification for each individual folder. We probably need to change this to start the foreground service once, perform all folder/account syncs currently queued up, and then stop the service.

issue_title: URLs in reopened drafts are bracket expanded not delimited (recursively)
generated_review: I've noticed an issue with URLs in my drafts. When I reopen them, the URLs get expanded in brackets instead of being delimited. It seems like this happens recursively too, making the links difficult to read and use. I hope this can be fixed for better usability.
issue_body:
URLs in drafts are left as written or is delimited once according to common practice and recommendations ([RFC 3986, app. C]([URL]

The recommendation and long standing practice (tracing back to an [appendix of W3C's URL specification from 1994]([URL] which the RFC builds upon) is to **delimit** URLs using angle brackets to allow a somewhat consistent interpretation (introduces some robustness to especially added line breaks).


Every URL present in a draft is expanded, not delimited, with a space and itself in angle brackets when it is reopened for editing. Such that fx. `[URL] becomes `[URL] <[URL]

The expansion is even recursive, so when reopening a saved draft for the second time this occurs again for both the original URL and the URL in brackets such that fx. `[URL] <[URL] becomes `[URL] <[URL] <[URL] <[URL] and this will continue.

This seems to me to be a misunderstanding trying to provide a rendered representative text for an URL, like the anchor text of a HTML anchor or a Markdown hyperlink. A bit like Markdown's ["autolink" which uses angle brackets]([URL] as a shortcut to creating HTML hyperlinks with the URL as duplicate anchor text in the rendering. However, I think K9 is not intended to do any interpreting of the text here. And I'll be surprised if this has has anything to do with the IMAP store (gmail).

As a side note, it also looks like [Wordpress has been discussing the use of angle brackets in links being sent, and they lost]([URL]

issue_title: Remove POP3 support
generated_review: Unfortunately, I've been using K-9 Mail for years, but recent updates have caused issues with my POP3 accounts. Instead of deleting messages after they're downloaded, it now behaves like an IMAP client, which isn't what I need. Please reconsider this change or provide a setting to toggle back to the original behavior.
issue_body:
Remove support for the POP3 protocol.

K-9 Mail never supported POP3's "download then delete from server" model. The app tries to treat POP3 accounts similar to IMAP where we download copies of messages but treat the server as single source of truth. Some settings exist to weaken that model, but the goal of #4970 is to get rid of these, too.

The hardest part about the removal is a deprecation strategy. We'll have to inform users that support for POP3 is going away before we actually remove it. They should have plenty of time to prepare moving to another protocol or another email client. I propose we show a non-dismissable info message above the message list. Clicking it could lead to a blog post with more information on the topic.

I don't want us to automatically delete user data. So once POP3 support is removed I propose we convert remaining POP3 accounts to read-only accounts. Users will still be able to view messages. They won't be able to copy, move, delete, or compose new messages from that account.

*This is part of the effort to [remove support for local messages]([URL]
reason: The review correctly identifies issues with POP3 accounts but does not mention the proposed deprecation strategy or user notification.

issue_title: Notification rules
generated_review:
Title: Wish for More Customizable Notification Rules

Description: K-9 Mail is a fantastic email app, but I find myself wanting more flexibility in setting notification rules. It would be great if we could implement a customizable rules-based system instead of relying on the current specific case options. This could allow for more nuanced notifications that better suit my preferences. Thanks for the excellent work!
issue_body:
Not all emails are equally important and deserve a notification. Right now K-9 Mail offers the following options:
- never create a notification for new messages
- only notify for messages from contacts
- don't show notifications for messages where the sender address is one of your account's identities
- only notify for messages in certain folders (using the clunky folder class mechanism)
- don't notify during "quiet time"

Often more flexibility would be nice. But I don't want to keep adding special cases. Instead I'd like us to have a generic rules-based system for deciding whether or not to create a notification.

A notification rule should have the following properties:
- **description/comment**: so users remember what the rule was all about
- **enabled state**: sometime you want to disable rules without deleting them
- **action**: the action that should be performed when the rule matches
  - *mute*: don't create a notification
  - *notification_channel*: create a notification using a particular notification channel; that way you can have different notification sounds, vibration on/off, etc
  - … maybe more in the future
- **action_extra**: argument for the 'action' method, e.g. the ID of the notification channel
- potentially multiple **clauses**: a rule matches when all clauses match
  - **property**: which property of the message is used for matching (e.g. sender, subject, body, header)
  - **property_extra**: free-form text to further describe the property, e.g. a particular header name
  - **match**: how to match the property (e.g. equals, contains, starts-with, etc.)
  - **match_extra**: free-form text to provide the argument for the 'match' method

We still want dedicated user interfaces for certain features, e.g. mute sender, mute thread/conversation. But we'll also want a user interface that gives access to all properties of a notification rule.


### Examples

#### Separate notification channel for company-internal emails
```
clause:
  property: sender
  match: matches
  match_extra: *@company.example
action: notification_channel
action_extra: company
```

#### High priority messages
```
clause:
  property: header
  property_extra: X-Priority
  match: equals
  match_extra: 1
action: notification_channel
action_extra: important
```

#### High priority messages from company-internal senders
```
clause:
  property: sender
  match: matches
  match_extra: *@company.example
clause:
  property: header
  property_extra: X-Priority
  match: equals
  match_extra: 1
action: notification_channel
action_extra: important
```

#### Mute sender
```
clause:
  property: sender
  match: equals
  match_extra: annoying-user@domain.example
action: mute
```

#### Mute mailing lists
```
clause:
  property: header
  property_extra: List-Id
  match: exists
action: mute
```

#### Mute particular thread
```
clause:
  property: header
  property_extra: References
  match: contains
  match_extra: <messageid@domain.example>
action: mute
```

### Implementation notes

- Notification rules should be per account (per folder?)
- Create dedicated database tables for notification rules
- Add support for importing/exporting notification rules
reason: The review accurately captures the desire for more customizable notification rules and reflects the key user-facing symptom.

issue_title: Only hide attachment boxes for images that are actually displayed inline
generated_review:
Title: Frustrating image attachment issue in K-9 Mail

Description: Recently, I encountered a problem while viewing emails with multiple attachments. When an email contains images referenced in plain text format, which are usually displayed as inline images, K-9 Mail wrongly hides them. This leaves me unable to view certain attachments, especially on mailing lists where the HTML part is stripped. What I expect is for K-9 Mail to support displaying images in plain text format and only hide those not directly referenced within the HTML email body. Please fix this issue in the next update so I can easily manage all my email attachments. Thank you!
issue_body:
Currently we hide attachments with a `Content-Disposition` value of `inline` and a `Content-Type` value matching `image/*`. Most of the time these are inline images referenced in a `text/html` part. But we should check to make sure that's actually the case. Otherwise users won't be able to access attachments that are not referenced in the `text/html` part. 

I noticed this happening on a mailing list where the `text/html` part was stripped. The `text/plain` part does reference the images using `[cid:…]`. But displaying images in `text/plain` parts is not something K-9 Mail supports right now.

See `AttachmentInfoExtractor.extractAttachmentInfo()`.
reason: The review accurately describes the issue with hidden image attachments and provides a clear user expectation.

issue_title: Neither list of mails nor view of individual mails show sender address or domain, makes phishing possible

Title: Missing essential email details causing potential security concerns

Description: Recently encountered a phishing attempt where the sender's actual email domain was hidden on K-9 Mail v5.732. This oversight makes it difficult to distinguish legitimate emails from fraudulent ones, as the sender's domain isn't displayed alongside the name and subject line. issue_body:
An organization was recently subject of a phishing attack were mails were send to many employees. The mail claimed to come from a high-level corporate officer. Let's call him Big Boss with his regular mail address of big.boss@corp.com. The authors of the phishing mail were aware of the corporate officer's name and sent the mail in his name, but with some randomly generate mail address: Big Boss <abc123@google.com>

When opening the mail for reading, still only claimed sender name, subject, mail body and other information is shown, but not the sender's mail address or at least the domain of the email address ('corp.com' vs 'google.com'). A well-crafted phishing mail cannot be discerned from a valid email of the real sender, despite that *it would be really easy to see in this case if the sender's mail address would be visible*.
I know that there is a 'show headers' function which allows you to inspect the underlying data including the sender's email address, but this is quite technical (thus not an option for many laymen) and requires to scroll through a lot of headers to find just the one line you are looking for.

issue_title: Configurable message actions
generated_review: I absolutely love K-9 Mail, but the lack of customization for message actions is driving me crazy! As a heavy email user with specific organizational needs, I desperately need the ability to remove or reorder these options according to my preferences. Please, make it possible soon, it would mean the world to me!
issue_body:
Different people use email in very different ways. Some actions on messages (delete, archive, mark as unread,  move, reply, …) are very important to one group of users, but are never used by others. K-9 Mail currently offers limited support to alter the list of actions that are displayed in the toolbar when viewing a message. This can be configured under 
`Settings > General settings > Display > Visible message actions`.

The existing feature isn't very flexible and works in ways that is surprising to many users. I suggest to change it so actions can be freely reordered or completely removed from the toolbar. The user interface for configuring message actions could be a list consisting of three sections. The first one contains the items that are displayed as icons in the toolbar, limited to a sensible number (maybe 4 or 5). The second section contains items that are displayed in the overflow menu (three dots). The third section contains additional actions that the user doesn't want to display at all.
Items in the list can be reordered using drag and drop, which also allows moving an item from one section to another.

The fact that we have sub-menus ("Send…" and "Refile…") makes this a bit more complicated. For a first implementation I suggest we keep the items of the sub-menus fixed and only allow the sub-menus itself to be reordered. The contents of the sub-menus should also exist as single items that can be placed individually. This may lead to an action being available twice in the toolbar, e.g. "Move" as icon and then as part of the "Refile…" sub-menu. But the same is true with the current implementation.

Another complication is the fact that we support a split-screen view where the message list and the message contents are displayed next to each other. In this view we "merge" the toolbar actions. Suggestions on how to best handle this situation are welcome.

Related: #3530
reason: Review accurately reflects the issue regarding the need for configurable message actions and expresses user frustration.

issue_body:

**Description**

1. Change password on mail server - in my case this is GMX. GMX requires credentials for send (SMTP) and sync via IMAP to the device
2. Compose new email and press send
3. Check contents of OUTBOX folder on the device - the email just created and sent sits there idling

**Expected behavior**

 -  5.600

The correct password supplied in the K9 prompt is only used for sync of inbox and folders  with imap.gmx.net (required credentials are user and password) but not for the OUTBOX folder which is connected to mail.gmx.net (SMPT server for outgoing mail; required credentials are again user and password).

issue_title: linebreaks are added to text of messages retrieved from server
generated_review: K-9 Mail app seems to be changing the format of my email messages, making them harder to read. It automatically adds breaks between lines even when they shouldn't be there. Please fix this issue so I can read my emails comfortably.
issue_body:
Ever since i use k-9, i notice that k-9 shortens line-length of messages, which it retrieved from the server (emphasizing that it is not about composing messages).

I guess that k-9 does this in an attempt to adjust text-content to the device's screen width. If the user zooms out/in, then k-9's adjusted line lengt is maintained and the text shrinks, leaving wasted "white area" horizontally, or the text expands beyond the screen area, respectively.

I consider this as a (design) bug, because it affects readability of text severely. Instead, k-9 could/should maintain the original line length and just wrap the text at the screen/window-edge, just as we are used to from our email clients on "desktop" environments: If the user zooms in, then the characters (should) become "larger" and wrapping (at screen/window-edge) is done "earlier" and more frequent, while if the user zooms out, then the characters (should) become smaller and the screen-edge-wrapping is done "later" and less frequent.

The problem in k-9's current approach becomes even worse when there is a "larger" image embedded into the content of the viewed message. Then, lines are typically modified* by k-9 to cover only a low number of words. Causing an extreme "gap" between the perceived text-"column"-width and the required zoom-choice in order to view a reasonable portion of the embedded image.

(*Yes, i do understand that the source code of a message is not modified by k-9 for other clients that might read the message later as well. The modification is of course only on k-9-displaying-level, therefore let's call it a "virtual" modification).

In the mentioned case of an embedded larger image, it only slightly matters whether k-9 zooms in to fit the "narrow" text-column (which it produced by adding virtual linebreaking) to the screen-width automatically vs. whether it zooms out to fit the image into the screen width automatically. Either way, I believe it is not the best choice.

issue_title: Add support for vibration patterns on Android 8+

Android 8 has introduced [notification channels]([URL] where an app can only provide an initial configuration. See also #5544

**Describe the bug**
Separate IMAP client deletes unread message, v5.802 does not retract New Message notification previously posted when IMAP PUSH saw new msg arrive

**To Reproduce**
1.  send message to an account watched via IMAP PUSH by K-9 v5.802

3. via another IMAP client (desktop, even K-9 v5.600 on another android), delete the message before marking it read
4. Android notification previously posted by K-9 v5.802 is not retracted and stays visible  (note that v5.600 properly retracts in such a case)

**Expected behavior**
A message never marked read but deleted by another client should retract K-9's previously posted new-message notification.

**Environment:**
 -  v5.802
 -  8.0 // old, I know
 - Device: LG V20 // old, I know
 - Account type: IMAP (gmail)

**Additional context**
Note as mentioned above, v5.600 (K-9) does retract notifications in such cases

A work-around that the end-user may practice is as follows:

Whichever separate non-K9(v5.802) IMAP client is being used (desktop client of some form on another machine, K-9 v5.600 itself on another Android device), if you FIRST mark the newest message read, THEN delete that newest message, K-9 v5.802 DOES properly retract the previously posted new-msg android-notification.

So I'm wondering if K-9 v5.802 could be changed to treat a message deletion (for a message just received and for which the android system notification was posted, and which is still an unread message) as experiencing both an "is read" and "is deleted" state change?

I realize, having briefly scanned the issues list here that there are many challenges surrounding android notifications, and that this may not be an easy thing to track down and solve.  I hope I've provided enough info.

message arrives, remains new/unread, is deleted from another IMAP client, K-9 v5.802 leaves the android notif up (while 5.600 removes the notif under the same conditions).

conversely:

message arrives, remains new/unrerad, is first marked read from another IMAP client, then deleted from another IMAP client, K-9 v5.802 tears down the android notif previously posted for the new message.

We should do the following, in order:
- [x] When the Unified Inbox is enabled and all messages belong to a folder that is included in the Unified Inbox, open the Unified Inbox.
- [x] When all messages belong to the same folder, open that folder.
- [x] Otherwise, open a message list view that only includes new messages.

Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable
Content-Type: text/plain;
 charset=utf-8; protected-headers="v1"
Subject: =?UTF-8?B?bW9uZXkg8J+kkQ==?=

I reviewed my other accounts, they all have the mail format with independent MIME block for the protected-headers="v1". So the worked format is that the protected-headers="v1" opens a new nest of MIME block (multipart/mixed) and include the actual mail body in its sub-block.

My conclusion (a guess) is that when you compose a new mail with simple text with the configurations "automatic message format" for the account, then you will get this weird format when K-9 decides to compose the message as plain text.

1. Configure account to enable "Encrypt message subjects"

issue_title: Support custom notification sound on Android 7 and older

Title: Missing custom notification sound option on Android 7 and below

Review: Loving K-9 Mail as my go-to email app, but I recently noticed an issue on Android 7 and older devices. It seems that I can't select a custom notification sound for new emails anymore. Previously, there was a handy feature that let me choose from various sounds, but now it appears to be missing.

issue_body:
On Android versions prior to Android 8 we display our own notification sound picker ("New mail ringtone"). The component uses [`RingtoneManager`]([URL] to retrieve the list of notification sounds. But on Android versions prior to Android 10 `RingtoneManager` will only return custom notification sounds if the app holds the [`READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`]([URL] permission. Since we no longer request that permission custom notification sounds can't be selected.

I don't want the app to request the `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permission just to support custom notification sounds. Given that, I believe we have two options:
1. Use the system picker for notification sounds: [`ACTION_RINGTONE_PICKER`]([URL] ~Investigate whether this will allow picking custom notification sounds without the calling app having the `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permission.~ (seems to work on an API 24 emulator)
2. Use the storage access framework to pick a notification sound, then copy it to app-private storage and expose it via a content provider to the system, e.g. using [PublicFileProvider]([URL]

issue_body:
### Checklist
