### Problem you are trying to solve

With the rise in demand for more security in mobile applications (as evidenced by requests like [URL] [URL] [URL] [URL] [URL] [URL] [URL] [URL] a lot of users are trying to seek solutions for common security risks such as unauthorized device access and network sniffing for credentials.  I understand K9 isn't an advanced security application, nor should it be, but I think this can give some users a much wanted peace of mind.

### Suggested solution

I'd like to have an option for K9 to NOT remember my email account password and just prompt the user to enter it if and when needed.

This way the user can rely on a third party application for encrypting their credentials or they can remember their password manually.  While this won't prevent unauthorized access to existing data on the device, it will prevent new data from being sent to the device and give protection against unauthorized users sending data using the saved account.  

It can also help the user to be more aware of the network they're connected to in the event they're connected to a rouge network or otherwise at risk for a man in the middle type of attack.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

If implemented, it'd probably be good to have an option in the per account settings, probably under general settings.  It could just be a simple checkbox for "Remember password" that's checked by default.

Another checkbox could be added when adding a new account to "remember" the password that would have to be unchecked. 

There could also be a global setting in the main General Settings under Privacy that unchecks it for all existing accounts (perhaps with a warning that any existing stored passwords will be removed) and keeps the creation checkbox unchecked by default.  

The effects could cause the app to prompt the user for the password for a given account when the app is opened, when a manual or automatic update is triggered, or when sending an email or other server request.

When entered, the password would be used for that connection attempt and "forgotten" when finished.  It would be similar to how Thunderbird operates if you decline to have it remember account passwords.

Title: Email issues with web browsing

Review: "I've been trying to share links through the browser but the emails aren't sending properly. Sometimes they get stuck and I have to manually send them from the outbox. It's really frustrating because it shouldn't be this complicated.

Other

issue_title: Can't switch account from POP3 to IMAP
generated_review: Experienced a frustrating issue with the latest update of K-9 Mail on my Pixel3 (Android 11). Despite switching accounts from POP3 to IMAP, it continues to use the old connection settings. This results in failed tests when connecting to the new server, which is quite inconvenient.
issue_body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.

6.000

Google Play

11

### Device model

Pixel3

1. Open settings for an account configured for POP3
2. Switch to IMAP, configure.
3. Tap Next for test.

Connection to IMAP server.

It's still using the Pop3Connection to connect to the IMAP port. So all test connections fail, with a display of the list of Capabilities returned from the IMAP server.

### Logs

```
at com.fsck.k9.backend.pop3.Pop3Backend.checkIncomingServerSettings(Pop3Backend.kt:128)
at com.fsck.k9.controller.MessagingController.checkIncomingServerSettings(MessagingController.java:1726)
at com.fsck.k9.activity.setup.AccountSetupCheckSettings$CheckAccountTask.checkIncoming(AccountSetupCheckSettings.java:504)
```

> D Pop3Connection: <<< QUIT BAD Error in IMAP command received by server.
> E AccountSetupCheckSettings$CheckAccountTask: Error while testing settings

The IMAP server is returning a set of RFC-valid Capabilities. It's obvious that it used the wrong protocol to query the server. I think I did completely exit/close the app and then re-enter to get the same results. So, as I recall, it doesn't seem to reset whatever flag is used to determine the POP3/IMAP protocol until after a successful test is done.

My solution was simply to create a new account, as IMAP and remove the POP3 account. This eliminated any possible issues related to local folders versus remote folders. This might be the best solution, although in the process, account settings for reading and writing are lost.

So one approach to resolving this might be to prevent us from changing the protocol type of an existing account between POP3 and IMAP.
Another approach would be to address the protocol selection, and check folder settings to make sure existing POP3 folders and their settings are not lost in the process of loading resources from a new IMAP server.

Do we care about those? - How do we handle long conversations? Do we break them apart after a limit is reached (I believe Gmail is doing that). [SCREENSHOT]

issue_title: Proper formatting when sending RTL/BiDi messages
generated_review: Can't send RTL messages properly; they show fine in K-9 but get messed up on Gmail.
issue_body:

Currently, when I send such messages, they render correctly only in k9 itself (and that only under specific circumstances), but not, e.g., in Gmail. It's actually a bit complicated, so bear with me... RTL languages (such as Hebrew / Arabic / Persian) are written right-to-left -- this refers both to the fact that the text is aligned to the right rather than to the left, as well as the fact that the second letter of a word is written to the left of the first letter, and the second word is written to the left of the first word, etc. When mixing RTL and LTR text in the same paragraph, things are even more complicated. Proper rendering of such text is done by the BiDi (bidirectional) algorithm. Specifically (and simplifying a bit), part of the algorithm is that the paragraph direction is determined by the language of the first character. In the following examples, "אבג" is the first logical word, with its first letter being "א" (Hebrew letter Aleph). The second word is "abc", and the third word is "דהו". As explained above, since the first character is in Hebrew (an RTL language) , the entire paragraph should be aligned to the right. When *composing* the message in k9, it renders correctly: [SCREENSHOT] Note that the first word (אבג) is rightmost, followed (moving from right-to-left) by the second word (abc) and then the third (דהו). Also, the entire paragraph is aligned to the right. However, when *viewing* the received message in k9, it does not display correctly: [SCREENSHOT] Not only is the entire text aligned to the left, but also the first word appears left-most, rather than right-most. The received message is also rendered incorrectly when viewed in gmail: [SCREENSHOT] On the other hand, when trying the same test from Gmail, it displays correctly all along -- displays correctly while composing it in gmail: [SCREENSHOT] renders correctly after being received in gmail: [SCREENSHOT] and also renders correctly when viewed in k9: [SCREENSHOT] Note that both messages are composed in HTML/RTF format. However, when inspecting the messages, it can be seen that the one composed by gmail conatins html "dir" attributes (showing only the text/html part of the message): ``` Content-Type: text/html; charset="UTF-8" Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable
=D7=90=D7=91=D7=92 abc =D7=93= =D7=94=D7=95

So continuing to investigate, I noticed that the above fix is applying the "dir" attribute to a `

issue_title: Set the new unread email system notifications timestamps to match the email metadata's date and time from the IMAP server, instead of the time of notification emission
generated_review: I've been using K-9 Mail for a while now, but lately it seems the app is showing me emails as new even when they aren't. It's really confusing because sometimes I see notifications for old emails. Please fix this issue soon so I can trust my emails again.
issue_body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.602

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

LineageOS 16.0 (Android 9)

### Device model

Any



1. Configure IMAP folder "A" (ex: the inbox) and folder "B" to be 1st class / to emit notifications on new messages
2. In K-9 mail, go to folder "A", swipe the sidebar open to see the list of folders
3. In another email client elsewhere (i.e. a desktop email client, or webmail interface), mark one old email from folder A as unread, and move that email to folder B
4. In K-9, pull down the folders list to force a refresh (or wait for it to eventually periodically poll all folders by itself, but that would take longer)

Note: While this scenario might seem uncommon, this is actually also pretty close to how things might happen with email filters sometimes, depending on timing (for instance, I have some email filters that cannot be handled server-side, so they are handled client-side by my desktop email client, so there is some delay).

Alternate scenario / alternate way to reproduce:
1. Leave your phone disconnected, powered off or in "Airplane mode" for a while
2. Arrange for some new emails to come in to your email account
3. Reconnect your phone, and see K-9's notifications come in... probably with the wrong timestamps



Notify about the "new" unread mail, but set the notification's timestamp to the email's "received" timestamp, not the time at which the notification is emitted. This will keep them in chronological order and will help me go through them by priority.



New/unread email notifications are emitted to Android system notifications "with the current timestamp at the time at which the notification was created / when the check was done", instead of using the email's "date/time received" timestamp from the server.

So in practice, I might get 30 email notifications timestamped as "Now", in disorder, most of which do not actually require my attention, instead of the notifications reflecting the time at which the emails were received by the IMAP server.

### Logs

Here are some screenshots showing the mismatched notification timestamp using the 2nd method (airplane mode while an email gets received by the server, then reconnecting K-9).

First, notice the timestamp of the received mail (12h52) vs the current time (12h56):

[SCREENSHOT]

...then, notice the timestamp of the notification ("Now", i.e. 12h56):

[SCREENSHOT]

---

## Is this actually possible?

It would seem so; in comparison, some other Android mail clients (like FairEmail) are able to correctly set the notification timestamp in the past.

issue_title: Reply behavior violates RFCs when a List-Post header is present
generated_review:
Title: Replies going to incorrect email addresses

I've noticed recently that my replies to emails aren't being sent to the correct person. It used to work fine, but now they're ending up somewhere else. I don't understand why this is happening and it's causing problems in my communication. Please fix so I can continue using the app without issues. Thanks!
issue_body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.603

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

10

### Device model

SM-G960U1

Reply to a message that contains a "sender" header

Address the reply to the address in the "From" header or to the address in the "Reply-To" header if present.

The reply is addressed solely to the address in the "Sender" header.

For several years a simple "reply" to a message sent via a mailing list
went solely to the address in a "List-Post" header, if present, rather
than to the original author in the "From" or "Reply-to" headers. 
That seems to have finally been fixed, but now, as of V6.603, a simple
reply is being sent solely to the address in the "Sender" header, if
present. 

Neither behavior is or was correct at any time, and the problem is
exacerbated by the "To" field in the reply composition containing only
"+1", so the person replying has no idea that this unexpected and
unwanted behavior is present.

Could we PLEASE conform to the relevant RFCs? A reply is to be addressed
to the "From" address(es) in the original message unless a "Reply-To"
header is present, in which case the reply is to be addressed there. Full
stop. A Reply-all should go to the "From" or "Reply-To" as well as to the
"To", "CC", and, if present "Bcc" addresses placed in the same headers
going back. 

From RFC 5322 Section 3.6.2 (updated but unchanged by RFC 6854): 

"The "From:" field specifies the author(s) of the message, that is, the
mailbox(es) of the person(s) or system(s) responsible for the writing of
the message. The "Sender:" field specifies the mailbox of the agent
responsible for the actual transmission of the message. For example, if
a secretary were to send a message for another person, the mailbox of
the secretary would appear in the "Sender:" field and the mailbox of the
actual author would appear in the "From:" field." 

"The originator fields also provide the information required when
replying to a message. When the "Reply-To:" field is present, it
indicates the address(es) to which the author of the message suggests
that replies be sent. In the absence of the "Reply-To:" field, replies
SHOULD by default be sent to the mailbox(es) specified in the "From:"
field unless otherwise specified by the person composing the reply." 

And from Section 3.6.3: 

"When a message is a reply to another message, the mailboxes of the
authors of the original message (the mailboxes in the "From:" field) or
mailboxes specified in the "Reply-To:" field (if it exists) MAY appear
in the "To:" field of the reply since these would normally be the
primary recipients of the reply. If a reply is sent to a message that
has destination fields, it is often desirable to send a copy of the
reply to all of the recipients of the message, in addition to the
author. When such a reply is formed, addresses in the "To:" and "Cc:"
fields of the original message MAY appear in the "Cc:" field of the
reply, since these are normally secondary recipients of the reply. If a
"Bcc:" field is present in the original message, addresses in that field
MAY appear in the "Bcc:" field of the reply, but they SHOULD NOT appear
in the "To:" or "Cc:" fields."

### Logs

_No response_

issue_title: Permanently acoustic notifications probably by K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android, but in most cases no new emails in Inbox
generated_review: K-9 Mail is driving me nuts! Notifications pop up constantly, but there's never any actual emails! My phone's going wild and I'm missing important messages. Fix this NOW!
issue_body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.711

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

Android 10

### Device model

LG K50 s



When my smartphone generates acoustic notifications probably invoked by K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android, in most cases no visual notifications about new mails in the Inbox of K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android gets displayed on the Launcher Screen of my smartphone and no new mail has arrived in my main email account at my mailhoster, or such a visual notification gets displayed on the Launcher Screen for maximally one second and then disappears, but in fact a new email has arrived, but this time in the Inbox of the alias email account of my main email account at my mailhoster, and this new mail is displayed in the corresponding folder in by K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android and in the email program KMail on my laptop.

When I notice an acoustic notification by my smartphone, I first check the Launcher Screen if it displays a visual notification about a new email in K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android, and if the Launcher Screen does not display such a visual notification I check my main mail account at my mailhoster with its alias mail account in the email program "KMail" on my laptop, and in most cases in K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android, too. In most cases it appears that now new mail had arrived in my main email account at my mailhoster.

Sometimes in these situations as described above, the acoustic notifications are not fully generated regarding their length, i. e. they get abruptly stopped before they reach the end of their acoustic signal sound file.

How often does this behavior occur?

To give you an impression about how often this behavior occurs: This morning between 5 and 7 A.M. my smartphone generated 3 acoustic notifications, while in these three cases no new mail had arrived in the Inbox of my main mail and alias mail account.

While I am writing this bug report, my smartphone has generated appr. 10 times such a "ghost" acoustic notification until now. OK, I am a little bit slow in writing this report because my mother tongue is not English. I think it will take me two hours to write and finally save this bug report here.

Some days ago my smartphone generated more often these "ghost" acoustic notifications than compared to today's morning. Like every 20 minutes or so. Note that the version of K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android installed some days ago (6.6xx) was older than the version which is currently installed on my smartphone (6.711). Today I updated K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android to its newest available version in the F-DROID store.

Note that the behavior described above occurs at home. I did not take my smartphone out of my apartment since about two weeks. My smartphone uses Wi-Fi at home to be connected to the Internet via my router.

I think that the behavior described above started from the moment on when I had changed the Wi-Fi name of my router (its SSID) here at home. In the settings of my router I added the text string "_optout_nomap" at the end of the name of the SSID of my router, i. e. this way:

"<SSID>_optout_nomap"

According to Mike Kuketz, a German IT security and data protection specialist, this SSID name extension tells Microsoft, Google and other similar providers (location mapping services) not to process such SSID's for registering their location geo data, which are used to locate the positions of smartphones and other devices. This information can be found (in German) in chapter "WLAN-SSID: Opt-Out" here:

[URL]

Note that I am using K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android in connection with OpenkeyChain on my smartphone, and that the adblocking app Adaway is running on my smartphone with several active ad blocking filters.

This afternoon I logged one of these "ghost" acoustic notifications on my smartphone using the logging/debugging functionality of K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android. This "ghost" acoustic notification which I logged occurred today at 14:58 o'clock German Winter Time.

This is what K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android has logged today at 14:58 o'clock German Winter Time:

[Note: Having uploaded this quote from the K-9 Mail log file, I noticed that it does not properly gets displayed here, although I used the "code" tags for that. I will upload the quote of the log file separately, just a moment, please.]

General description of how I set up K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android:

- K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android accesses one main email account at my mailhoster which has one alias email account which K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android accesses, too. Incoming mails in the main email address and in the alias email address are both shown in the the Unified Inbox.
- Access to these two mail addresses at my mailhoster via IMAP
- Push is not activated at all
- K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android retrieves (looks for new) mails every 15 minutes

I could upload the exported settings of my K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android setup, but I would do that first, if you think that there is something strange documented in the log information above.



K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android should only notify me with acoustic notifications about new emails in the Inboxes of my main email account and of the alias mail account.

issue_title: [Account setup] Prefill server text field in manual setup flow
generated_review:
Title: K-9 Mail Needs Improvement in Server Setup

Review: The manual account setup process in K-9 Mail can be frustrating. Yesterday, I tried setting up my new account and instead of suggesting the server name as before, it left the field blank. I typed in what I thought was the correct server name but got an error. Turns out, the server name you suggested earlier wasn't accurate. Next time, please prefill the server text field with a valid but incorrect domain format so that I don't waste my time with errors during setup. Thanks!
issue_body:
When the app can't find a configuration, users have to manually specify the server settings. In the past we've suggested a server name (e.g. imap.EMAILDOMAIN). The idea was to save the user time typing the server name when there's a good chance our suggestion (partially) matched the actual server name. However, often the name wasn't correct but users assumed the app auto-detected the value. So they went ahead and tapped the "Next" button, only to get an error when checking the server settings.

As dedicated contributors, we all appreciate the straightforward guidelines enforced by Spotless and Detekt when adding test code to our project. These automated checks make contributions a breeze.

It's time we demystify these unwritten rules. Clear, accessible guidelines are not just a convenience—they are a necessity for efficient and effective collaboration.

We recognize the need for transparency and ease in our contribution process. Here's our action plan to smooth out the contribution process:

2. **Documenting the Undocumented:** When automation isn't feasible or is too resource-intensive, we'll create a clear, concise set of guidelines. This 'Dos and Don'ts' list will be a valuable resource, guiding contributors away from common pitfalls and aligning everyone with best practices.

By implementing these steps, we aim to make contributing a more seamless, frictionless experience. Let's work together to enhance our project's code quality and maintainability.

issue_body:
Let's encrypt is phasing out their certificate [cross-signing]([URL] that allowed Android Devices prior to 7.1.1 to establish TLS connections.

They've announced that it will [phase out]([URL] begining Feb 8th, 2024. 

This will result in a `java.security.cert.CertPathValidatorException: Trust anchor for certification path not found.` exception for every domain that renewed their certificate after that date or creates a new one.

We need to change to a trust store that trusts ISRG Root X1.

issue_title: "Remind me of this email" feature
generated_review:
Title: Urgent Need for "Remind Me" Feature in K-9 Mail

Desperately needing this amazing app to meet my organizational demands! Please consider adding a "Remind Me of This Email" feature. It would be immensely helpful to manage tasks related to new emails without losing track or having to juggle multiple apps. Thank you for your time and consideration!
issue_body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.710

### Problem you are trying to solve

Receiving new emails that imply some task/response one would like to work on later is annoying as
 - one can either open the email but then needs to use a separate todo app to remind oneself about it later or,
 - one could refrain from reading the full email to make the notification stay there in order to not forget working on it later.

### Suggested solution

A "Remind me of this email" feature would solve the issue.
This has been worked on in this really old PR: [URL] - however it was then closed, by reasoning as follows:

> 1. I think "hiding" messages is an important part of a snooze feature. How that's accomplished technically is another matter (I like the 'move to another folder' approach).
> 2. The 'notify again' time doesn't seem to be persisted anywhere. That'll break the feature e.g. when the device reboots. In my opinion a reminder functionality that doesn't work reliably is worse than none at all.
> 3. Right now nothing is preventing snoozed messages from being removed from the device, e.g. when they fall outside the sync window.
> 4. There's no visual indicator for a snoozed message. Also, no way to un-snooze.

Regarding point 1. and 4., I think it boils down to personal preference/the idea one has of the feature whether "snoozed" emails should be hidden. If it's more a "remind me" feature (like Slack has), than a "snooze this email" feature, I see no need at all to hide the email. In fact, I'd think it's better UX to not hide and just re-trigger the notification after a while as one can then still read the email (e.g. while on the go), ponder about what to do with it, and therefore work more efficiently on it later (when being back home). Therefore, at least as a first step I think a remind me feature could/should be implemented without hiding the email in the app. This is a lot less work too, as I understood it. Consequently, point 4. is also not strictly necessary anymore then - a little icon indicating that a reminder has been set would surely be nice but is not _required_ to obtain a solid UX in my eyes.

Regarding point 3.: This is a valid point and I don't know how much work it is to prevent these messages from being removed from the device or to re-fetch them later. Maybe some internal progress since 2016 has also improved this situation in k9 already (?). In either case, while having/making the email still available when the user clicks the notification would surely be better, I think it wouldn't be a deal breaker for this feature if the email is gone then - this should rarely happen as I'd assume the "remind me" feature is rather intended for short term uses (a few hours) than days, making it unlikely emails disappear that fast. Also - is there any difference to leaving notifications intentionally open for that time in the current app? Is there anything that prevents those emails from being removed from the device? If not then this should not be a requirement for this feature either.

This makes point 2. the only remaining blocker for the feature implementation from the PR. But from my experience, I'd assume scheduling a permanent reminder is not that much of an effort (I have never worked with the k9 codebase though).

I opened this as a new issue to start a discussion on what UX is intended for this feature as suggested in the PR from 2016. There has been [this]([URL] related issue, but I don't think the discussion there has been very constructive. It has been closed because of the different interaction model connected to a snooze feature - however this does not apply to a "remind me" feature as I described here.

I really think this feature would be extremely useful to lots of people. It would definitely save me from a lot of (if not any) worries and annoyances in my day to day life with k9 mail.

That being said, weighting estimated implementation effort against usefulness, I would definitely not say this feature should be low priority (as the snooze feature was classified to be before).

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

A popup to select reminder time can be opened by either of the following means:
- clicking an action on the push notification of an email
- tapping a context menu action of an email in the inbox list view
- swiping an email to the right in the inbox list view
- tapping a toolbar button or menu entry in the email details page.

In the popup, one can select common reminder times like "30 mins", "1 hour" etc. Optionally, more "sophisticated" times like "this evening, 19pm" or "tomorrow morning, 9am" could also be suggested. Potentionally, these times could be configurable in the app settings. Also potentionally there could be an Option to set a custom reminder time in the popup.
reason: The review clearly requests the 'Remind Me' feature, directly reflecting the source issue's request for a new feature.

issue_title: SMTP for forward-only addresses
generated_review: I have an email account that forwards all messages to another server, but K-9 Mail can't send emails from it. It keeps saying there's an error. Please fix so I can manage my emails properly.
issue_body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.603

### Problem you are trying to solve

SMTP-only accounts and per-identity SMTP support have been requested previously, but this use case hasn't been satisfactorily addressed.

Here's the problem:

I have an e-mail forwarding account provided by a professional organization.  It has NO inbox.  All mail sent to that account is forwarded to a server I control and appears in the inbox of my server.  That server has several traditional identities that use a local SMTP server.

The local SMTP server can not send from the forwarded address - it fails spf/dmarc and recipients such as gmail bounce any attempt to do so.  Instead, I'm required to send using a SMTP server associated with the professional organization.  (Actually, they outsource to mailroute.net, but it's the same thing.)

In K-9 ("the app"), I can setup an account for this identity that uses the correct SMTP server.  But there is no INBOX.  That leaves me with specifying an invalid IMAP server and setting Poll to never.  And so there is ONLY an OUTBOX.

I can read e-mail to the forwarded address from the account on my server.

But to send from the forwarded address, I have to switch accounts.  Compose/send.  But I can't see the inbox.  So then switch back to see replies or other mail that I need to respond to.

I can't "upload sent messages" because there's no Sent folder - again, just an Outbox.  So I have to Bcc myself, and then manually move the Bcc to Sent..

This is a lot of manual work just to be able to send from the correct identity.

### Suggested solution

SMTP servers should be first class objects, as in Desktop Thunderbird.

Identities should be able to be associated with any SMTP server.

In my case:

The forwarding address would be an identity under my server.  Outbound mail from that identity would use the special SMTP server.  Inbound mail for that identity would appear in the target inbox via it's IMAP server.

Then I can read the mail associated with that identity, and respond all from the same account.  Switching would only be necessary to among identities, not accounts, 

(I do not use a "unified inbox"; my identities are distinct.)

Review: I've been using K-9 Mail for years and love its features, but there's one small issue that has become increasingly confusing lately. issue_body:
In the "incoming server settings" screen users can configure whether the [ID command]([URL] should be sent to the IMAP server (including the app name and version as arguments).

I think a good option for a new name is "Send client information", mostly because the relevant setting in Thunderbird is named `mail.server.default.send_client_info`.

In addition to changing the user-visible string we should also change all associated variable and parameter names.

issue_body:
As part of #7807 we need a mechanism to dynamically retrieve the localized application’s name depending on the build application, specifically for K-9 Mail or Thunderbird for Android. The app name should be injectable into string resources using XLIFF placeholders to allow localization.

- **AppNameProvider Implementation:** Concrete implementations of the AppNameProvider for K-9 Mail (K9) and Thunderbird for Android (Tb).
- **XLIFF Placeholder:** Defined XLIFF placeholder to inject the app name into string resources.
- **Dependency injection:** A Koin module that sets up the dependency injection.

1. send an encrypted message with the subject header protected
2. look at raw message sent on wire
3. external Subject header field shows "Encrypted message", or some localized variant of it

It would be better to use the non-localized string `[...]` as recommended in the default HCPs in [draft-ietf-lamps-header-protection]([URL]

Using a localized string leaks the user's locale to any network operator that can view the message, which reduces size of the anonymity set.  Furthermore, using a specific string unique to thunderbird-android (or k-9) leaks information about what e-mail client the user is using.  This not only reduces the size of the anonymity set further, it also potentially leaks information that an adversary could use for targeted attacks based on known flaws with specific MUAs.

Finally, a subject line of "Encrypted message" (in whatever language) can be accidentally copied into a reply message, which itself is *not* encrypted.  So the string "Encrypted message" isn't even a reliable signal to the end user who receives such a message.

the external Subject header field for an encrypted message shows "Encrypted message" or some other localized string.

### Problem you are trying to solve

I am unable to proceed past the initial account setup screen due to incompatibility with my default browser, Firefox, which is configured with strict security settings that block essential sign-in functionalities.

This prevents me from adding an email account, thereby affecting the core functionality of the app.

It would also solve issues other people have with the email setup, but improperly describe as issues with OAuth etc.

### Suggested solution

Introduce a feature within the email setup workflow to allow users to select their preferred browser for sign-in processes.

This could either be a temporary override for the default browser setting or a more permanent browser choice saved within the app's preferences for all web-based interactions. Settings are however inaccessible during the initial setup.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

The issue arises because the sign-in process redirects to a web page, which does not load properly in Firefox due to the security settings I employ (e.g., script blocking), and can't really turn off.

Allowing the user to select an alternative browser like Brave, where such restrictions can easily be temporarily lifted, would solve this issue. No specific UI changes are needed beyond a simple browser selection option in the settings or during the sign-in process.


I've asked ChatGPT (gpt-4o) if a solution is viable, and it seems possible:
If the goal is to allow users to specifically choose a browser that isn't the default system browser for certain actions, like signing into Thunderbird, an implicit intent isn't quite sufficient. You would need to implement a more targeted approach, possibly using an explicit intent that directly invokes the chosen browser app.

For implementing explicit intents to target a specific browser, you will need to know the package name of the browser app the user has chosen to handle the login process. Here's a general approach on how to do this:

1. Allow the user to select the browser: You could provide a settings option in Thunderbird where users can select their preferred browser from a list of installed browsers.


2. Store the selected browser’s package name: Once the user selects a browser, store the package name of that browser.


3. Use an explicit intent to target the selected browser:

```
val url = Uri.parse("[URL]
val intent = Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, url).apply {
    setPackage(selectedBrowserPackageName)  // Use the stored package name
}
if (intent.resolveActivity(packageManager) != null) {
    startActivity(intent)
} else {
    // Handle the case where the selected browser is not available
    Toast.makeText(context, "Selected browser is not installed.", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
}

```

This code snippet explicitly targets the browser app chosen by the user. The setPackage method is used to direct the intent to the specific app identified by selectedBrowserPackageName, which is the package name of the browser saved from the user's selection.

Offer users the option to have an LLM parse the content of the email, and create a short digest, providing a more meaningful overview of the message.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

The model chosen should be (in order of importance):

1. fast: the model should quickly process incoming messages, allowing for the generated text to appear both in notifications and inbox, without unduely delaying notifications
2. low-resources: the use of the LLM preview function should not unduely affect battery life
3. lightweight: the model istelf should be reasonably small so as to not unduely impact the install size of thunderbird
4. obedient: the model should follow instructions to ensure only a concise preview is returned
5. accurate: this is last in the list, as the status quo of preview lines is often useless. anything reasonably relevant would be an improvement

There may be considerations,

- how many of the stored emails to generate previews for
- should a user be able to restrict function to different power-saving settings (charging, standard, battery saver)
- should models be user loaded, or shipped with thunderbird
- should the functionality be local only, or should there be support cloud and self hosted providers

For a minimum viable feature, there should be
- user settings to enable swapping preview lines for digest lines
- user setting to toggle/configure back processing of emails
- user setting to enable swapping in notifications or only in dashboard
- LLM backend to process an email into a digest

Risks involved:
- Inaccuracies: Digest may be incorrect, causing the user to ignore import emails, or give urgency/legitimacy to unimportant or malicious emails
- Feature creep: shipping this feature may create undesired focus on "AI" features, like LLM email co-writing, or LLM-reading, taking valuable focus and time away from valuable core issues
- Ethics and public perception: "AI" is a currently divisive topic. Shipping such a feature may raise discussions on the ethics behind model training, and mozilla/thunderbird's inherent approval thereof
- Future burden: Should legal issues be settled regarding the training or use of LLMs, there may be a requirement to remove or modify parts or all of this feature.

issue_title: Account accent color does not take effect immediately in Thunderbird Android
generated_review: Recent update on K-9 Mail seems to have an issue with account colors. Changed the color of my email account in settings, yet the change doesn't seem to take effect until I exit and reopen the app. Could be a minor glitch, hope it gets fixed soon.

8.0

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

Pixel 6

1. Launch Thunderbird

Upon returning to list of accounts, the accent color of the previously chosen account should reflect the newly chosen one.

issue_title: Inconsistent Setting for Notification LED
generated_review: K-9 Mail 8.0 version on ShiftOS L 2.0, F-Droid. Sadly, Notification LED settings inconsistent, can't select desired color or frequency anymore. Was working fine before update.

### App

Thunderbird for Android

### App version

8.0

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

ShiftOS L 2.0 (based on AOSP 8.1.0)

### Device model

Shift5me ([URL]



Go to Settings > Account > Notifications > Notificationlight
(The path is freely translated from DE. Hope it fits.)




Redirect to the device settings to customise color and frequency of the LED, like K-9 did before the 8.0 update (I switched to TB, so I don't know what the current K-9 version 8.0 does).



In TB you see a preselected set of colors to choose from. But you are still able to set an individual color for TB in the device settings (Apps & Notifications > Notifications > Notification-LED and add TB there), that overrules the TB settings. So this is confusing, reading e.g. blue in the TB settings, but having the LED flashing green as set for TB in the device settings.

I would prefer being redirected to the device settings, when klicking Notificationlight in the TB settings.

Additionally the TB settings don't give a clue which color tone it is. In my case I have set several blue tones from light over dark to a purpleish to display, which kind of message was recieved (SMS, Mail, Messenger, ...). And I use other colors for other notifications, so changing to red, blue and green for different incoming messagetypes is not an option (for me).

Starting with Version 8.2 K-9 mail has changed its behaviour when switching from WLAN to a Mobile Network.

I have an IMAP (imap.mydomain.com) and SMTP (smtp.mydomain.com) Server running in a private network behind a public IP.

When my smartphone is connected to the private WLAN, it gets its IP via DHCP (static mapping) and with it also the ip address of the internal name server to resolve imap.mydomain.com and smtp.mydomain.com. The internal name server resolves both hosts to their LAN IP adresses. The K-9 client connected to the WLAN (part of the LAN) connects (TLS) to the services without problems.

Now, when I leave the WLAN, the smartphone switches to the Mobile Network. While retrieving the Mobile IP address also new name servers are provided to the Smartphone. Using this name servers the two hosts are resolved to the public IP of the my private network. The router then does a port forwarding to the LAN IPs of the two services.

If the imap and smtp services can be reached over the Mobile Network, I expect K9 to silently try to reconnect and only come up with an error message IF the reconnection attempt failes. This is how it worked before 8.2. 

When switching from WLAN to mobile Mobil networks K-9 seems to run into a connection timeout of the connections initially established from within the WLAN. That’s expected, as the smtp and imap services are not available at the LAN IP any more. This leads to K-9 throwing connection errors for every account configured. Error message is “authentication failed”, however I think that’s not the root cause and the error message is incorrect. 

This did not happen in prior versions. In prior versions K-9 silently re-established the connection to the server in background, which would include to close the idle connection, re-resolve the host’s DNS via the new name servers provided by the mobile network and the establish the connections to the smtp and imap server again using the public ip.

Starting with 8.2 K-9 client runs into a timeout and does not automatically reconnect/re-resolve the host names. Even worse, the error seems to be blocking unless the error message is clicked. The smtp and the imap configuration screen is displayed and i have to “okay” them to force K-9 to re-establish the connection (so the message is not only informational). I have to do this twice, since the first time K-9 comes up with the same error, only the second time it actually seems to re-resolve the host names and succeds reconnecting to the imap/smtp services. I have to do this for every email account configured. And: It does not persist, next time i switch from WLAN to Mobile Network, the same happens again. I even experienced K-9 to crash after the first error message has been clicked. 

Funny thing is, it does not happen when switched from the Mobile Network to the WLAN after having established connections to the services over the Mobile Network.

issue_title: Sync Debug Tooling
generated_review: Great feature for troubleshooting sync issues, but could use an option for longer log duration.
issue_body:
# 🎯 The objective

Allow us to investigate non-trivial sync/push issues reported by users.

Often it’s not possible for users to export a debug log right after sync or push stopped working. Since we’re using Android’s system log which uses a ring buffer internally, the relevant log messages will be overwritten after some time. So we want to add a mechanism that allows users to log the behavior of the app for a longer period of time. This will provide us with a way to gather the information necessary to find and fix the sync/push problems that can only be reproduced by users.

---

### 🎒 Resources

- [[URL]

## 🦮 Rules of the Road

### 🟢 In Scope

- Add an item to the “Debugging” section in settings to allow enabling/disabling logging to an internal file.
- Limit the logging duration to a fixed time (24h).
- Allow the user to export the contents of the internal log file to an “external” file.

### 🔴 Out of Scope

- User-configurable logging duration

### 🚧 Technical and/or Business Requirements

- Log calls can come from any thread. But file access must happen in a background thread to not impact performance.
- Use a buffered writer to avoid writing to flash storage for every log message.
- Install an uncaught exception handler to flush the log buffer to disk before the app is killed.

## Project tasks

- Create custom Logging tree for Timber to write to file
- Determine and implement which errors are logged to file vs the current logger
- Export file or direct user to file location
- Set time limit on logging. 
- Question: Do we delete old logs? Or just start a new file for the next time frame?

issue_title: Folder Hierarchy
generated_review: Hierarchical folder organization would greatly improve navigation in K-9 Mail.
issue_body:
# 🎯The objective

The aim of this project is to support reacting to release feedback by improving the display of folders within the account drawer, in order for users to better navigate between folders and be more productive when finding the email that is relevant to the user. More specifically, we would like to show the folders in a hierarchy and collapse folders as needed.

### 🎒Resources

- This was a prior roadmap item for the 2024 roadmap which got deprioritized to get the release out of the door.

## 🦮Rules of the Road

### 🟢In Scope

- Add a folder hierarchy to the account drawer
- Provide a way to collapse folders starting at a certain level

issue_title: Incorrect numbering when saving duplicate attachments for application/octet-stream attachments
generated_review: Dear developers of K-9 Mail, I found an issue when saving duplicate attachments. It seems that the numbering is incorrect for application/octet-stream attachments. For example, if a file named 'file.pdf' already exists, instead of naming the new one as 'file (2).pdf', it is named 'file.pdf (1)'. Please fix this issue, as it causes problems later with other applications. Thank you.
issue_body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App

K-9 Mail

### App version

9.0

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

Android 15, CalyxOS 6.6.23

### Device model

Fairphone 4 (FP4)

1. Receive a mail with an attachment.
2. Save that and do it again with another mail with the same attachment (I guess it also works for the same mail).

Let's say the attachment is named `file.pdf`. Given a file named `file.pdf` already exists in the Downloads folder, the file should be named  `file (2).pdf` or similar.

The file is named  `file.pdf (1)`. This is not (actually) (very) funny, but causes problems, because many applications including the built-in file picker of Android do not detect that as a PDF file anymore in that example.
So this breaks a lot of functionality in a subtle way and you have to look twice and have at least basic knowledge about files (notably many people may not have this anymore) to fix it.
Thing is it e.g. may also break images and people could wonder why they don't see saved images in their gallery etc.

Workaround:  renaming, of course

Another less erious issue: Notice how it is suffixed with `(1)`? While this may make sense for technical people, it makes less for everyone else.
I checked how Nautilus (GNOME file manager) does it e.g. when I copy a file in the same dir and it names them `file (copy).pdf` and even `file (second copy).pdf` for the second.

And if I copy a file that already exists in the target location (which is likely more similar to the issue at hand), I can rename it and the default suggestion is: `file (2).pdf`:
[SCREENSHOT]

IMHO both versions are a better UX.

generated_review:
Title: Urgent help needed for K-9 Mail signature issue

I've been using K-9 Mail on my Nothing Phone 1 with Android 15, and I love its functionality, but there's a frustrating bug regarding signatures. My emails have become cluttered due to incorrectly placed signatures breaking the signature stripping feature. Please fix this issue soon as it's critical for me to maintain professional communication. Thank you!
issue_body: ### Checklist - [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report. - [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible. ### App Thunderbird for Android ### App version 10.0 ### Where did you get the app from? F-Droid ### Android version Android 15 ### Device model Nothing Phone 1 Hi, Thunderbird for Android allows users to configure a signature that is always appended to emails when they're sent from that particular account. Signatures are configured under "Settings -> select your account -> Sending mail -> Composition defaults". However, the signature is appended to the wrong part of the message body. This is because the default configuration for signature placement is "Settings -> select your account -> Sending mail -> Composition defaults -> After quoted message" What this means in a real life scenario is that if the user has an ongoing email thread with several earlier correspondences, and they reply from their mobile into that thread today, their signature is put at the very bottom at the entire thread after everybody's every reply. I can list at least 4 reasons why this doesn't make sense: - Nobody reads the bottom line of a long email thread with several replies. Essentially this behaviour makes signatures invisible to recipients. - After a few replies, the bottom lines of the email thread will be nothing but a bunch of signatures one after another, as seen on the attached screenshot. Additionally, signatures get mixed and recipients won't be able to tell which signature belongs to which correspoindence. - Signatures lose their contextual connection to the actual message they belong to. - No sane user would expect signatures to work this way :) Additionally, this breaks the "Settings -> select your account -> Sending mail -> Strip signatures on reply" functionality. Even with that feature enabled, signatures are **not** stripped from replies as I guess we can't find them where they are supposed to be. **I recommend that we make 'Before quoted message" the default behaviour for account signatures and perhaps remove "After quoted message" altogether. Alternatively, if we don't remove "After quoted message" because it covers some special use case, fix "Strip signatures on reply" to work with this option.** --- **Incorrect behaviour with the default "After quoted message""**

issue_title: Automate f-droid releases
generated_review: Please improve the automation of F-Droid releases. Currently, it's manual and requires our attention each time. It would be great if we could adjust build files for a more regular update.
issue_body:
I think we should take care of this now, otherwise we'll never do it and it will be annoying every time. We currently need to submit f-droid builds manually. There is an opportunity to automate it based on tag updates, but our files aren't ready for this because it uses regex. I think we have two options:

#### 1) Adjust build files to a regexable format
- Set [URL] to enable auto updates
- Set [URL] to Tags and add the appropriate tag pattern
- Set [URL] to read from either the respective build.gradle.kts, or a separate version.txt file.
- Adjust our CI especially release process so that version.txt or build.gradle.kts is correctly adjusted.

Upside here is that it is all automated, we adjust our version files once and then f-droid does the rest. Downside is that once we tag (which is early), f-droid will pick it up, so we have no way to hold a build. We should make sure that the regex is fairly stable, so that we don't accidentally break this by changing something in build.gradle.kts and it maybe picks up the wrong version.

#### 2) Add a build step after publish_hold that will send a pull request to f-droid
- Add a step that checks out fdroiddata, updates the yml files, makes sure their linters pass
- Create a pull request such as [URL]

Upside is that we do it after the publish_hold step and it is similar to the play store review. Downside is they have to manually review each pull request.

#### 3) Defer tagging in our builds until after publish_hold

- Make it so that tagging only actually happens after the publish_hold is confirmed
- Continue same steps as in (1)

Upside is that we can hold builds also for those who use FFUpdater or similar. The build is only considered a release once the publish step completes. We get the upsides from (1) as well. The only downside is that this is more effort since we're making some major adjustments to our release process.

generated_review:
Title: Disappointed after switch from Email by Jetpack Smith

Review: After using Email by Jetpack Smith for years, I was excited to try Thunderbird for Android as a more customizable alternative. However, the lack of swipe actions for TalkBack users is a significant setback. This feature is essential for navigating my emails efficiently, something that the competitor app handles effortlessly. issue_body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App

Thunderbird for Android

### App version

11.0b4

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

14

### Device model

Pixel 5

1. Turn on TalkBack.
2. Open Thunderbird.
3. Open a folder.
4. Navigate with TalkBack to one of the messages in the message list.

- Tapping with three fingers on the message brings up the TalkBack menu. One of the options is "Actions", which allows the user to choose the left or right swipe actions.
- Swiping up or down on the message cycles through the left or right swipe actions.

### Background

To better serve Thunderbird users with TalkBack enabled, I’d like to request [Accessibility Actions]([URL] be added to the message list.

The available actions should at least match the currently configured [swipe actions]([URL] (Toggle selection, Mark as read/unread, Add/remove star, Archive, Delete, Spam, or Move). 

An example of an Android app with Accessibility Actions is Raccoon, a social media client for Mastodon and Friendica. (See their [commit #567]([URL] for the rationale.)

- Each post has several buttons below it: reply, reshare, add to favorites, add to bookmarks, and options. 
- If Accessibility Actions were not enabled, then when navigating with TalkBack, the user would encounter each of these buttons, one at a time.
- Instead, with Accessibility Actions enabled, TalkBack only stops once at each post. The buttons are not focused. Instead, TalkBack tells the user: “Actions available. Swipe up or swipe down and double tab to activate.”
- The user can swipe down to cycle through the following actions: reply, reshare, add to favorites, add to bookmarks, link to poster, options, or activate which loads the post into a view by itself, equivalent to tapping in the post body.

#### Demo

[URL]

[Demo transcript]([URL]

This setup allows users to quickly browse posts with a minimum number of swipes, while still having access to quick actions.

By contrast, the official Android Mastodon app iterates through each button under each post. There appears to be no way to jump from one post to another, so browsing a timeline with TalkBack is more time-consuming.

### Implementation in Thunderbird

- An example use case for Thunderbird is: a user is browsing newly arrived messages. Several messages are marketing emails, and the user chooses to delete them directly from the timeline. The user saves time by not navigating to each email individually.

- I believe Accessibility Actions are popular with blind users, based on [these poll results from 23 Feb 2025]([URL] ) where 77% of the 30 respondents like using them. 

- It’d be important to do some user research to determine which actions should be included. Bonus points if the actions and their ordering are configurable. This way, a user's most-used action can be available with just one swipe.

No Accessibility Actions are available to the user.

Delete a message from inbox #### Variant 1 - fetching folder Messages from the selected folder are fetched from server (e.g. using command `EXAMINE "INBOX.Spam"`) and displayed. #### Variant 2 - deleting messages Deleted message is moved to the trash folder. #### Variant 1 - fetching folder Command `EXAMINE "INBOX.INBOX.Spam"` is sent and obviously fails, because there is no such folder. #### Variant 2 - deleting messages Command similar to `UID MOVE 27707:27708,27714:27715 "INBOX.INBOX.Trash"` (here I was deleting multiple messages) is sent and also fails. issue_title: Logging - Enable debug logging option not providing useful data
generated_review: K-9 Mail is generally fantastic, but I'm struggling due to a persistent logging issue that doesn't seem to provide helpful data anymore. It's been hindering my productivity and I'm finding it difficult to troubleshoot problems effectively. Could we please address this soon? Thank you.
issue_body:
After our recent changes to the Logging API, the "Enable debug logging" option is no longer providing useful data. 

We now use the `Logger` interface for logging, which uses the `CompositeLogSink` to determine whether any logging should occur. As a result, the log level remains unchanged, and logs are not displayed in the logcat. Additionally, the `CompositeLogSink` has its own `LogLevel`, which overrides the log levels of the individual sinks. This makes it impossible to update the log level at runtime, as it is defined as a singleton through Koin.

As a result, when exporting logs using `logcat -d` within `LogFileWriter`, there are no useful logs available.

Our team is developing a tool that can automatically identify potential resource issues in Android applications.

To detect resource anomalies, we designed five **neutral cycles**—GUI event sequences that should not increase resource usage:

① **DOC (Double Orientation Change)**
② **Home (Return to Home Screen → Resume AUT)**
③ **Notification (Open Notification Bar → Close Notification Bar)**
④ **Text (Input Text → Clear Text)**
⑤ **Scroll (Swipe Down/Right → Swipe Up/Left)**

The first three cycles are designed to trigger **3 main pairs of lifecycle callback functions** (i.e., onCreate() and onDestroy(), onStart()/onRestart() and onStop(), onResume() and onPause()), while cycles ④ and ⑤ are based on UI interaction semantics, covering user **input** and **scrolling** scenarios that may also affect resource usage.

If executing a specific neutral cycle 50 times in a given state leads to continuous growth in certain resource metrics, we regard it as a potential **resource leak or mismanagement issue** that may cause software aging.

issue_title: Debug menu
generated_review: Debug menu should be more accessible, especially for regular users who want to test new features. Currently, it's only available in certain builds, and even then, it requires a hidden gesture to access. A more user-friendly approach would be appreciated.
issue_body:
### Scope

- Provide a centralized UI for debugging without external tools.
- Allow non-engineers (QA/PM) to flip feature flags safely during testing.
- Make logs discoverable, searchable, and shareable from within the app.

### Out-Of-Scope

- Not a replacement for production-grade observability or remote config.
- No persistent remote sync of flags (local-only for now).
- No alteration of the app’s release build behavior unless explicitly allowed.

### Requirements

- Access:
  - Debug Menu is available only in `debug`/`daily` builds by default.
  - Optionally unlockable in `release`, `beta` with a hidden gesture and an additional confirmation warning.
- Feature Flags:
  - List all known flags with current values.
  - Toggle boolean flags.
  - Persist changes locally (survive app restarts?).
  - Expose a “Reset to defaults” action.
- Logs:
  - Display an on-device rolling buffer of recent logs (min 2,000 lines or 1–5 MB; configurable).
  - Filter by level (`VERBOSE/DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR`) and by tag.
  - Search text query across visible logs.
  - Ability to copy selected lines and “Share” as a text file attachment.
  - Option to clear the in-memory log buffer.
- Safety:
  - Changing flags applies immediately where feasible, otherwise after app restart (with do you really want to restart prompt).
  - Add visual indicators when non-default flags are active.

### UX Outline

- Entry point: from app’s settings menu within → `Debugging`. 
  - Optionally: tap app version 7 times on About screen to reveal in non-debug (store a flag in prefs).
- Debug Menu tabs or sections:
  1) `Feature Flags`
     - List of flags with current value, type indicator, and description.
     - Toggle/switches for booleans; dropdowns for enums; text fields with validation for strings/ints.
     - Buttons: `Reset All`
  2) `Logs`
     - Toolbar: Level filter, Tag filter (autocomplete), Search box.
     - Paginated/virtualized scrolling list of lines: `[time] [level] [tag] message`.
     - Buttons: `Clear`, `Share Logs`.
reason: Review captures the need for a more accessible debug menu but does not mention the specific features requested.

# Description

## Overview

For incoming calls, ringer should sound on mobile-device speakers, even if Bluetooth headset is connected.

The reason is that a user may have recently spoken on a call using a headset, then removed the headset, without ending the connection between the headset and the mobile device. In this case, because the ringer sound currently only occurs through the headset, the user would not have effective audio indication of an incoming call. The native  system for processing regular incoming telephone calls produces sound on both the mobile-device internal speakers as well as any connected headset. As this behavior is generally desirable, Signal application should follow the same pattern.

## Steps to Reproduce 

1. Connect Bluetooth headset.
2. Receive incoming call.
3. *Notice that audio notification occurs through headset but not mobile-device internal speakers. Thus, effective audio indication of incoming call depends on user currently wearing headset.*

issue_title: Skin tone when grouping emojis
generated_review: Group emoji skin tones seem random and inconsistent, ruins group chat experience. Fix please.
issue_body:
> - Skin tone variations of the same 'base emoji' will be grouped together in the badge.
> - When picking which variation to show in the reaction bubble, we will always prefer the variation you selected if you are participating in the reaction, and show the most recent if not.

_Originally posted by @greyson-signal in [URL]

I don't think the choice described in the second bullet point is optimal or natural. It's confusing, unexpected and can lead to strange situations. Moreover, it emphasizes the order in which emojis arrive  which is counterintuitive when grouping (because the entire point of grouping is to abstract away from the information about the individual emojis.) 

I just encountered this in a group where 7 people used tone A "thumbsup" emoji and then one person used tone B and then the badge changed to B. This was surprising and unexpected, in particular if B is is not the neutral tone. Some people in the group who commented on this considered this a bug. 

Moreover, the badge shown was inconsistent between the participants because of the rule that it depends on your own choice. I think strictly speaking, one could even make the point that this is a unnecessary violation of a security property load because different users will disagreements over what the state is. (Sure, we live in an   asynchronous world, so we can't reach this property... But here all messages have arrived, so we don't need to violate agreement.)

I suggest that grouping for the badge either
 * always uses the neutral/yellow tone (That is less surprising because the tone will never change but it's still surprising when there's only a single tone different from the neutral one), or
 * uses the unique tone if there's one and uses the neutral tone when there's one than one tone present in the set. (That still means the tone can change but it changes at most once.)

I'd prefer the second option.

issue_title: Messages not received until app is placed in background or restarted, and probable root cause + fix
generated_review: Signal app seems to delay message delivery unless it's running in the background or restarted. I hope the team looks into this issue as it can cause some inconvenience during conversations.
issue_body:
<!-- This is a bug report template. By following the instructions below and filling out the sections with your information, you will help the developers get all the necessary data to fix your issue.
You can also preview your report before submitting it. You may remove sections that aren't relevant to your particular case.

Before we begin, please note that this tracker is only for issues. It is not for questions, comments, or feature requests.

If you would like to discuss a new feature or submit suggestions, please visit the community forum:
[URL]

If you are looking for support, please visit our support center:
[URL]
or email support@signal.org

Let's begin with a checklist: Replace the empty checkboxes [ ] below with checked ones [x] accordingly. -->

- [x] I have searched open and closed issues for duplicates

- [x] I have read [URL]


----------------------------------------


The bug is fairly general: I've waited for up to an hour waiting for messages to be received. I've seen other people report similar things. If I switch apps (ex. switch to a game, and then switch back to Signal) my messages start going through.

I think I've found the root cause, so this issue describes the smallest set of steps to reproduce the issue. I will likely send a pull request to fix that small sequence, but that fix will likely need to be made more general.

Possibly related issues since Feb 1:
* [URL]
* [URL] (perhaps)
* [URL]
* ~~[URL]
* [URL]
* [URL]


It is important _not_ to switch Signal into the background during these steps.

*On your phone*

- First, go through the "registration" flow: Welcome, Enter Phone, Verify Phone, Re-enter Signal PIN, Enter Profile Info
- Second, send a message "hi" to another Signal user ("other")

*On other phone*

- Third, accept the message sender (or see the "Your safety number ... has changed)
- Fourth, reply to the message with "Hi2"

*On your phone*

- Fifth, wait for a long time (1hr 2 mins and counting) ... no "Hi2" message
- Sixth, move the Signal app into the background and then back into the foreground. _Sometimes_ you will get the "Hi2" message. If you do get a message, it will be immediately after switching apps.
- Seventh: If you close the Signal app and re-open, you will get the undelivered messages immediately.

**Actual result:** Reply message is stuck for a long time
**Expected result:** You get the reply message within seconds

### Screenshots
<!-- you can drag and drop images below -->



**Device:** Android Emulator Pixel 2 XL 
**Android version:** 9.0 x86 with Google APIs
**Signal version:** 5.5.0


* [URL] is the reproduction steps from "First" to "Fourth". No reply message seen.
* [URL] is the steps from "First" to "Sixth". (Noise: I additionally sent the first debug log URL to the "other" user in step "Sixth".) No reply message seen.
* [URL] is the steps from "First" to "Fourth" but only after applying the "Limited Fix" below. I can see the reply message immediately.

### Probable root cause 1
1. The BackgroundMessageRetriever will keep doing "Skipping retrieval -- app is in the foreground" correctly because the Signal app has never been in the background. All the FCM messages will be ignored.
2. The IncomingMessageObserver.MessageRetrievalThread will be stuck in an Object wait state (through IncomingMessageObserver.waitForConnectionNecessary). The only way for it to connect to a websocket is if someone notifies IncomingMessageObserver ... which only happens when the Signal app is has a foreground or background event. 
3. One of the 5 conditions in IncomingMessageObserver.isConnectionNecessary() is TextSecurePreferences.isPushRegistered() == true. That value changes (see log line `03-12 16:54:39.432 23431 23633 I TextSecurePreferences: Setting push registered: true`). However, according to "2." above, there is no one to notify IncomingMessageObserver! If there were some notification, we would see a corresponding `IncomingMessageObserver: Network: true, Foreground: true, FCM: true, Censored: false, Registered: true, Websocket Registered: true, Proxy: false` log line, but we don't.

The above explains why people are getting inconsistent, seemingly irreproducible behavior. Only if they switch their app, the messages magically start. And even switching their app does not always work, because the foreground / background event is not emitted reliably.

### Probable root cause 2

1. The AppForegroundObserver used by IncomingMessageObserver seems flaky. It would be useful to actually emit a log line when the app is foregrounded or backgrounded to know for sure, but the lack of `IncomingMessageObserver: Network: true, Foreground: true, FCM: true, Censored: false, Registered: true, Websocket Registered: true, Proxy: false` log line in the second debug log even after foregrounding/backgrounding repeatedly indicates that AppForegroundObserver is not reliable.

### Limited Fix for probable root cause 1

Added "new code" to the bottom of `org.thoughtcrime.securesms.registration.service.CodeVerificationRequest#verifyAccount`

```java
    TextSecurePreferences.setWebsocketRegistered(context, true);
    // ...
    TextSecurePreferences.setPushRegistered(context, true);
    // ...
    // BEGIN new code
    IncomingMessageObserver incomingMessageObserver = ApplicationDependencies.getIncomingMessageObserver();
    synchronized (incomingMessageObserver) {
      incomingMessageObserver.notifyAll();
    }
    // END new code

    PinState.onRegistration(context, kbsData, pin, hasPin);
```

This limited, hacky fix just sends an `Object.notifyAll()` notification after the registration flow. A more general fix would be to send a notification when any of the 5 conditions changes. For example, any change via TextSecurePreferences.setPushRegistered should directly or indirectly notify IncomingMessageObserver.

I could submit a pull request as-is *or* do a more clean and more general fix. If a more general fix, I'd like to get suggestions from the Signal team for a clean mechanism to do the notifications (ex. is there an internal-to-Signal-app event mechanism?).
reason: The review accurately captures the main issue of delayed message delivery and the conditions under which it occurs.

I've noticed on my device that the conversation activity will occasionally get into a state where the back button doesn't do anything. I'm not sure why this only happens on my device, but I think I found the root cause.


- Open a conversation (I have 100% repro rate in 1:1 conversations but groups don't seem to repro for some reason)
- Begin composing a message to open the keyboard
- Lock the screen
- Unlock the screen (critically, on my device the keyboard is closed by the system during this lock/unlock cycle and the bug does not repro on my friends' devices where this is not true)
- Press the back button

**Actual result:** 
The app will be in a state where the back button has no effect regardless of how many times it's pressed.

**Expected result:** 
The back button should pop the conversation activity and bring up the conversation list.

### Screenshots
Not comfy sharing screenshots since I don't have a burner phone sorry :(


<!-- replace the examples with your info -->
**Device:** Pixel 4A
**Android version:** 11 (running GrapheneOS not the stock rom)
**Signal version:** 5.8.x (Going from memory here) and a build built from the current master branch.



Let me know if you need this.

### Probable root cause

For some reason the system chooses to close the soft keyboard during the lock/unlock cycle. I'm not entirely sure why this happens. When the system is unlocked, `onMeasure` is called in `KeyboardAwareLinearLayout`, but I don't think the resize has actually completed yet. My hypothesis is that `getAvailableHeight` returns the old height, which causes the keyboard state to not be updated during the device unlock. Since the old state sticks around, the layout continues to believe that the keyboard is open. That bad state in `KeyboardAwareLinearLayout` causes the `onBackPressed` logic in `ConversationActivity` to trigger the keyboard closure flow instead of the `super.onBackPressed` flow. Since the keyboard isn't actually open, it can't be closed so the entire back button press is a no-op.

It seems like triggering `updateKeyboardState` and `onRotation` in `KeyboardAwareLinearLayout.onSizeChanged` instead of `KeyboardAwareLinearLayout.onMeasure` fixes this issue, which supports the theory that onMeasure is called too early in the resize operation for `getAvailableHeight` to return the correct (new) value. That could have ripple effects elsewhere in the codebase but it seems like a fairly safe change overall, so I'm going to send a PR for it.

issue_title: Sent photos are compressed
generated_review: Photos appear blurry and lose details after being sent through Signal app.
issue_body:
- [x] I have searched open and closed issues for duplicates

- [x] I have read [URL]




When sending a photo via Signal, it is downsized, recompressed and its EXIF data is removed. The same happens if a photo is sent as a normal file. Signal detects it is a photo and tampers with it nonetheless.

The current implementation effectively removes a great portion of information from the file. Especially rescaling the photo greatly reduces its filesize, but information is lost. All this might be undesired in many cases and I believe it falls under _existing functionality that does not work as intended_.

In the case of EXIF data there is an argument that it should be removed due to privacy concerns, especially the location tag. I think it is a great feature that Signal is able to filter EXIF, but if it is a desirable feature and not a bug, it should be properly implemented and user-configurable (probably with a separate option for location tag filtering).

In the case of photo downsizing, it is especially dire with photos taken with Signal. Even the saved local copies of the photos cannot be saved in higher quality and do not contain any EXIF data. As was previously mentioned, it is also hard to send previously taken photo in full quality. I think photos shouldn't be tampered with by default at least when sending files via generic file transfer function.

**To recap**, this bug report contains three **related** issues:
- Photos, taken via Signal, cannot be saved in full quality and do not contain EXIF data.
- Photos, sent via Signal, are downscaled and EXIF-filtered and even in the case of general file transfer, hacks need to be employed to circumvent this feature, effectively making it a bug.
- EXIF filtering with its current silent implementation leaves a question whether it is a feature or a bug.
reason: The review accurately reflects the issue of photos being compressed and losing quality when sent.

----------------------------------------


After restarting signal (force-kill, reboot, crash), signal looses/forgets preferences (dark theme, pin entry, messages) but remembers account details, identity etc.
Even sent messages are gone. Strangely, some initial messages (first ones sent after setup) do appear.
On a synced signal desktop all messages do 'stay'.

This started to happen after upgrading to v5.23.8, but even downgrading to v5.20.3 kept the same behavior.

Clearing all signal data (effectively a re-install) full re-install of the app, and even a full factory reset (including storage) did not resolve the issue.


- install signal
- set dark theme and 'disable' pin
- restart signal (force-kill, reboot, etc)

** Actual result. **
theme is white again, pin entry is asked again, message history is gone

**Expected result:**
signal remembers everything
