issue_title: Blocking Defeat/Circumvention - Corner Case
generated_review: Blocked users can still message me privately within a shared group.
issue_body:
This is more or less a corner case, but it's still a means by which a blocked user can effectively unblock themselves under a specific circumstance, and do so in a manner that's silent, meaning the person who blocked them is unaware of it.

**Prerequisites:**

1.  Both the blocked user (User B) and the user who blocked User B (User A) are members of a common group.

2.  User A has never sent User B any messages outside of the group, and vice versa.  They have no past association or communication history on Signal.  The group chat is their only link.

**Problem Condition:**
1.  The corner case manifests when User A blocks User B while they are both members of a common group chat, and User B _then_ proceeds to send User A a private message for the first time, outside of the group chat.

2. Once User B attempts to send User A a private message outside the group chat, it automatically unblocks User B from User A's perspective, and there's no notification or indication on User A's primary mobile device that this has occurred.  The only way User A would discover this—outside of the obvious and unwanted resumption of User B's messages and emoji actions appearing in the group chat—is the indication that User B has been sporadically unblocked on a linked Windows device.

[SCREENSHOT]

3. The message User B tried to send User A was not delivered or readable from User A's perspective, but it's patently obvious given the context surrounding the matter between User A and User B that User B attempted to send this message.

So there you have it.  This user that I blocked on February 5th managed to unblock themselves without me finding out about it until March 2nd when I started seeing their unwanted emojis/messages in the group chat again.  I immediately re-blocked them, and left the group a couple weeks after that.  Sometime after leaving the group, I opened up Signal on my linked Windows device, and discovered the anomalous message request pictured above.  The indication that I unblocked them on February 16th was quite obviously BS, because I most definitely did no such thing.  I archived the group chat weeks earlier, and hadn't viewed or interacted with it until March 2nd.  The only rational deduction is that this person attempted to send me a message on February 16th, outside the group chat that I was a member of at the time, and this somehow unblocked them without my interaction or knowledge.

This message request that slipped through the cracks is a major bug, corner case or not, and so is the fact that they were able to unblock themselves without me knowing about it and resume sending emojis/messages in the group chat that I could see.

issue_title: Signal Sent Screenshots to Random Contacts: Possible Interference from System App on Duoqin F22
generated_review: Signal inadvertently shared old screenshots due to a pre-installed app - investigate first.
issue_body:
Hi all,

I’m writing to report a very unusual and concerning incident involving Signal on my Duoqin F22 Android phone.

Last Sunday, after having my phone powered off for several hours, I turned it back on and immediately noticed that Signal had sent two old screenshots (including my status bar and home screen) to five seemingly random contacts. These screenshots were not taken recently, and I certainly did not initiate or authorize their sending. There are no linked devices, and I hadn’t opened the app or interacted with the phone before this happened.

While investigating, I discovered that my device came with a pre-installed system application called DebugLoggerUI.apk, located at /system/app/DebugLoggerUI/. The app has permissions like:

    READ_LOGS
    MODIFY_PHONE_STATE
    RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED
    SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW
    SET_DEBUG_APP

The firstInstallTime for this app is before I bought the phone, which strongly suggests it was included by the manufacturer. The device is a Duoqin F22 (also sold as Qin F22), a minimalist Android phone with a keypad and small screen.

This has raised serious concerns about whether the phone’s system environment may interfere with or monitor Signal’s behavior, and whether it’s even safe to use Signal on such a device. I tried using MVT (Mobile Verification Toolkit) to extract data, but MVT couldn’t pull full logs or APKs. This is likely because the device reported as “busy,” possibly due to this logging app.

Has anyone else experienced anything like this?

    Can Signal devs confirm whether system-level interference could ever result in screenshots being sent to contacts?
    Could the presence of such a logger app affect Signal’s integrity or messaging functions?
    Should I consider this a compromised environment?

Happy to provide logs, extracted APKs, and any further info if that helps the investigation.

Thanks for all the amazing work you do.
Ant.

issue_title: ANR error when registering an account with reglock set
generated_review: Experienced an ANR issue during account registration, specifically when the app attempts to chain multiple tasks simultaneously. Seems like a priority issue with the StorageSyncJob and ReclaimUsernameAndLinkJob causing delays.
issue_body: When the registration process is successful, Signal Android tries to restore the storage account, and then tries to chain two jobs to each other and block until completion: StorageSyncJob and ReclaimUsernameAndLinkJob, inside the RegistrationViewModel.kt class, function onSuccessfulRegistration. ReclaimUsernameAndLinkJob has a higher priority than the StorageSyncJob (PRIORITY_HIGH vs PRIORITY_DEFAULT, because StorageSyncJob is called with forRemoteChange), they both execute on the same queue (StorageSyncJob.QUEUE_KEY), so ReclaimUsernameAndLinkJob takes priority as mostEligibleJobForQueue. The issue is that, by calling AppDependencies.jobManager.startChain(StorageSyncJob.forRemoteChange()) .then(ReclaimUsernameAndLinkJob()) .enqueueAndBlockUntilCompletion(TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(10)), this makes ReclaimUsernameAndLinkJob dependent on StorageSyncJob. This creates a Starvation situation that block both jobs from running. I think that a possible solution should be: create StorageSyncJob with PRIORITY_HIGH (as in the forAccountRestore() function inside StorageSyncJob) + create ReclaimUsernameAndLinkJob with a lower priority, but this means writing another constructor where this job is instantiated as such. ### Screenshots

issue_title: Disappearing message timer's delivery confirmations compromise deniability of blocking a user
generated_review: I noticed something odd while using Signal. After setting the disappearing message timer, my contact got an instant delivery confirmation. This shouldn't happen, as per the docs, Signal doesn't tell when you're being blocked. It's a bit confusing and compromises privacy.
issue_body: # Summary Receiving instant delivery confirmations after setting a disappearing message timer reveals to contacts with high confidence that they have been blocked. # Observed behavior A blocked contact can deduce from an instant delivery confirmation after setting a disappearing message timer that one has been blocked by the respective contact. # Expected behavior According to Signal's user documentation Signal should not tell a user that one has been blocked. > "*Signal does not tell you if you are being blocked by someone else.*" ([Docs]([URL] When a user has been blocked, one should not receive an instant delivery confirmation as this is the way Signal behaves with contacts that a user has not been blocked by. # Steps to reproduce Considering **Alice** (*Blocker*) and **Bob** (*Blocked*) this behavior can be reproduced: 1. Establish contact between **Alice** and **Bob** by either of them sending a message request that is approved by the other. 2. On **Alice**'s device **Bob** is blocked by the *Block* function in the contact settings. 3. **Bob** sets a disappearing message timer. When receiving a response within a few seconds, **Bob** knows that he has likely been blocked. **Bob** can increase his certainty by repeating this step at multiple different times. # Priority / Security implications I found this behavior a few weeks ago and even considered it a very minor security issue _if_ considering the deniability of the blocking a security objective. Having heard of "[*Silent Signals: Exploiting Security and Privacy Side-Channels in End-to-End Encrypted Messengers*]([URL] by *Gegenhuber*/ *Günther* at DEFCON 33 about delivery confirmation analysis I considered my observation to be more important than I initially estimated. issue_title: Message queue blocked by unresolved mentions in quotes

It keeps blocking incoming messages, leaving me frustrated and unable to communicate effectively. Please look into this urgent matter and provide a swift resolution. Thank you.
issue_body:
A user noticed that incoming messages were blocked on the Molly app. The issue occurs when a quoted message contains mentions that point to unknown recipients.

The stack trace shows: `Recipient$MissingAciError: Missing ACI for -1`.

This happens in `MentionUtil.mentionsToBodyRangeList` when it calls `Recipient.requireAci()` on unresolved recipients.

It appears that `getMentionsForMessage` (called by `getValidatedQuote`) can return unknown recipients, and `mentionsToBodyRangeList` does not filter them. This causes the transaction to fail and blocks the entire incoming message queue. 

While the bug was observed on Molly, it may also exist in upstream Signal, so it is reported here on behalf of the user. I don't know the exact root cause yet, so I'm reporting it for investigation rather than proposing a fix.

issue_title: Message order can be mangled by a client device changing time zones or making changes to OS time
generated_review: Signal is usually great, but sometimes it gets confused when we travel or change our phone's time settings. Messages appear jumbled up which makes following conversations difficult. I hope they fix this soon.
issue_body:
Background:
I manage a group where members often travel to different time zones independently from each other. It is also common for our members to manually set their individual OS time (in windows or android) while travelling, to stop other system/app bugs that arise from changing locations so much. When using Signal for communicating with the team around the world, many members complain that their Signal messages are getting ordered incorrectly on their device.

I inspected 3 user's devices after they got back from their last trip. All three users were a member of a signal group chat, but the chat history appeared radically different on each device (specifically, messages were out-of-order, replies were tagged to messages that were written in the future, etc).

Even when the user notices there is a problem, there is no way for them to "refresh/repair" the chat.

This could cause problem for users, such as:
. makes group communication less reliable when travelling
. Cause confusion and bad decisions if messages are misunderstood (ie. a "Yes, leave now" message might show up on the wrong day and cause a totally different result than was intended.
. Some small potential for malicious activity (someone with access to the message group could manipulate the message order and take a screenshot that implicates the correspondents in an exchange that did not actually happen)
. This seems like an unforecasted system state, so some debugging attention should be spent hear to make sure there isn't some way to use this as a springboard to an even bigger bug

Steps to replicate:
. Provision 3 android devices with the signal app and different Signal user accounts (user A, B, C)
. Create a signal group chat with A, B, and C as members. Admin roles don't seem to be significant to the problem
. Make sure that the android system time is the true current time on all three devices
. A, B, and C send messages to the group
. A adds 18 hours to their system clock and restarts the signal app, B subtracts 18 hours from their system clock and restarts the signal app. C keeps their time the same (as a control)
. A, B, and C send messages to the group
. A subtracts 18 hours, B adds 18 hours (to bring them back to their original offset).
. A, B, C send messages to the group

. Gather the devices up and compare the message history's

At this point, the message history on device A, B, and C will show very different sequences and timestamps for the messages.

Observations:

issue_body:
When operating in restricted environment (country that blocks signal), with censorship circumvention ON and relay calls ON (needed for calls to work at all) initiating signal call is often broken in the following manner:

1) user initiates call 
2) signal reaches "ringing" state 
3) the recipient does not in fact get any sort of ring or notification 
4) call times out or call initiator gets bored of waiting and cancels 
5) a few seconds later the recipient gets "missed call notification" 
6) **if the call initiator tries again at this point, the call rings properly for recipient, connects perfectly and has very good quality** 

Do note that turning off call relaying and/or censorship circumvention breaks calls completely in this setting (never connect) 

Workaround: 

Call initiator has to send a signal text message first (any content) and wait for the delivery report to show two hollow ticks (delivered, not read) 
Initiating the call at this point (right after signal text message has been delivered) ensures that the call will both ring properly for recipient and connect well, usually with good quality

**Severity:** High  
**Affected Versions:** All versions of Signal Windows Desktop application up to **[latest version as of the report date]**

## Summary
The Signal Windows desktop application allows the sharing of Python script files (`.py`), which can execute arbitrary code on the recipient's system if Python is installed and the file is run. This poses a significant security risk to users with Python environments, bypassing the application's design intent to block executable files (e.g., `.exe`).

## Description
Signal Windows desktop application explicitly blocks the sharing of `.exe` files to prevent the execution of malicious code. However, it does not restrict the sharing of Python script files (`.py`), which can achieve similar results if the recipient has Python installed on their system.

When a user receives and runs such a file, it can execute arbitrary commands, potentially leading to full system compromise.

## Impact
- **Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE):** An attacker can craft a Python script that, when run, executes malicious commands on the victim's system.  
- **Bypass of Security Controls:** The ability to share `.py` files undermines the security measure of blocking `.exe` files, defeating the purpose of this restriction.  
- **User Trust:** Signal's reputation as a secure messaging application is compromised if users can inadvertently execute malicious code through shared files.

## Proof of Concept (POC)

### Preparation:
Create a Python script (`evil.py`) that performs a benign action for POC purposes:

```python
import os
os.system("calc.exe")  # Opens Calculator
os.system("powershell -Command dir")  # Runs 'dir' command in PowerShell
````

### Exploitation:

1. Send the `evil.py` file to a target user through the Signal Windows desktop application.
2. Ensure the target user has Python installed on their system.
3. Instruct the target user (or socially engineer them) to run the `evil.py` file using a Python interpreter (e.g., by double-clicking or running `python evil.py` in a command prompt).
4. Observe the execution of `calc.exe` and the `dir` command in PowerShell, confirming arbitrary code execution.

### Prerequisite:

Ensure Python is installed on the attacker’s and target’s systems.

### Attacker Actions:

2. Send the `.py` file to a target user via Signal Windows desktop.

### Target Actions:

1. Receive the `.py` file in Signal.

issue_title: Screen Recording Allowed During OTP and Registration Screens
generated_review: I'm really concerned because my phone screen can record when I input my verification code and personal info on Signal. This feels unsafe since important info shouldn't be visible like this.
issue_body:
**Severity:** Medium  
**Bug Type:** Information Disclosure / Privacy Hardening Gap  
**CWE ID:** CWE-359 – Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor  

# Introduction
During account registration and login, Signal Messenger allows the OTP and registration details to be captured through native screen recording on both Android and iOS devices. This behavior exposes sensitive authentication data and contradicts the expected privacy controls in a security-focused messaging application.

# Steps to Reproduce
1. Install the latest Signal Messenger on an Android or iOS device.  
2. Begin registration by entering a valid phone number.  
3. Start the device’s built-in screen recording feature.  
4. When the OTP is received, enter it into the application while recording is active.  
5. Stop the recording and play it back.  
6. Observe that the OTP code, phone number, and registration screen are visible in the recording.

# Actual Result
The OTP and registration details are fully visible in the recorded video.

# Expected Result
The application should block screen recording or obscure sensitive information during OTP entry and registration to prevent data disclosure.

# Impact
1. Disclosure of OTP codes that are intended to remain confidential.  
2. Exposure of personal identifiers such as phone numbers during account setup.  
3. Increased risk of account takeover if a malicious actor gains access to screen recordings.

# CVSS v3.1 Score
**Base Score:** 5.3 (Medium)  
**Vector String:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`

## CVSS Metric Breakdown
- **AV:L (Attack Vector – Local):** Exploitation requires the attacker to have local access or control of screen recording on the victim’s device.  
- **AC:L (Attack Complexity – Low):** No special preconditions are required.  
- **PR:L (Privileges Required – Low):** Attacker must have permission or ability to run a recording application.  
- **UI:N (User Interaction – None):** No further user action beyond normal OTP entry is required.  
- **S:U (Scope – Unchanged):** The issue is confined to the application process.  
- **C:H (Confidentiality Impact – High):** Sensitive authentication data and identifiers are exposed.  
- **I:L (Integrity Impact – Low):** Captured OTP may be used to register or interfere with the account setup process.  
- **A:N (Availability Impact – None):** No impact on service availability.

# Suggested Fix
1. On Android, apply `FLAG_SECURE` to OTP and registration activities to block screenshots and recordings.  
2. On iOS, enable secure text entry for OTP fields and monitor `UIScreen.capturedDidChangeNotification` to obscure content when recording is detected.  
3. Blur or hide sensitive fields in the app switcher view.  
4. Restrict sensitive data display to only essential information during registration.

# Proof of Concept
Reproduce the steps as from above steps to reproduce section

# Business Risk of Bug
Allowing screen recording on OTP and registration screens in Signal Messenger results in the disclosure of sensitive authentication information. Implementing standard OS-level protections will align with Signal’s privacy-first model and prevent unintended information exposure.

issue_title: Media backup/restore becomes completely stuck due to a deadlock in `UploadAttachmentToArchiveJob.kt`
generated_review: Experienced an issue with media backup/restore that became stuck, possibly due to a recurring deadlock in the UploadAttachmentToArchiveJob.kt. Seems like there's an overlap in using the ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking multiple times within this function, causing delays and rendering the process unresponsive.
issue_body:
The deadlock occurs because `ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking` is called while already inside another `runBlocking` call on the same single-thread executor.

In `UploadAttachmentToArchiveJob.kt`, several early-exit conditions wrap `setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification()` inside `ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking { }`:

```kotlin
// Lines 156-161 (original code)
if (SignalDatabase.messages.isStory(attachment.mmsId)) {
    Log.i(TAG, "[$attachmentId] Attachment is a story...")
    ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking {                          // <-- OUTER runBlocking
        setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, ...)
    }
    return Result.success()
}
```

However, `setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification()` (defined at line 354) **already uses `runBlocking` internally**:

```kotlin
private fun setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(...) {
    ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking {                          // <-- INNER runBlocking
        SignalDatabase.attachments.setArchiveTransferState(...)
        ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.throttledNotifyAttachmentObservers()
    }
}
```

Since `ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.executor` is a **single-thread executor** (`Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor`), this creates a classic deadlock:

1. Thread A calls outer `runBlocking` → submits task to executor → waits for result
2. Executor's single thread starts executing the outer task
3. Outer task calls `setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification`
4. Inner `runBlocking` submits another task to the same executor → waits for result
5. **DEADLOCK**: The executor thread is waiting for the inner task, but it can't run because the executor thread is already occupied by the outer task

### Affected code locations

4 instances in `UploadAttachmentToArchiveJob.kt`:

| Line | Condition |
|------|-----------|
| 159-161 | Story attachment check |
| 167-169 | View-once attachment check |
| 175-177 | Expiring message check |
| 183-185 | Long text attachment check |

### Impact

Once the deadlock occurs, **ALL jobs** that need `ArchiveDatabaseExecutor` become permanently blocked, including:
- `RestoreAttachmentJob`
- `CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob`
- `UploadAttachmentToArchiveJob`

The "Restoring media" progress indicator stalls and never completes.

### Fast Fix That Worked Out For Me

Remove the redundant outer `ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking` wrappers since `setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification` already handles the executor internally:

```diff
     if (SignalDatabase.messages.isStory(attachment.mmsId)) {
       Log.i(TAG, "[$attachmentId] Attachment is a story. Resetting transfer state to none and skipping.")
-      ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking {
-        setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
-      }
+      setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
       return Result.success()
     }

     if (SignalDatabase.messages.isViewOnce(attachment.mmsId)) {
       Log.i(TAG, "[$attachmentId] Attachment is a view-once. Resetting transfer state to none and skipping.")
-      ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking {
-        setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
-      }
+      setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
       return Result.success()
     }

     if (SignalDatabase.messages.willMessageExpireBeforeCutoff(attachment.mmsId)) {
       Log.i(TAG, "[$attachmentId] Message will expire within 24 hours. Resetting transfer state to none and skipping.")
-      ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking {
-        setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
-      }
+      setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
       return Result.success()
     }

     if (attachment.contentType == MediaUtil.LONG_TEXT) {
       Log.i(TAG, "[$attachmentId] Attachment is long text. Resetting transfer state to none and skipping.")
-      ArchiveDatabaseExecutor.runBlocking {
-        setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
-      }
+      setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
       return Result.success()
     }
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a Signal account with **Media Backups enabled** (paid backup tier)
2. Have some media in your backup that includes **stories, view-once messages, or expiring messages**
3. Restore the backup on a new device or after reinstalling
4. Observe the "Restoring media" progress - it will start briefly then completely stall

### Conditions that trigger the bug

The `UploadAttachmentToArchiveJob` must encounter an attachment that is:
- A story (`isStory` returns true), OR
- A view-once message (`isViewOnce` returns true), OR
- A message expiring within 24 hours, OR
- A long-text attachment

These are common during backup sync when restoring a device.

Any

issue_title: NullPointerException in `CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob` when attachment has no `remoteLocation`
generated_review: Recent update introduced an issue where media attachments fail to be archived if they lack a remote location, leading to a 'NullPointerException'. This problem seems particularly prevalent for attachments on unsupported CDNs. Hopefully, this can be fixed soon as it makes backup management quite frustrating.
issue_body:
`CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob` crashes with a `NullPointerException` when attempting to copy an attachment that has a `null` `remoteLocation` or is on an unsupported CDN (CDN_0). The crash occurs in `BackupRepository.toArchiveMediaRequest()` due to a force-unwrap of a nullable field.

In `BackupRepository.kt`, the `toArchiveMediaRequest()` extension function force-unwraps `remoteLocation`:

```kotlin
// BackupRepository.kt line 2142
private fun Attachment.toArchiveMediaRequest(mediaName: MediaName, mediaRootBackupKey: MediaRootBackupKey): ArchiveMediaRequest {
    val mediaSecrets = mediaRootBackupKey.deriveMediaSecrets(mediaName)

    return ArchiveMediaRequest(
        sourceAttachment = ArchiveMediaRequest.SourceAttachment(
            cdn = cdn.cdnNumber,
            key = remoteLocation!!    // <-- CRASH: NPE when remoteLocation is null
        ),
        // ...
    )
}
```

The `remoteLocation` field is nullable (`String?`) in the `Attachment` class, but no validation occurs before this force-unwrap.

### Call Stack

```
java.lang.NullPointerException
    at org.thoughtcrime.securesms.backup.v2.BackupRepository.toArchiveMediaRequest-Xn6CfqA(BackupRepository.kt:2142)
    at org.thoughtcrime.securesms.backup.v2.BackupRepository.copyAttachmentToArchive(BackupRepository.kt:1685)
    at org.thoughtcrime.securesms.jobs.CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob.run(CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob.kt:137)
```

### When does `remoteLocation` become null?

Attachments can have `null` `remoteLocation` in several scenarios:

1. **Local-only attachments** - attachments that were created locally but never uploaded to Signal's CDN
2. **Attachments on CDN_0** - older attachments or attachments that haven't been through the normal upload flow
3. **Stickers and other special attachment types** - these are often stored locally
4. **Restored attachments** - during backup restore, attachments may not yet have remote locations

The `CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob` is designed to copy attachments from the transit CDN to the archive CDN, but it doesn't validate that the attachment actually exists on a copyable CDN before attempting the copy.

### Missing Validation

`CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob` defines `ALLOWED_SOURCE_CDNS`:

```kotlin
companion object {
    val ALLOWED_SOURCE_CDNS = setOf(Cdn.CDN_2, Cdn.CDN_3)
}
```

But this is never checked in the `run()` method before calling `BackupRepository.copyAttachmentToArchive()`.

### Fast Fix That Worked Out For Me

Add validation in `CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob.run()` before attempting to copy:

```diff
     if (attachment.archiveTransferState == AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE) {
       Log.i(TAG, "[$attachmentId] Not marked as pending copy. Enqueueing an upload job instead.")
       AppDependencies.jobManager.add(UploadAttachmentToArchiveJob(attachmentId))
       return Result.success()
     }

+    if (attachment.cdn !in ALLOWED_SOURCE_CDNS) {
+      Log.i(TAG, "[$attachmentId] Attachment CDN (${attachment.cdn}) is not in allowed source CDNs. Enqueueing an upload job instead.")
+      setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
+      AppDependencies.jobManager.add(UploadAttachmentToArchiveJob(attachmentId, canReuseUpload = false))
+      return Result.success()
+    }
+
+    if (attachment.remoteLocation == null) {
+      Log.i(TAG, "[$attachmentId] Attachment has no remote location. Enqueueing an upload job instead.")
+      setArchiveTransferStateWithDelayedNotification(attachmentId, AttachmentTable.ArchiveTransferState.NONE)
+      AppDependencies.jobManager.add(UploadAttachmentToArchiveJob(attachmentId, canReuseUpload = false))
+      return Result.success()
+    }

     val result = when (val archiveResult = BackupRepository.copyAttachmentToArchive(attachment)) {
```

This follows the same pattern used in `AttachmentDownloadJob.kt` (line 229) which already checks `attachment.cdn !in CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob.ALLOWED_SOURCE_CDNS` before deciding whether to copy or upload.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a Signal account with **Media Backups enabled** (paid backup tier)
2. Have attachments in your message history that are on **CDN_0** (older attachments or locally-created media)
3. Trigger a backup sync (can happen automatically or during restore)
4. The app will crash when `CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob` attempts to process these attachments

### Conditions that trigger the bug

- Attachment has `cdn = CDN_0` (not in `ALLOWED_SOURCE_CDNS`)
- Attachment has `remoteLocation = null`
- `CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob` is scheduled for this attachment

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Device

Any Android device

### Android version

Any

### Signal version

7.65.4 and 7.66.3 (commit `fee062e727`)

Crash log signature:

```
FATAL EXCEPTION: JobRunner-Temp-X
Process: org.thoughtcrime.securesms, PID: XXXXX
java.lang.NullPointerException
    at org.thoughtcrime.securesms.backup.v2.BackupRepository.toArchiveMediaRequest-Xn6CfqA(BackupRepository.kt:2142)
    at org.thoughtcrime.securesms.backup.v2.BackupRepository.copyAttachmentToArchive(BackupRepository.kt:1685)
    at org.thoughtcrime.securesms.jobs.CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob.run(CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob.kt:137)
    at org.thoughtcrime.securesms.jobmanager.JobRunner.run(JobRunner.java:XXX)
```

## File references

- `app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/jobs/CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/backup/v2/BackupRepository.kt` (line 2142)
- `app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/attachments/Attachment.kt` (defines `remoteLocation: String?`)

This bug have masked by other issue ([such as deadlocks in the job system]([URL] Once those are resolved, this NPE becomes apparent as `CopyAttachmentToArchiveJob` is able to actually execute and encounter attachments with invalid/missing remote locations.

While working on the Molly and UnifiedPush projects, we've identified several inconsistencies in how Android's `ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback` reports Internet availability across API levels and configurations. Especially for users with always-on VPNs and kill switch enabled, but also seen it in other cases.

In practice, this can lead to delayed notifications, missed calls, or battery drain. Signal has found similar issues, with recent commits reintroducing deprecated APIs to mitigate them (#14462). We haven't tested this directly in Signal, but it may be related to issues such as #14415, #7733, #8692, #14116.

We think we have a reliable solution using only the NetworkCallback API, following patterns from AOSP and avoiding deprecated APIs. Normally we'd just submit a PR, but there are some differences between Molly and Signal (e.g. proxy handling and minSdk 23 vs 27), so it would need some adaptation and extra testing.

Before doing that work, we wanted to check whether such a PR would be welcome. If so, we're happy to prepare it. We can also share logs and concrete repro steps if that helps.

issue_body:
Signal Android version 7.70.1 and applicable to Signal across all platforms.

When joining a private group that requires admin authorisation to join, after the point of applying to join and awaiting acceptance , the group description is available to read and access.

### Why is this an issue: 

I am aware of large numbers of organisations who put Group specific and privileged information in the group description for access by all group members. This includes other web resource links.

This information is not available before applying to join the group. 

### How to fix: 

Hide group description from all parties unless they are fully accepted members of the group. 

OR 

Give group admins an ability to set Group-wide information notices that are only available to fully accepted members of the group. Currently this is not possible outside of the Group Description.  Group wide notices are required for giving late joiners to any group the ability to access resources for the group outside of the "chat" context (with all the mess that goes with that such as message timers and having to repeat earlier posts for newer group members).

The media picker takes several minutes to open on devices with large photo libraries (10,000-50,000+ photos/videos). The app appears frozen while the gallery loads.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a device with a large media library (50,000+ photos/videos)
2. Open any conversation in Signal
3. Tap the attachment button and select the gallery
4. Observe load time

## Expected Behavior

Gallery opens within 1–2 seconds, showing the most recent items first, with more loading as you scroll.

## Actual Behavior

Gallery takes **minutes** to open. The UI is unresponsive until all media has loaded.

## Root Cause

The media picker loads the **entire** library into memory before displaying anything.

### What happens internally

MediaStore queries do **not** read actual files—they query Android's internal SQLite database for metadata. However, the current implementation still causes major delays because:

1. **No pagination:** [MediaRepository.getMediaInBucket()]([URL] filters by folder ("bucket") but loads **all items within that folder** without a `LIMIT` clause. When "All Media" is selected, the folder filter is removed and it returns every photo/video on the device.

2. **Massive object allocations:** Each of 100k rows creates `Media`, `Uri`, and `String` objects—hundreds of thousands of allocations causing GC pressure.

3. **Two queries + in-memory merge + sort:** Images and videos are fetched separately, merged, then sorted in memory with `Collections.sort()`.

4. **UI blocked:** The ViewModel waits for the complete list before submitting anything to the RecyclerView, so users see nothing until the entire process finishes.

### Key insight

The bottleneck is **not** file I/O. It's cursor iteration over 100k rows, object allocations, and blocking the UI while waiting for the full dataset.

## Affected Code

- [MediaRepository.getMediaInBucket()]([URL] — unbounded queries, full cursor iteration
- [MediaGalleryViewModel.loadItemsForBucket()]([URL] — maps entire list before UI update

## Suggested Fix

1. Implement pagination (Paging3 or `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` queries)
2. Load only the first 200–500 items for fast initial render
3. Load more items on scroll
4. Consider `MediaStore.Files` with media type filter to avoid two queries

## Impact

Severe UX degradation for users with large photo libraries. The app appears frozen when trying to share media.
It forces the user to share media from third party apps to Signal but Signal itself takes too long to show a media picker.

issue_title: Saved images use download date instead of sent/received date in gallery
generated_review: Frustrated beyond belief! All my pictures from Signal conversations are mixed up and hard to find! Why can't you fix this basic thing? My phone's gallery is a disaster because of your broken app! Fix it NOW!!
issue_body:
When manually saving images from a Signal conversation to the device gallery, the saved images appear with the download/save date instead of the original sent/received date. This causes photos to be incorrectly sorted in the gallery app, making it difficult to find older photos in their proper chronological position.

Interestingly, videos are saved with the correct date, while images are not.

## Related issues

This appears to be related to #10453, which reported photos being saved with incorrect timestamps (appearing as if captured in the "far far future"). That issue described the opposite problem — future dates instead of past dates — but both stem from the same root cause: the inconsistent timestamp handling in `SaveAttachmentUtil.kt`.

The original issue (#10453) requested that photos be saved with the **current timestamp**, but the more appropriate behavior would be to use the **original sent/received timestamp** — this preserves the chronological context of the media and matches how videos are already handled.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Receive an image in a Signal conversation (e.g., sent days or weeks ago)
2. Long-press on the image and select "Save" (or use the save option from the media viewer)
3. Open the device's gallery/photos app
4. Check the date metadata of the saved image

**Actual result:** The image appears with today's date (the date it was saved), not the date it was originally sent/received. In the gallery, it shows up among today's photos instead of its original chronological position.

**Expected result:** The image should retain the original sent/received timestamp, appearing in the gallery at its correct chronological position (like videos already do).

## Root cause analysis

The issue is located in `SaveAttachmentUtil.kt` in the `createMediaUri()` function. When creating the MediaStore entry for saved attachments, the code sets:

```kotlin
MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_ADDED to TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toSeconds(System.currentTimeMillis()),
MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_MODIFIED to TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toSeconds(System.currentTimeMillis())
```

This uses the current system time instead of the original message timestamp (`attachment.date`), which is already available and correctly used for generating the filename.

Additionally, `MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_TAKEN` is not set at all, which is the primary field that gallery apps use for chronological sorting.

## Proposed fix

Pass the original timestamp through to `createMediaUri()` and use it for the MediaStore metadata:

```kotlin
val contentValues = contentValuesOf(
  MediaStore.MediaColumns.DISPLAY_NAME to fileName,
  MediaStore.MediaColumns.MIME_TYPE to mimeType,
  MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_ADDED to TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toSeconds(timestamp),
  MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_MODIFIED to TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toSeconds(timestamp),
  MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_TAKEN to timestamp
)
```

issue_title: Sharing a contact via Android share menu results in 'invalid file' on GrapheneOS
generated_review:
Title: Issue with sharing contacts via Signal on GrapheneOS

Dear developers, I've been using Signal for a while now and it's been great, but I've encountered an issue when trying to share a contact via the Android share menu on my GrapheneOS device. Instead of the contact being shared as a vCard attachment in the Signal conversation, the app reports the file as invalid and fails to attach it. This is strange because sharing the same contact to SMS/MMS apps works perfectly fine. I hope this can be addressed in the next update to ensure seamless functionality across all devices and platforms. Thank you for your time and efforts in maintaining such an essential communication tool
issue_body:
When sharing a single contact from the AOSP/GrapheneOS Contacts app to Signal via Android's share menu (ACTION_SEND with `text/x-vcard` MIME type), Signal reports the file as invalid and does not send the contact.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open Contacts app on GrapheneOS (stock AOSP-based contacts app)
2. Open any contact
3. Tap Share > choose Signal
4. Signal shows "invalid file" or silently fails to attach the contact

**Expected:** The contact is shared as a vCard attachment in the Signal conversation.

**Actual:** Signal rejects the file as invalid.

**Key observation:** Sharing the same contact to SMS/MMS apps works perfectly. The vCard data itself is valid. The issue appears to be in how Signal resolves the shared content URI.

**Likely root cause:** The Contacts app shares a `content://com.android.contacts/contacts/as_vcard/` URI. Signal's `ShareRepository.resolve()` calls `contentResolver.openInputStream()` and `contentResolver.query()` on this URI. If Signal does not have `READ_CONTACTS` permission (common on GrapheneOS, where users often deny this or use Contact Scopes), the URI read fails with a `SecurityException` that Signal catches silently, resulting in `ResolvedShareData.Failure`.

Additionally, the ContactsProvider returns `NULL` for the `SIZE` column on vCard URIs (`OpenableColumns.SIZE` maps to `"NULL"` in `sContactsVCardProjectionMap`). If Signal's size validation treats zero/null size as invalid, this would also cause rejection.

**Note:** A complementary fix has been submitted on the GrapheneOS Contacts side to explicitly add `FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION` to the share intent ([GrapheneOS/platform_packages_apps_Contacts#25]([URL] However, Signal should also handle this case gracefully, as other apps using the same AOSP share pattern will have the same issue.

### Related issues
- #12324 - "Sharing contacts file (vcf) does not work"
- #6520 - "send and receive contacts (vCard) properly"

### Device

15

issue_title: Dynamic Shortcuts are incorrectly sorted
generated_review: It's a fantastic app overall, but the dynamic shortcuts are driving me crazy! My most important chats are constantly in the wrong order when I use them. Please fix this urgently, as I rely heavily on this app and finding conversations quickly is crucial.
issue_body:
The dynamic shortcuts (when long pressing on the app icon on the launcher) are being incorrectly sorted. My first pinned chat is number 4 on the list, my last pinned chat is number 1 on the list.

This is because `createQuery(... preferPinned: true)` creates a query that leads to an incorrectly sorted result, as the pinned order table is ordered descending instead of ascending like everywhere else. This causes the pinned chats to appear in reverse order (4, 3, 2, 1 instead of 1, 2, 3, 4). This was probably done because `NULL` values are ordered above `NOT NULL` values when ordering ascending. The fix for this would be to replace 
`"$TABLE_NAME.$PINNED_ORDER DESC, $TABLE_NAME.$DATE DESC"` with `"$TABLE_NAME.$PINNED_ORDER IS NULL ASC, $TABLE_NAME.$PINNED_ORDER ASC, $TABLE_NAME.$DATE DESC"` in [line 2137 of org.thoughtcrime.securesms.database ThreadTable.kt]([URL]

Users are in a state where contact names were once imported from system contacts, but can no longer be edited or effaced, nor are they able to see the contact's profile name as they are known to others in common groups.

## Repro Steps
Setup:
Local party:
Android 16 on Pixel 6a
Signal 8.2.1 available from the Play Store but not yet installed
Has phone number PN_L

Remote party is on phone number PN_A, already registered with Signal with "allow people to find me by phone number" enabled.

### Phase 1: Get the name from contacts into Signal
1. On the local party, create a local contact card for PN_A, name it "Government Name".
2. Download, install Signal, and do an initial registration with PN_L, allowing access to contacts, and creating a pin. Backup is not setup.
3. In signal, compose a message. See that PN_A is already registered with Signal and can be messaged by "Government Name" obtained from local contacts.
4. Local sends a message to "Government Name". (PN_A), creating a PNI to PNI session. 

### Phase 2, restore the contacts name from Signal Secure Value Recovery
5. Local resets their state: Deletes the signal app. Renames the PN_A contact card to "Dawn"
6.  Local redownloads Signal. On initial setup:
    6a Disallows contacts access. 
    6b Registers PN_L with Signal
    6c Declines to restore from backup (was not setup)
    6d restores with the pin setup in step 2.
7. The remote party replies on the PNI to PNI session created in step 4. Clicks through the safety number changed warning.
8. Local observes a message coming in from "Government Name".

## Expected behavior
Step 8 is possibly the expected behavior. This is the name previously known to the user, it was preserved and restored with the pin restore. However....

1. Users can no longer delete "Government Name" from their signal app, even if they changed it in their contacts. Enabling contacts access from Android settings does not overwrite "Government Name" in Signal with the new "Dawn" from local contacts. (It's not obvious to me that the android app is aware of a contacts permissions change made from android settings, or of a way to tell it to start ingesting contacts data to overwrite this bad state.) Nonetheless the preferable user control is in the Signal app, not in an upstream data source in Contacts.
    1a. Users may hide "Government Name" by setting a nickname, but falls back to "Government Name" if the nickname is deleted, indicating that data is still present
2. Users have no way of indicating their preference of seeing PN_A's profile name, putting them in an inconsistent state with other members of shared groups. This puts the local user at grave risk of outing "Government Name" to other members of the group as they aren't aware of the profile name that PN_A is presenting as to the group.

## Desired behavior
1. Users have a way to efface imported contact names
2. Users can choose to see others' profile name. 
3. Users are prevented from accidentally disclosing private names through ux that establishes the profile name as a the safe shared terminology for a given user in a group.

issue_body: The app currently periodically presents the user with two severely misleading in-app notifications encouraging them to enable Signal Secure Backups. While I strongly believe that these should be one-time notifications, there is an even stronger case that they should be disabled entirely if the user has already enabled On-device Backups. Currently neither is the case. Signal Secure Backups, while a nice feature for the average user, are not compatible with every threat model. Repeated pestering to enable the feature is a user-hostile UX decision. In addition to being severely misleading, these notifications cannot be permanently dismissed or disabled. While I myself care enough to manually tap "Not now" at least once per week, this will obviously lead to most users eventually giving in and enabling this compromising feature. ### Screenshots
